items.title: Suivi-évaluation de la campagne de reboisement : le préfet d’Assoli constate l’évolution des plants dans les communes 1 et 2
items.description: Bafilo, 14 nov. (ATOP) – Le préfet d’Assoli, Lt-Col. Viagbo Mensah, accompagné de son staff technique et du directeur préfectoral de l’environnement, le capitaine Panassa Dihèza, a effectué une tournée de suivi-évaluation des sites de reboisements dans les communes Assoli 1 et 2, le jeudi 12 novembre à Bafilo. Cette descente sur le terrain s’inscrit dans le cadre du suivi de la campagne de reboisement de 2024-2026, visant à contribuer à l’atteinte d’un milliard de plants reboisés d’ici 2030. Elle a permis au préfet et sa suite de se rendre respectivement à Awangala dans la commune Assoli 1, à Dikorodè et Tagbadè dans l’Assoli 2. Le but est d’apprécier l’évolution des plants reboisés d’identifier ceux qui sont morts et d’envisager des approches de solutions pour la prochaine campagne. Il s’est agi également de sensibiliser les communautés riveraines, sur l’importance de la protection, de l’entretien et du suivi constant et régulier des sites reboisés afin d’éviter les feux de brousse, la divagation des animaux sur ces sites. A la première étape de la tournée sur le site d’Awangala reboisé essentiellement des plants de Khaya sénélengalensis depuis 2024, la délégation constate que ces plants se distinguent nettement d’autres qui ont atteint une hauteur raisonnable. Cependant, certains plants sont morts ou endommagés et nécessite un remplacement. A l’occasion, le préfet a exhorté les communautés et leurs responsables à renforcer la surveillance du site à procéder au regarnissage des plants morts par de nouveaux à la prochaine campagne. Il a également donner des orientations pour la résolution de certains conflits liés au foncier, tout en demandant aux chefs traditionnels d’impliquer davantage la communauté fulbé dans l’entretien et la protection des plants afin qu’ils prennent conscience pour ne pas laisser les bœufs passer par le site. Les acteurs mobilisés ont entamé l’entretien du site, en désherbant, taillant les arbustes et traçant des pares-feux pour éviter les feux de brousses. A Dikorodè dans l’Assoli 2 , le préfet et sa suite accompagné du maire, a visité le site reboisé à la campagne de 2025 et 2026. Là, le constat est encourageant, sur ce site est déjà entretenu, les jeunes plants de Gmelina ou teck blanc croissent bien mais restent tout de même fragiles. Le Lt-Col. Viagbo a insisté sur le suivi régulier afin de mieux protéger les jeunes plants contre le passage des animaux et parfois certains insectes rongeurs. A Tagbadè, site reboisé en 2025, les eucalyptus ont atteint une hauteur tandis que les Gmelina qui croissent moins vite ont été visités par les animaux. Au terme de la sortie, le préfet a souligné que le bilan est globalement positif en termes de croissance des plants. Mais, il invite les populations riveraines à un entretien régulier des pares-feux, à la surveillance des animaux en divagation et ceux du pâturage et au regarnissage des plants morts dès la saison pluies prochaines afin de contribuer significativement à l’atteinte des objectifs fixés par le gouvernement en matière de la politique environnementale au Togo. Le directeur préfectoral, en charge de l’environnement a exhorté les communautés à pratiquer la régénération naturelle assistée en entretenant au même moment les petits arbustes qui poussent tout seuls au côté des plants reboisés afin favoriser des forêts denses. ATOP/TAL/BA

Doufelgou / Prévention des maladies à potentiel épidémique : les leaders communautaires mobilisés
items.description: Niamtougou, 14 nov. (ATOP) – Les membres du comité local d’organisation (CLO), les chefs traditionnels et les responsables des formations sanitaires de Doufelgou ont été informés et sensibilisés sur les signes d’alerte et les mesures de prévention des maladies à potentiel épidémique (MPE), le vendredi 13 novembre à Niamtougou. La rencontre est initiée par le ministère en charge de la Santé. Elle vise à renforcer les connaissances de ces différents acteurs sur les moyens de prévention et de lutte contre ces maladies, notamment la méningite, la rougeole, le choléra, la fièvre Lassa et la maladie à virus Ebola, susceptibles de provoquer de graves flambées épidémiques au sein des communautés, particulièrement en saison sèche. Les échanges ont permis aux participants de mieux connaître les principaux signes cliniques de ces maladies, notamment la fièvre brutale, la fatigue intense, les maux de tête, la raideur de la nuque dans le cas de la méningite, ainsi que les troubles digestifs. Les manifestations hémorragiques, telles que les saignements du nez et des oreilles, le sang dans les selles ou les vomissements, ont également été évoquées, de même que les différents modes de transmission. Les participants ont, par ailleurs, été entretenus sur les mesures de prévention individuelles et collectives. Il s’agit notamment du lavage régulier des mains à l’eau et au savon, du port du masque, de l’adoption des gestes barrières, de la vaccination lorsque celle-ci est indiquée, de l’assainissement des lieux publics et de la sensibilisation permanente des populations. La reconnaissance rapide des symptômes et le signalement précoce des cas suspects, ainsi que le renforcement de la surveillance aux frontières à l’approche des fêtes de fin d’année, ont également été soulignés. Le préfet de Doufelgou, Col. Aziaba Ayi Sessi, a indiqué que cette rencontre constitue un cadre approprié pour renforcer la surveillance communautaire, favoriser la détection précoce des cas suspects et préciser le rôle de chaque acteur dans la riposte. Il a insisté sur la nécessité de promouvoir les bonnes pratiques d’hygiène individuelle et collective afin de préserver la santé des populations. Le préfet a invité les chefs traditionnels et religieux à relayer les informations reçues auprès de leurs communautés. Il a également exhorté les enseignants et les parents à inculquer aux enfants les bonnes habitudes d’hygiène, notamment le lavage des mains au savon, l’utilisation des latrines et la consommation d’eau potable. Aux agents de santé communautaire, Col. Aziaba a recommandé une vigilance accrue et le signalement sans délai de tout cas suspect, sans stigmatisation des malades. Il a enfin appelé les populations à faire confiance aux services de santé, à respecter les recommandations vaccinales et à éviter l’automédication ainsi que la propagation de fausses informations sur les réseaux sociaux. Pour sa part, le directeur préfectoral de la Santé de Doufelgou, Dr Alassani Nourou, a rappelé que la prévention demeure la meilleure arme contre les maladies à potentiel épidémique. Il a souligné que la détection précoce et le signalement rapide des cas, conjugués à la lutte contre les rumeurs et la stigmatisation, sont essentiels pour contenir les risques de propagation et éviter la panique au sein des communautés. Dr Alassani a exhorté des agents de santé à redoubler de vigilance, à respecter rigoureusement les mesures de protection et les protocoles de prise en charge, et à renforcer la surveillance dans les formations sanitaires, les établissements scolaires, les marchés et aux frontières. ATOP/SG/TAL/BA

items.title: Machines agricoles : face aux prix élevés du neuf, l’Algérie prospecte l’occasion en Italie
items.description: L’Algérie , qui a souffert cette année de manque de moissonneuses-batteuses pour sa récolte de céréales, veut accélérer la mécanisation de son agriculture qui a besoin désormais de machines et d’équipements à la hauteur de ses ambitions et adaptés aux spécificités des zones dans lesquelles l’activité agricole connaît la plus forte expansion, soit les régions du Sud et des Hauts-plateaux. Des représentants du secteur sont allés prospecter les opportunités de la filière italienne au salon EIMA de Bologne. La 47e édition de l’EIMA (Exposition internationale des machines pour l'agriculture et le jardinage) de Bologne (Italie) s’est tenue cette année du 10 au 14 novembre avec la participation de 1700 exposants. Les dernières innovations en matière d'équipements agricoles imposants et sophistiqués y sont présentées. L’Algérie y a tenu un stand. Acquérir des machines adaptées au Sud et aux Hauts-plateaux “ Dans les halls, les tracteurs à chenilles côtoient les moissonneuses-batteuses dont les plus imposantes peuvent embarquer jusqu'à 20 000 litres de grain ”, a constaté une équipe de la télévision algérienne dépêchée sur place. La délégation y a rencontré trois représentants du monde agricole algérien, venus “ repérer les équipements les plus adaptés aux exploitations algériennes ”. “ Notre agriculture est aujourd'hui développée et nous voulons l'élargir. Il nous faut des équipements de plus grande puissance pour le Sud et les Hauts-plateaux ”, déclare Abdellatif Dilmi, secrétaire général de l’Union national des paysans algériens (UNPA). Outre les céréales, le Sud algérien est aussi un bassin de production de pommes de terre. Cette filière a également besoin de machines adaptées et performantes. “ Il y a des facilitations concernant les terres dans les régions du sud. Nous devons y créer de grands pôles de production de pomme de terre pour élever le rendement et la qualité. L'avenir de cette filière est au sud. Actuellement, la région d’El Oued, à elle seule, représente 40 % de la production nationale. Il y a d'autres wilayas comme El Ménéa, In Salah et Ouargla qui vont suivre. Ce sont des régions difficiles, ça demande de la mécanisation ”, soutient pour sa part Mohamed Touam, secrétaire général du Conseil national interprofessionnel de la pomme de terre (CNIF). Face aux prix élevés, l’achat en coopération d’équipements d’occasion Il est vrai que les prix appliqués sont très élevés pour les moyens dont disposent les agriculteurs algériens. Par exemple, a constaté la Télévision algérienne, “en Europe, une moissonneuse batteuse à chenilles équipée d’une barre de coupe de près de 11 mètres de large, est proposée à 415 000 euros hors taxes”, soit plus de 60 millions de dinars au taux de change officiel. Au taux parallèle, c’est plus de 110 millions de dinars. Ces prix peuvent paraître inaccessibles, mais des solutions existent. Il y a l’achat en coopération, la possibilité d’acquérir du matériel d’occasion mais en bon état et les aides de l’Etat. “Nous verrons quels sont les équipements usagés, de 5 à 7 ans d’âge, les mieux adaptés à nos conditions”, a indiqué Abdellatif Dilmi. L’Algérie autorise en effet depuis quelques années l’importation d'équipements agricoles usagés, de moins de 7 ans d'âge. La disposition a été introduite dans la loi de finances pour 2023. Mettre à profit l’excellence des relations entre l’Algérie et l’Italie “Le taux bancaire est bonifié et la période de remboursement est adaptée. Tout cela est conditionné par la création de coopératives agricoles”, a soutenu pour sa part Ahcene Guedmani, président de la Fédération nationale des producteurs de pomme de terre. La consule d'Algérie à Milan, venue accompagner la délégation algérienne à l’exposition, a souligné un autre avantage pour les agriculteurs algériens : « l’excellence » des relations entre l’Algérie et l'Italie qui, selon elle, peut faciliter les échanges avec les constructeurs d’Italie, un pays connu “pour son industrie moderne et développée, notamment dans les engins et machines agricoles”. L’article Machines agricoles : face aux prix élevés du neuf, l’Algérie prospecte l'occasion en Italie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: NCCIA warns youth against joining illegal call centres for lucrative salaries
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) on Saturday warned that loopholes in the existing system are being exploited by illegal call centres , online betting operators and international fraud networks to launder money and trap victims. Addressing a press conference, NCCIA (Islamabad/Rawalpindi) Additional Director Muhammad Shoaib Khan said fake companies were being registered with weak verification, after which bank accounts opened in their names were integrated with loan apps, betting and gaming portals to receive and transfer illicit funds. Therefore, he called for stricter rules on company registration and bank account verification. The press conference was primarily called to warn educated youths against becoming involved in cybercrime by joining illegal call centres in pursuit of lucrative salaries, urging those seeking jobs with call centres to ask their employers where they are registered and appealing to parents to check whether their children were working at an illegal call centre carrying out scams, fraud or other illicit activities. “Ask them what documents the company has, what registration it operates under, which company they work for, which company is providing the loans, where the money is coming from and who is putting money into these applications,” Khan said. Acknowledging that young people and university students were engaging in such jobs because the salaries were higher than average, he noted that they risked ending up becoming part of the entire trap and operation. “If your son or daughter is arrested in such an operation, the FIR (first information report) becomes part of their record. Tomorrow, when they need a character certificate or apply for a government job, that record can affect them,” the NCCIA officer warned. He said the issue concerns merchant accounts provided by banks and the accounts into which money is deposited. A bank account is linked to a company that may already have been registered despite weaknesses in proper verification, standard operating procedures or the Know Your Customer (KYC) process. “After the company has been registered, the bank opens an account for it. The operators then take that company’s bank account and integrate it with their online betting or gaming portal,” Khan said, adding that the NCCIA team is working on recommendations to these institutions so that they improve their checking systems. The additional director said the agency already raised the issue with senior officials at the policy level, and loopholes identified during investigations and interrogations are brought to light so they can be addressed. He said the NCCIA wants to address cases where one-person companies or similar companies were registered and their bank accounts were subsequently used in this way. Meanwhile, Khan said that the NCCIA identified the role and other details of each individual involved: who used which computer, what their role was, the extent of their involvement, who trapped victims, made the calls and edited the material. “We do not treat everyone as having played the same role. After establishing those roles, we prepare the proper FIR and proceed accordingly,” he explained. The NCCIA additional director noted the agency raided two call centres in the Islamabad-Rawalpindi Zone over the past three days. In the Rawalpindi raid, 11 people, including 10 women, were arrested, while in the Islamabad raid, 143 people were arrested, including 43 women. He said the centres were carrying out transnational scams and fraud, targeting countries in South Asia. Modus operandi Explaining the modus operandi, he said the two centres in the latest raids worked differently. At the Rawalpindi centre, an elaborate setup posing as the police had been created. The operators would offer loans, and when it was time to recover the loans — or when they had trapped someone and wanted to extract money — they would call and scam that victim. The suspects would tell a person that they were either being surveilled or on a hit list. Once someone fell into their trap, they would transfer the person to a setup made to look like the police in Bangladesh, put the victim in contact with someone posing as a police officer and then extort money. At the Islamabad centre, they worked in layers; first, they trapped the victim and convinced them to install an application on their mobile phone. Once it was installed, they obtained access to the person’s photo gallery. After accessing the gallery and obtaining a selfie, they would issue a loan for a minimal amount. But their real target was to collect the person’s credentials: mobile number, personal information and other data. They also obtained information about close family members whom the borrower had identified as guarantors, such as a wife, father, brother, cousin or other family members named as next of kin. Once they had collected all these credentials, the case would be passed to senior members. When they had extracted all of the money they could from someone, they would wipe out that person’s account and close the case. The second method was to take a person’s selfie and other pictures from their phone gallery and edit them into pornographic material, using the person’s face in what appeared to be a professional manner. They would then start threatening, harassing and blackmailing the victim. “Even though the resulting pictures might have been fabricated, the threats were still effective. The victim would be under tremendous pressure, fearing that the images would reach their community or family. Under that pressure, the person would start paying money,” Khan said. He said the scammers extracted personal information in the name of loans, manipulated it and used it against the victims, or created sexual content depicting the victim and extracted money through harassment and blackmail. Responding to a question about masterminds, Khan said they were present at every call centre and also arrested. After that, the agency would investigate local facilitators, including whoever rented out the building, those who made the arrangements and connections and those who set up the operation through a fake company. “We also trace the people who pay the bills and pursue those involved. Then we work at the transnational and international level. We have liaison arrangements with different countries. If a handler or operator belongs to another country, we communicate through embassies and our international contacts,” he noted. A global problem The additional director further stated that international cooperation was being strengthened because such call centres had become a global problem. The NCCIA would handle investigations in Pakistan, while the relevant agencies in the United Kingdom, the United States, China and other countries would handle such matters in their respective jurisdictions. Khan added that in a previous Rawalpindi call-centre case, foreign nationals were arrested and were now in jail, and they will face punishment according to Pakistani law. On the changing methods of call centres, he acknowledged that they were no longer necessarily operating in large plazas. In one house, 10 to 12 people gathered with a computer setup and connected their applications and websites to bank accounts. Someone may be sitting in another country while the people here trap the victim, the NCCIA official pointed out. Once the victim starts depositing money into the account, the person in the other country receives the money. He noted that the Rawalpindi centre had been operating for about a month, while the Islamabad facility had been established only 15 or 20 days earlier. The floor managers and overall HR managers at both centres were locals, he added. “We will investigate and interrogate further to establish who is connected to the back-end operation. We need to find out in which country the application was developed, who developed it and who is handling it,” Khan stated. Staying safe Speaking about how the youth could tell which call centres are legal, Khan said the first thing is common understanding. “If an entire floor is generating sexual content, you know that is illegal. That is a matter of common sense.” Khan added that when applying for a job, young people should ask which organisation the business is registered with, who approved it and what approval it received from the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan. Moreover, he said that many loan applications are operating legally because they have proper permission and follow a lawful procedure. The NCCIA inspects their whole system, including whether the applications are accessing people’s photo galleries, and examines their loan-recovery mechanism. If a borrower does not pay, there are legal channels and procedures for recovery. On foreign nationals involved in cybercrime, Khan said he did not have an exact number, but acknowledged that there have been many deportations. “The number in prison is in the hundreds. When the agency raids one call centre alone, it may find between 150 and 250 people on average,” he added. Khan also rejected attributing call-centre crime to one nationality, saying there are people of multiple nationalities who come to Pakistan and become involved in this work. The agency had also arrested 37 suspects allegedly involved in harassment and blackmail cases over the past two to three years, the official added. The suspects had extracted money from women through harassment and blackmail, and the victims had endured this for the past two or three years. On online betting and gambling, Khan said operators initially give users profits deliberately, enticing people to put more money into these portals. They then assess the victim’s financial capacity and, once convinced that the victim has invested their savings, they wipe out the money and cut off contact. “We are working on this issue and, God willing, will take further action soon. We are making every effort to address fraud involving millions and billions in the name of online betting and gaming,” he stressed. Appealing to young people and businesspeople, including major business owners, Khan urged them against putting business money into buying tokens online and depositing money into gaming applications, gaming websites or betting platforms. “Initially, they may even be allowed to withdraw their money, but essentially the operators are giving them time, playing with their mind and encouraging them to keep depositing more money,” he explained. Khan said the cyber-patrolling teams work around the clock, 24 hours a day, seven days a week.

items.title: Mondial 2030 : l’Espagne maintient la pression pour accueillir la finale
items.description: La bataille autour de la finale de la Coupe du monde 2030 se poursuit. Le président de la Fédération royale espagnole de football (RFEF), Rafael Louzán, a une nouvelle fois affirmé que le match ultime devait se jouer en Espagne, qualifiant cette exigence de « non négociable ». Intervenant vendredi à l’occasion du 20ᵉ Congrès national de droit du sport, organisé au Complexe culturel San Francisco de Cáceres, le dirigeant espagnol a défendu la candidature de son pays pour accueillir la finale du Mondial 2030, coorganisé par l’Espagne, le Maroc et le Portugal. « L’Espagne doit, pour de multiples raisons, organiser ce match », a déclaré Louzán, estimant que cette question « ne devrait même pas avoir fait l’objet d’un débat ». Le président de la RFEF a présenté le Mondial 2030 comme une opportunité majeure pour l’Espagne, mettant en avant sa capacité organisationnelle et sa volonté d’en faire un événement placé sous le signe de la durabilité. Selon lui, les trois pays organisateurs sont appelés à unir leurs efforts afin de garantir la réussite de la compétition, tout en assurant que l’Espagne entend proposer les meilleures conditions possibles pour accueillir le tournoi. Cette nouvelle sortie intervient alors que la question du stade qui accueillera la finale demeure l’un des principaux enjeux du dossier de candidature tripartite. 3,4 milliards d’euros de retombées attendues Pour appuyer la position espagnole, Rafael Louzán a également évoqué une étude d’impact économique et social réalisée par PwC. Celle-ci estime que l’organisation du Mondial 2030 pourrait générer environ 3,4 milliards d’euros d’excédent économique pour l’Espagne, attirer près de 1,5 million de touristes et contribuer à la création de quelque 90.000 emplois. Le dirigeant espagnol a par ailleurs souligné la dynamique actuelle du football espagnol, qu’il considère comme étant dans l’une des meilleures périodes de son histoire, après les nombreux succès enregistrés ces dernières années. Il a notamment cité la prolongation du sélectionneur Luis de la Fuente jusqu’en 2032 et la consolidation de l’organisation du football professionnel espagnol. Alors que les discussions se poursuivent sur la répartition des matchs, Louzán a appelé à patienter avant de connaître la liste définitive des sites retenus en Espagne. Le dirigeant espère que son pays pourra s’appuyer sur un réseau de stades à la hauteur de l’événement et défendre ainsi son ambition d’organiser non seulement une partie importante de la compétition, mais surtout son rendez-vous le plus prestigieux : la finale. Pour l’heure, aucune décision définitive n’a toutefois été annoncée concernant le lieu de la finale du Mondial 2030, qui reste au cœur des discussions entre les différents partenaires de l’organisation. The post Mondial 2030 : l’Espagne maintient la pression pour accueillir la finale appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Mfantsipim @150: Haruna Iddrisu calls for collective effort to tackle indiscipline in schools
items.description: The Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, has called on traditional rulers, religious leaders, parents and students to support efforts to tackle growing indiscipline in schools across the country. He said addressing misconduct in educational institutions required a collective national effort, stressing that the responsibility should not be left to school authorities and the government alone. Speaking at the 150th anniversary celebration of Mfantsipim School on Saturday, November 14, Mr Iddrisu expressed concern about what he described as growing and unacceptable indiscipline in Ghanaian schools. He said traditional authorities, churches, Islamic leaders, parents and students all had important roles to play in restoring discipline and ensuring that schools remained safe environments for teaching and learning. “The growing indiscipline, we need the support of our traditional rulers, we need the support of our church and Muslim leaders, we need the support of parents, and we need the support of students to stem the growing and unacceptable indiscipline in our schools across the country,” he said. The Minister’s appeal comes amid concerns about misconduct and other forms of inappropriate behaviour in some second-cycle institutions, with calls for stronger collaboration between school management, parents and communities to address the situation. Mr Iddrisu maintained that discipline was essential to the development of responsible students and the preservation of standards in the country’s educational institutions. He suggested that traditional and religious institutions, alongside parents, must help reinforce the values of respect, responsibility and accountability among young people.

items.title: The 2027 budget is a “common sense” budget – Senyo Hosi
items.description: Convener of the OneGhana Movement and Finance and Economic Policy Analyst, Senyo Hosi, has described the government’s 2027 budget as a “great common-sense budget”, praising its focus on revenue generation, expenditure discipline and economic stability. He said the government had shown greater efficiency in raising revenue and responsibility in managing public spending, adding that the country needed to build on the progress rather than turn the budget discussion into a political contest over who had performed better. Speaking on JoyNews ‘ Newsfile on Saturday, November 14, during a discussion on the 2027 budget, Mr Hosi said he did not often praise budgets in such terms but believed the 2027 financial plan deserved recognition. “The budget, I must admit, is a great common-sense budget. It’s one of the most common-sense budgets. I don’t say that so often, you know, but this budget is very commonsensical,” he said. He attributed his assessment to what he described as improvements in government revenue generation and expenditure management. “I think the government has been more efficient and effective at revenue generation and more responsible at expenditure. Let’s give credit where credit is due,” he stated. Mr Hosi urged Ghanaians and political actors to move beyond partisan comparisons and focus on how the country could improve its economic management. He said the priority should be to identify what was working and determine how those gains could be sustained to benefit the wider economy. “Let’s rather build, not on who did what more than the other, but how better we can do things. That’s the conversation I want us to start having,” he added. While commending the government’s fiscal management, Mr Hosi said the next major task was to translate economic stability into increased production and opportunities for ordinary Ghanaians. He said that discussions about fiscal consolidation and macroeconomic indicators should not lose sight of the people whose lives were affected by economic decisions. “Because this is about real lives. It’s not about statistics. There are people, human beings behind every number that we are discussing here,” he said. He acknowledged the importance of fiscal consolidation but argued that the country needed to move beyond stabilising the economy and focus on expanding productive activities. “We are here; we understand the fiscal consolidation conversation. It’s great. But we need to see a proper transition from stability to production,” he stated. Mr Hosi also referred to former Vice-President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia’s call for Ghana to move from taxation to production, saying the principle was not wrong, although the previous administration had failed to deliver on it. “Bawumia was not wrong when he said we have to move from taxation to production. He wasn’t wrong. The only problem is that they didn’t deliver it in their time,” he said. He said economies could only achieve sustainable growth when supported by responsible public spending and sound macroeconomic policies. “Every economy can be built on proper fiscal discipline, proper macroeconomic structure, and it promises that,” he stated. Mr Hosi also welcomed the government’s decision to make maintaining economic stability the first pillar of its economic agenda, saying this would provide the foundation for other development priorities. “That’s why, in the new economy, the first thing I wanted, I liked the fact that you made it your pillar one to maintain that stability, because with that you can actually now achieve lower cost of funds,” he said. He added that a stable economic environment could allow Ghana to maintain relatively low interest rates while ensuring positive real interest rates, creating a more predictable environment for businesses and investors. “We can actually still have low interest rates and still have positive real interest rates and build a pathway for investments,” he said.

items.title: Tinubu met Nigeria in ICU – Mutfwang
items.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Plateau State Governor, Caleb Mutfwang, has said President Bola Tinubu met Nigeria in an intensive care unit, ICU, when he assumed office but has gradually moved the country into recovery through his administration’s policies. Mutfwang stated this on Saturday while speaking at the APC North-Central Presidential Campaign Rally at the Zaria Road Stadium, Jos, where he declared Plateau State’s support for Tinubu ahead of the 2027 presidential election. The governor said, “You met Nigeria in the intensive care unit, and through the policies you have administered, like a drug, you have been able to bring Nigeria out of the intensive care unit. We are now in recovery. “We are confident that if you continue, we will not only recover but prosper as well. That is why we are determined that in the 2027 election, there is no alternative for us. We will stick with you and go with you.” He described Tinubu as a friend of Plateau State and the North-Central region, citing the Federal Government’s interventions in road infrastructure, education and healthcare. “We consider you as a friend of Plateau State and North-Central Nigeria in general. You have demonstrated your love for our state and our region through the developmental strides we have seen in road infrastructure, education and healthcare.” “On the Plateau, students in tertiary institutions have received assistance through the NELFUND scheme to the tune of over N11 billion. You have approved the road from Akwanga to Jos. You have also approved the road from Jos to Shendam, right through to Ebonyi. We are truly grateful,” he said. Mutfwang also commended the President’s wife, Senator Oluremi Tinubu, for her support to the people of Plateau State, recalling her visit to the state with gifts. “Your dear wife, our mother, is a darling of the Plateau people. We now know that we have a mother in Aso Rock. When she came visiting us, she did not come empty-handed. Like a good mother, she came with a bag full of gifts for our people, and we will always be grateful,” he said. On presidential election Recalling his promise to reciprocate Tinubu’s kindness during the President’s previous visit, the governor said the time had come for Plateau people to demonstrate their appreciation through their votes. “The time has come and the time is now. By the grace of God, we are going to show our gratitude come January 16, 2027, because we have seen a man who loves us.” “When Plateau takes a direction, many other communities that share affinity with it will also follow suit. We are confident that the votes we will give Mr President in this election will be unprecedented,” he said. On security, Mutfwang commended the Federal Government for its support, saying the state had recorded significant progress in tackling insecurity in the last three months. “In the last three months particularly, we have made tremendous progress in dealing with insurgency. Like you have often said, we will defeat insurgency, and already we can see victory on the way.” “With commitment and sustainability, we will eliminate these enemies of peace and progress, and we are confident that you will lead us in that direction,” he said. The governor, however, appealed to Tinubu to support the state in facilitating the return of internally displaced persons to their ancestral communities. “We will continue to solicit your help, Mr President, to make sure that our people who are internally displaced return to their ancestral homes. “We will be approaching you with a Marshall Plan for the return of our people to their ancestral homes. It is going to require substantial intervention from you, and we are confident that what you have done before, you will do again,” he said. Mutfwang also appealed to the President to assist in completing the Zaria Road Stadium, describing it as a facility whose construction began about 40 years ago. “Mr President, I will be pleading with you on behalf of the Plateau people. Please roll away our reproach. We need your help to make this stadium one of the international stadiums in Nigeria. I am sure it will become a symbol of pride for you when this is done,” he said He further disclosed that his administration had established an employment hub expected to provide jobs for 2,000 young people, alongside a technology hub designed to support security operations. “We have created an employment hub for 2,000 young people who will be working in America and Europe from the comfort of their homes here in Jos. “We have also created another hub for technology so that we can deploy effective technology for the detection of criminals,” he said. The governor added that additional buses had been procured to ease transportation challenges facing residents of the state. items.title: India stun Pakistan by one wicket in last-ball U-19 Asia Cup final thriller
items.description: Mohit Ulva and Venkata produced a decisive unbeaten ninth-wicket stand to snatch a thrilling one-wicket victory for India over Pakistan in the U-19 Asia Cup final, chasing down a daunting 338-run target off the final delivery of the match in Muscat on Saturday. With India struggling at 252 for eight, Ulva and Venkata joined hands to turn the game around, taking the contest into the final over with eight runs required. Ulva, who remained unbeaten on 49 off 26 balls, struck the winning boundary off Ahmed Hussain’s final delivery to take India to 339 for nine. Venkata remained not out on 11. India had appeared to be out of contention after losing eight wickets for 252, despite a solid start to their chase. Manal Chauhan’s aggressive 47 and the subsequent lower-order resistance kept India in the hunt before Ulva and Venkata completed the remarkable recovery. Earlier, Pakistan had posted 337 for nine after being put into bat, with Usman Khan leading the charge with a commanding 107, his fourth century at this level. Abdul Qadir smashed 80 off just 54 balls, while captain Farhan Yousaf added 63 as Pakistan looked set for a total in excess of 350. Pakistan were cruising at 204 for two after 30 overs, but India’s bowlers staged a strong comeback in the closing stages. Kavya Paresh Patel claimed four for 68, while Chigurupati Venkata, who replaced the injured Ishan Sood, took three for 40. Pakistan managed only 63 runs in the final 10 overs while losing six wickets. India’s chase began on a positive note, with Aaryavir Sehwag and Lakshya Raichandani providing a solid opening stand. However, regular wickets in the middle overs put the asking rate under pressure and left India needing a remarkable recovery in the closing stages. The dramatic finish capped a high-scoring final, which featured the highest aggregate in India-Pakistan U-19 ODIs.

items.title: Here’s the latest.
President Zardari, PM Shehbaz discuss country's political, economic and security situation
items.description: President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday discussed the country’s political, economic and security situation in detail, the premier’s office said. PM Shehbaz warmly welcomed the president upon his arrival at the former’s residence in Lahore’s Model Town, the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said. The premier briefed the president on his recent visit to Turkiye, where he participated in the 31st Conference of Parties to highlight Pakistan’s efforts in climate action. Both leaders exchanged views on “cooperation among allied parties, continuation of consultation and progress on public welfare projects”, PMO said. It added that the two leaders also reaffirmed their commitment to working together to accelerate economic stability and development in the country. National Assembly Speaker Ayaz Sadiq Khan, Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar, PM’s Adviser on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah, ex-PM Raja Pervez Ashraf, Senator Saleem Mandviwalla and MNA Hamza Shehbaz were also present during the meeting. President Zardari’s meeting with the premier comes just two days after Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi called on the president. After media reports emerged claiming that Naqvi and the president had discussed the possible formation of new provinces during their meeting in Nawabshah, the President House clarified that “no such discussion” took place. The Presidency explained that “matters concerning national security and the regional situation” were discussed during the meeting. The last publicly reported meeting between President Zardari and PM Shehbaz was on Oct 10 , where the two discussed the country’s security situation just a day before the federal government imposed emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. In August, the prime minister had called on the president and briefed him on the Makkah defence pact signed days earlier between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye.

items.title: Retour des Burkinabè de Guinée : Plus de 52 000 compatriotes dont 11 328 enfants officiellement rentrés au bercail
items.description: Le Conseil national de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CONASUR) a annoncé le rapatriement de 52 325 personnes depuis le début des opérations de retour des Burkinabè affectés par les événements survenus en Guinée. Dans un communiqué publié le 13 novembre 2026, la ministre de la Famille et de la solidarité, le lieutenant-colonel Passowendé Pélagie Kaboré, a indiqué que le 6e convoi arrivé à cette date, a permis d'accueillir et de prendre en charge 6 919 compatriotes. Sur l'ensemble des personnes rapatriées, le bilan fait état de 51 125 hommes et de 1 200 femmes. Les effectifs comprennent également 11 328 enfants ainsi que 1 370 ressortissants d'autres nationalités. Les opérations se poursuivent avec les Conseils régionaux de secours d'urgence et de réhabilitation (CORESUR), et l'appui de la mobilisation citoyenne, qui ont assuré le transport de 10 032 personnes depuis Bobo-Dioulasso vers leurs destinations respectives. À cela s'ajoutent les initiatives individuelles de retour. Le CONASUR réaffirme son engagement à poursuivre les opérations de rapatriement et exprime sa reconnaissance à l'ensemble des acteurs mobilisés. Il appelle également les populations à maintenir leur élan de solidarité et à faire preuve de responsabilité dans le partage des informations, en privilégiant les sources et les canaux officiels. items.title: ECG announces three-day planned power outage in parts of Ashanti Region for upgrade works
items.description: The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has announced a three-day planned power outage in parts of the Ashanti Region to allow the Ghana Grid Company Limited (GRIDCo) to upgrade the transmission line between Anwomaso and the Ridge Bulk Supply Point. The exercise, scheduled from Monday, November 16, to Wednesday, November 18, forms part of ongoing efforts to improve electricity supply in the region. In a public notice issued on Saturday, November 14, ECG said the temporary interruption was necessary to enable GRIDCo to continue work on the transmission line, which involves replacing the existing 364MVA single-circuit line with a modern double-circuit system. The new transmission line will have a capacity of 2 x 488MVA, giving it a combined capacity of 976MVA. According to ECG, the upgrade is intended to strengthen the transmission network and improve power supply to customers in the affected parts of the Ashanti Region. The planned outage will take place from 7:30 am to 5:00 pm each day throughout the three days. ECG has listed several communities and businesses that will experience temporary power interruptions during the exercise. The affected areas include parts of Kaase, Guinness Ghana Limited, Fan Milk, Coca-Cola, Bomplex, Georgia, Abattoir, Boadi, Emina, Appiadu, Kokoben, Donyina, and surrounding areas. The company has appealed to customers in the affected areas to take note of the announced schedule and make the necessary arrangements ahead of the planned interruption. “The inconvenience that will arise as a result of this outage is deeply regretted,” the statement said.

items.title: Mfantsipim @ 150: Top 12 WASSCE-performing SHSs to receive GH¢2m each from GETFund – Haruna Iddrisu
items.description: The Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, has announced that the 12 best-performing senior high schools in the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE) will each benefit from GH¢2 million in GETFund support to expand their infrastructure. He said the funding, announced on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama, forms part of the government’s plans to improve facilities in high-performing schools and expand access to quality secondary education. Speaking at the 150th anniversary celebration of Mfantsipim School, Mr Iddrisu said the intervention would support infrastructure development in the beneficiary institutions, including the construction and expansion of classrooms, dormitories, ICT centres, libraries and other essential facilities. He specifically mentioned Mfantsipim School as one of the institutions expected to benefit from the investment, with plans to expand its assembly hall. “I am also happy to announce on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama that the best 12 performing senior high schools at WASSCE will benefit from GH¢2 million GETFund funding, which will include expanded infrastructure, including the assembly hall of Mfantsipim School,” he said. The Minister explained that the government had made provision for a substantial allocation from the Ghana Education Trust Fund (GETFund) in the 2027 funding formula to support infrastructure development in Category A senior high schools. According to him, GH¢250 million from the GETFund’s 2027 formula will be dedicated to expanding infrastructure in the schools as part of efforts to improve their capacity and accommodate more students. He said the investment would focus on addressing infrastructure needs, particularly the shortage of accommodation and teaching and learning facilities. The announcement also adds to the government’s broader education reform agenda, which includes reviewing the Free Senior High School policy and redirecting investment towards improving foundational learning and expanding educational infrastructure.

items.title: Développement communautaire : le centre Cifop d’Eguilaye, une résilience agroécologique
items.description: Des dindes, des oies, des pintades, des poules se pavanant dans leurs domaines respectifs, offrent un charme inédit au Centre d’incubation et de formation professionnelle (Cifop) d’Eguilaye, un village de la commune de Tenghory. À côté de ce spectacle attrayant de volaille, le maraîchage à l’état de balbutiement avec des pépinières de légumes, d’arbres fruitiers témoigne de l’enthousiasme des responsables de ce centre qui allie à la fois formation et production pour booster le développement local. Créé en 2021 par l'ONG Jed mais fonctionnel à partir de 2024, ce centre encore appelé Lama Docile concentre des domaines maraîcher, avicole, horticole, arboricole… Il abrite aussi un logement, un réfectoire et des salles de formation. L’espace renforce les capacités des jeunes, femmes dans ces différents domaines. A lire aussi : Des acteurs formés sur les bonnes pratiques de fertilisation des terres rizicoles « C’est pour booster le développement local. Nous formons des jeunes qui n’ont pas fait d’études poussées. Nous leur offrons la chance de bénéficier d’une formation professionnelle afin qu'ils se lancent après dans une activité de développement », a expliqué Anifane Manga, directeur du centre Lama Docile à l’issue d’une visite guidée vendredi 13 novembre. Financé par l'ONG Luxembourg, ce centre se particularise surtout par son penchant pour la pratique, plus que la formation. Il avant tout avec les jeunes et les femmes des villages et des localités environnantes. « Nous travaillons avec les jeunes, la population locale, les femmes dans la saponification, le maraîchage, la transformation, l’entreprenariat. Nous faisons aussi de la production de chair, de pondeuses », indique M. Manga. En perspective, le centre va se lancer à partir de janvier dans la production de chèvres et la construction d’une unité de transformation. Installée dans une zone à fortes potentialités agricoles sur une dizaine d’hectares, Lama Docile veut investir sur toute la chaîne de valeur. « Nous voulons faciliter les moyens de conservation et être dans le secteur secondaire », renseigne son directeur. Kadidiatou SONKO (Correspondante)

items.title: Robbery suspect who escaped from Konongo police custody arrested at Kasoa hideout
items.description: Police in Kasoa in the Central Region have recaptured Ibrahim Somaila, one of the suspects who escaped from police custody at Konongo, after a tip-off led officers to his hideout in the town. According to a police report, the Kasoa Central District Command received information around 10:30 pm on November 2, 2026, from a reliable informant. The informant told the police that one of the escapees, who is linked to a recent robbery, was hiding in Kasoa. The night duty officer, ASP Richard Ashiagbor, was informed, and surveillance was set up through the night. At about 1:20 am on November 3, the officers arrested the man at his hideout. D/C/Inspector Francis Afari of the Kasoa District CID, working with G/Sgt Isaac Akomanyi of the Kasoa Central District and the informant, carried out the arrest. The police say Somaila was then taken to the Central East Regional Police Headquarters, and the Konongo Divisional Crime Officer, DSP Richard Debrah, has been informed. Police say the suspect is being held for further action.

items.title: FO says Climate Minister Musadik Malik nominated to represent Pakistan at SCO moot in New Delhi
items.description: The Foreign Office (FO) said on Saturday that Climate Change Minister Musadik Malik had been nominated to represent Pakistan at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue in New Delhi from Nov 20-22. In a statement, the FO said the gathering would bring representatives from SCO member states to discuss issues related to civilisational dialogue and cultural understanding. “The government of Pakistan remains committed to promoting dialogue among civilisations and fostering people-to-people contacts within the SCO framework in a spirit of mutual respect,” the statement said. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on X: “Pakistan who is chairing the SCO Council of Heads of State (CHS) in 2026-27, will participate in SCO Civilisational Dialogue in New Delhi this month.” According to Indian news outlet ANI , 10 SCO members — including Pakistan — have been invited to participate in the inaugural Civilisational Dialogue. It added that the gathering was proposed by New Delhi. In a press briefing on Friday, Indian foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that India has invited several SCO member states to take part in the dialogue, adding that New Delhi looks forward to hosting the gathering. Islamabad has a long history of engagement with the SCO through hosting meetings and chairing bodies within the group. It also holds the permanent chairmanship of an SCO working group on poverty alleviation, which focuses on improving living standards across the region. In October 2024, Islamabad hosted the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting , which India’s Minister for External Affairs Dr S. Jaishan­kar attended on behalf of his prime minister. Jaishankar’s trip, months before the May 2025 military conflict between the neighbours escalated tensions, marked the first such visit by an Indian foreign minister in nearly a decade. Last month, India sent its SCO National Coordinator Alok Dimri to Islamabad for a preparatory meeting for the next SCO CHS meeting in August 2027 , which Pakistan is set to host . “This is my first time on Pakistani soil; these SCO-related programmes will continue throughout the year and culminate in the Islamabad summit,” the Indian official had told PTV News . Pakistan’s chairmanship of SCO CHS marks another step in the country’s growing engagement with the regional organisation, which has expanded its focus from security cooperation to economic development and regional connectivity. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar has noted that Pakistan’s membership has evolved from observer status to proactive full membership since 2017, reflecting its commitment to multilateralism and regional cooperation. Earlier this month, Pakistan also assumed the chairmanship of the SCO Interbank Consortium (SCO-IBC) for 2026-27, the Ministry of Finance said, with HBL Chairman Sultan Ai Allana taking charge for the period. “The development coincides with Pakistan’s chairmanship of the SCO for the same period, reflecting the country’s role in promoting regional trade, investment, financial connectivity and economic cooperation”, the ministry said. Pakistan also chairs SCO’s Reg­ional Anti-Terrorist Structure (SCO-RATS), a role it assumed in September 2025.

items.title: RDC : 30 millions de personnes menacées par une crise alimentaire aiguë alertent quatre organisations onusiennes
items.description: La menace d'une crise d'insecurite alimentaire aigue ou pire (phase 3 ou superieure du CPI) plane sur 30,3 millions de Congolais entre janvier et juin 2027, alors qu'elle ne concernait que 26,5 millions de personnes durant la meme periode de l'annee 2026. C'est ce qui ressort d'un communique conjoint du Programme alimentaire mondial (PAM), de l'Organisation des Nations unies pour l'alimentation et l'agriculture (FAO), de l'UNICEF et de l'OMS, publie le 13 novembre. L'aggravation de la situation est imputee essentiellement aux conflits, aux deplacements de population, a la hausse des prix alimentaires, a l'epidemie d'Ebola (entre autres epidemies) et au niveau dangereusement insuffisant de l'aide humanitaire face aux besoins croissants, expliquent les organisations de l'ONU. La meme source avance des chiffres detailles indiquant que pres de 29 millions de personnes sont confrontees a une insecurite alimentaire aigue de niveau critique ou pire entre septembre et decembre 2026, parmi lesquelles 3,6 millions sont dans une situation d'urgence. Ce dernier chiffre devrait augmenter de pres de 600 000 personnes des le debut 2027, a 4,2 millions de Congolais. Situation urgente dans l'est de la RDC C'est dans l'est de la Republique democratique du Congo (RDC) que les besoins en aides sont les plus urgents, plus de 11 millions de personnes pouvant etre confrontees a une crise, voire pire, entre janvier et juin 2027, notamment au Nord-Kivu, au Sud-Kivu et en Ituri. Neuf autres territoires de cette partie du pays pourraient etre confrontes, quant a eux, a une situation d'urgence. Toutes ces zones ont donc en commun un besoin urgent d'aide humanitaire, alerte le communique. Les familles et les enfants particulierement exposes Le communique cite une analyse du Centre international de prevision alimentaire (CPI) qui identifie les crises au Moyen-Orient, en mer Rouge et en Ukraine comme des facteurs aggravants de la crise alimentaire en RDC. Il pointe egalement d'autres facteurs tels que l'insecurite, les aleas climatiques et l'acces limite a la terre et aux intrants agricoles qui sont a l'origine de la baisse des recoltes et des revenus agricoles qui privent les familles de nourriture et des moyens pour se nourrir. Les enfants congolais de moins de cinq ans sont les plus vulnerables aux effets de la crise alimentaire qui engendre une malnutrition aigue, aggravee par le manque d'acces aux soins de sante, a l'eau potable et a l'assainissement. Cette combinaison de plusieurs facteurs, aussi graves les uns que les autres, « accentue les consequences de la faim et rendent le redressement plus difficile, surtout la ou les services de base sont deja satures », previent le communique onusien. La FAO, le PAM, l'UNICEF et l'OMS ont appele a une riposte sans delai, combinant un financement et une action diplomatique urgents et coordonnes afin d'accroître l'aide alimentaire, de proteger et de retablir les moyens de subsistance agricoles, de prevenir et de traiter la malnutrition aigue, de maintenir les services essentiels de sante, de nutrition, d'eau potable et d'assainissement, et de garantir un acces humanitaire sûr et sans entrave.

Otti, Ajaero, others pay tributes to late NLC scribe, Ugboaja
items.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — It was a night of tears, fond memories and glowing tributes on Friday as labour leaders, government officials, family members and associates gathered in Umuahia to celebrate the life and legacy of the late Secretary-General of the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC), Comrade Emmanuel Okechukwu Ugboaja. Ugboaja, who hailed from Nkpa in Bende Local Government Area of Abia State, died at the age of 60. At the Night of Tributes organised by the Abia State Government at the International Conference Centre, Umuahia, speakers took turns to recount the late labour leader’s contributions to workers’ welfare, organised labour and humanity, describing his death as an irreparable loss. Abia State Governor, Dr Alex Otti, who led the tributes, described Ugboaja’s death as painful, but said his contributions to the labour movement and society would remain an enduring legacy. Otti particularly celebrated his emergence as the first and only indigene of Abia State to occupy the position of NLC Secretary-General among the five individuals who had held the office. “Out of the five Secretaries-General of the Nigeria Labour Congress, Comrade Emmanuel Ugboaja was the only one from Abia State. “He was the first NLC Secretary-General from our State, and that is a significant achievement,” the governor said. Reflecting on the meaning of life, Otti said a person’s worth was not measured by the number of years spent on earth but by the positive impact made and the legacies left behind. He expressed confidence that the late Ugboaja had successfully fulfilled his earthly assignment, urging his family not to surrender to despair but to draw strength from the Christian hope of resurrection. “From everything we have heard about him today, we have no doubt that Comrade Emmanuel Ugboaja finished his race here on earth. There are no mistakes with God. “We urge the family not to mourn like those without hope. Our prayer is that on the resurrection morning, when the trumpet shall sound, Comrade Emmanuel Ugboaja will be among those who will rise to eternal life,” Otti said. The governor prayed for the peaceful repose of the deceased’s soul and journey mercies for those who attended the event. In his tribute, NLC President, Comrade Joe Ajaero, described Ugboaja as a committed labour activist and a worthy son of the workers’ movement. Ajaero recalled that their relationship dated back to 1993, when both were actively involved in their respective professional and union activities. He described the deceased as a man of strong convictions who remained steadfast in the struggle for workers’ rights and made significant contributions to the growth of organised labour. The NLC president urged members of the labour movement and others who encountered Ugboaja to preserve his memory and sustain his legacy, noting that his death was another reminder of the fleeting nature of human existence. In their respective tributes, TUC Secretary, Engr. Festus Osifu; Abia State NLC Chairman, Comrade Okoro Ogbonaya; and other labour stakeholders joined workers across the country in mourning the late unionist. They described him as humble, remarkable, eloquent and a blessing to humanity, the Nkpa community and Abia State, lamenting that his death had created a huge vacuum in the labour movement. They prayed God to comfort his family and grant them the fortitude to bear the loss. Speaking on behalf of the family, the deceased’s brother, Mr Patrick Ugboaja, described him as a national and international figure who, despite his towering profile, never lost touch with his roots. He recalled that beyond his demanding responsibilities in the labour movement, the late Ugboaja was also a farmer, devoted family man and friendly personality who related freely with people, irrespective of their backgrounds. Patrick expressed deep appreciation to Governor Otti, the Abia State Government and everyone who had stood by the family during their difficult period. Speaking on behalf of the younger generation of the family, the deceased’s son, Emmanuel Ugboaja Jnr., remembered his father as a disciplined man who understood the need to strike a balance between professional responsibilities and recreation. He said the values of discipline, focus, hard work and determination consistently instilled by his father had become enduring lessons for him and his younger siblings. He also recalled his father’s generosity and selfless disposition, particularly his commitment to helping others. Earlier, in a sermon titled, “Before the Translation: What Will Be Your Testimony?”, drawn from Hebrews 11:5, Very Rev. Dr Emmanuel Chukwuma challenged the congregation to live purposeful lives and leave behind positive testimonies before their departure from the world. The cleric also commended Governor Otti for his developmental efforts in Abia State, expressing optimism about the governor’s second-term ambition. The Night of Tributes attracted labour leaders from within and outside Nigeria, government functionaries, family members, friends and associates, who gathered to honour the memory of a man whose influence extended beyond the workplace into the wider society. Ugboaja is scheduled to be buried on Saturday after a funeral service at Amohoro Nkpa, his country home. items.title: Clashes between gangs, vigilantes kill over 50 in Zamfara – Report
items.description: Clashes between criminal gangs and local vigilantes have left more than 50 people dead in northwestern Nigeria’s Zamfara state, residents told AFP Saturday. Zamfara is one of several states in northwest and central Nigeria terrorised by kidnapping-for-ransom and cattle-rustling gangs who raid villages, kill and abduct residents as well as looting homes before burning them. Locals call the gangs bandits. Vigilantes from Zoma village in Bukkuyum district ambushed the bandits who were passing through the village on Thursday after kidnapping several people from nearby Gummi district, the sources said. “We were alerted that the bandits were heading our way, so our vigilantes laid in wait for the bandits and engaged them in a fierce gunfight,” said a traditional village chief who asked not to be identified for personal safety. “Our vigilantes killed 44 of the bandits … we also lost nine vigilantes in the fight,” said the chief, adding that a notorious bandit commander called Jijji, who had led the kidnapping, was also killed in the fight. – Call for weapons – News of bandit attacks in remote areas is usually slow to emerge due to poor telecommunications and distance. A Zamfara state police spokesman contacted by AFP said the force had yet to receive details about the clashes. Zoma residents Kabiru Tafida and Basiru Buhari reached by AFP gave the same account of the clashes and toll. “We call on the authorities to provide our vigilantes with guns and ammunition to fight these bandits who use sophisticated weapons,” Buhari said. Banditry in Africa’s most populous country traces its roots to conflicts between herders and farmers over access to limited land and water, made worse by climate change and population growth. Out of the violence emerged powerful gangs, largely composed of Fulani herders — and a kidnapping economy, while at times forging alliances with jihadists. In Zamfara’s neighbouring state Katsina, a bandit leader recently told AFP that “years of injustices” drove him and other cattle herders into banditry. He spoke during a rare interview which came during the reporting of an article for The New York Review of Books, co-authored by an American academic and writer Helen Epstein and an AFP northern Nigeria reporter. The Nigerian military routinely refers to bandits as “terrorists”, and runs a dedicated military campaign in the northwest to combat them. Worsening insecurity and the high cost of living have become major issues in the ongoing presidential campaign, as Bola Tinubu runs for a second term in January polls. Les demandes brutales de la Russie sur l’Ukraine
items.description: Selon le quotidien allemand Bild , la Russie a présenté lors des discussions d'Abou Dhabi, une série d'exigences dépassant très largement le cas ukrainien. Moscou les décrit comme la base d'un « nouvel ordre de sécurité européen » Russlands brutale Forderungen an Europa », Bild , 13 octobre 2026.'> 1 . Le New York Times a également eu accès au document contenant ces exigences, daté du 10 novembre Russia Revives Demand That NATO Retrench to Secure Ukraine Deal », The New York Times , 13 novembre 2026.'> 2 . Concernant l’Ukraine, les demandes russes reprennent la plupart des objectifs de guerre formulés par Moscou depuis le début de l’invasion à grande échelle. L’Ukraine devrait accepter de perdre près d’un cinquième de son territoire. Aux 110 000 km 2 déjà occupés, soit 18 % du pays, s’ajouteraient les parties du Donbass encore tenues par Kiev, principalement dans l’oblast de Donetsk. L’Ukraine verrait sa souveraineté sur la politique internationale, largement restreinte. Son adhésion à l’OTAN serait exclue, tandis que celle à l’Union européenne resterait possiblement ouverte. Selon le New York Times , Moscou envisagerait l'adhésion de l'Ukraine à l'Union européenne uniquement si le pays ne participait pas à la politique de défense commune. Zelenky a affirmé que les États-Unis ont demandé si l'Ukraine serait disposée à céder la région du Donbass, située à l'est du pays, à la Russie, en échange d'une adhésion à l'OTAN Zelenskyy Says US Floats NATO Membership in Deal for Donbas », Bloomberg , 14 novembre 2026.'> 3 . L’Ukraine perdrait enfin une partie de ses capacités militaires. Odessa et Mykolaïv seraient démilitarisés et ne pourraient plus accueillir de bases navales. Au-delà de l'Ukraine, les exigences russes vont dans le sens de ce qui a été annoncé par la Maison-Blanche , et demandent une « négociation de l'architecture de sécurité européenne ». La Russie souhaite que l’OTAN retire ses troupes et ses bases aux frontières de l’alliance telles qu’elles existaient en 1997, excluant ainsi de l’alliance la Tchéquie, la Hongrie et la Pologne (qui ont rejoint en 1999), la Bulgarie, les trois pays baltes, la Roumanie, la Slovaquie, la Slovénie (en 2004), l’Albanie, la Croatie (en 2009), le Monténégro (en 2017), la Macédoine du Nord (en 2020), la Finlande (en 2023) et la Suède (en 2024). Selon le New York Times, les responsables russes présents à Abou Dhabi ont clairement indiqué qu’ils considéraient la guerre froide et le pacte de Varsovie comme un modèle potentiel pour l’Europe d'après-guerre en Ukraine. Yuri Ouchakov a également déclaré que Poutine avait insisté lors de ses discussions avec Kusner et Witkoff sur le fait que la proposition russe de 2021 visant un retrait de l’OTAN reflétait toujours « notre vision des piliers d’une architecture de sécurité indivisible ». De plus, si en 2021 la Russie avait demandé à l’OTAN d'abandonner ses accords de « partage nucléaire », Moscou demande désormais que la France et la Grande-Bretagne excluent la possibilité d’utiliser leurs armes nucléaires pour protéger d’autres pays européens. Selon le journal biélorusse Nasha Niva , la proposition russe vise aussi à transformer la Moldavie en république fédérale réunissant la Moldavie, la Gagaouzie et la Transnistrie. En cas d'adhésion à l'Union européenne, ces deux dernières pourraient organiser des référendums d'indépendance Россия предлагает превратить Молдову в федеративную республику, в состав которой войдут Гагаузия и непризнанное Приднестровье , Nasha Niva , 13 novembre 2026.'> 4 . Moscou aborde ces discussions comme si elle faisait face à une capitulation ukrainienne, et n’offre en échange que de renoncer aux leviers de pression qu’elle a elle-même installés. Ses armes nucléaires quitteraient la Biélorussie et Moscou s’engagerait également à ne pas y déployer de missiles de portée intermédiaire, tels que les missiles Iskander et Orechnik. Ses troupes évacueraient également la Transnistrie. Les déclarations de Vladimir Poutine confirment par ailleurs qu’il n’y a aucune marge de négociation pour la Russie, en s’inscrivant dans ce que l’on a appelé la doctrine Gromyko . « Demandez le maximum, y compris ce que vous n’avez jamais eu ; présentez des ultimatums, car vous trouverez toujours un Occidental prêt à négocier ; enfin, ne cédez rien, car vous trouverez toujours une offre correspondant à ce que vous recherchez, exigez plus afin d’obtenir le tiers ou la moitié de ce que vous n’aviez pas au départ. » Le 12 novembre, au Kremlin, alors qu'il recevait les émissaires américains Steve Witkoff et Jared Kushner, le président russe a rejeté toute présence militaire étrangère en Ukraine après un accord de paix. Il a averti que des forces européennes déployées dans ce cadre deviendraient des « cibles militaires légitimes » et que les combats reprendraient immédiatement. Il a également écarté l’idée de zones démilitarisées, estimant que seule la frontière d’État pouvait servir de ligne de démarcation. L’ Institute for the Study of War y voit la réaffirmation d'une revendication portant sur l’intégralité des régions de Donetsk, Louhansk, Kherson et Zaporijjia, y compris des territoires que l’armée russe n’a jamais conquis Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment , 13 novembre 2026.'> 5 . De son côté, Vladimir Medinski, conseiller du président et chef de la délégation russe à Abou Dhabi, a exclu tout échange territorial dès le 11 novembre et annoncé l’extension continue de la « zone de sécurité » russe du côté de Soumy et de Kharkiv. La Russie, a-t-il ajouté, reprendra « chaque pouce de sa terre, d’une manière ou d’une autre », laissant entendre que l'agression russe pourrait se poursuivre au-delà des territoires conquis en Ukraine Мединский пообещал вернуть « каждую пядь русской земли » и обвинил Европу в гибели украинцев , Moscow Time, 11 novembre 2026.'> 6 . L’article Les demandes brutales de la Russie sur l’Ukraine est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Mfantsipim @ 150: Gov’t to build 10 model SHSs, upgrade 30 Category B schools – Haruna Iddrisu
items.description: The Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, has announced plans by the government to construct 10 new model senior high schools across the country and upgrade 30 Category B schools to the standard of Category A institutions. He said the initiative forms part of the government’s broader investment in secondary education following the completion of a review of the Free Senior High School (Free SHS) policy introduced in 2017. Speaking at the 150th anniversary celebration of Mfantsipim School in Cape Coast on Saturday, November 14, Mr Iddrisu said the government, under President John Dramani Mahama’s administration, had completed its assessment of the Free SHS programme as part of efforts to reset the country’s education priorities. According to him, the review has informed a decision to redirect some investments towards strengthening foundational learning, particularly literacy, numeracy, agricultural science and mathematics. “President John Dramani Mahama and the NDC government, under the reset, have completed the review of the Free Senior High School project implemented in 2017, and the decision of government is to realign investment into basic foundational learning in order that we will get a rise in literacy and numeracy, agricultural science and mathematics literacy,” he said. The Education Minister explained that strengthening basic education was necessary to improve learning outcomes and equip pupils with the essential competencies required to progress successfully through the educational system. He stressed that improving foundational learning would remain a key consideration in the government’s education reforms. $300m investment in secondary education Mr Iddrisu also announced a further investment of $300 million in the country’s secondary education infrastructure, aimed at expanding facilities and improving learning conditions across senior high schools. He said the funding would support infrastructure expansion in schools nationwide, although the specific allocation of the funds to the various projects was not detailed in his remarks. As part of the investment, the government plans to establish 10 new model senior high schools, with one to be constructed in each of 10 regions. The initiative is expected to expand access to quality secondary education while providing additional facilities to accommodate students and improve the delivery of teaching and learning. 30 Category B schools to be upgraded In another major component of the government’s plan, 30 Category B senior high schools are to be upgraded to match the standards of Category A institutions such as Mfantsipim School. The initiative is intended to narrow the infrastructure and facilities gap between the different categories of senior high schools and ensure that more students have access to quality educational facilities, irrespective of the category of school they attend. Mr Iddrisu cited Mfantsipim as an example of the standard the government wants the selected schools to attain. The proposed upgrades are expected to improve infrastructure and the general learning environment in the beneficiary institutions. Education reset The announcements form part of the government’s broader education reform agenda, which seeks to review existing policies, strengthen foundational learning and improve infrastructure at the secondary level. The completion of the Free SHS review signals the government’s intention to reassess investment priorities within the education sector while maintaining attention on access and quality. The planned construction of 10 model senior high schools and upgrading of 30 Category B institutions also represent an effort to improve the distribution of educational infrastructure across the country. Founded in 1876, Mfantsipim is one of Ghana’s oldest secondary schools and has produced generations of prominent professionals and national leaders.

items.title: Burundi: onze partis d’opposition rallient la candidature de Ndayishimiye pour 2027
items.description: À quelques mois de la présidentielle prévue le 3 mai 2027, onze formations politiques burundaises se réclamant de l’opposition ont annoncé leur ralliement au président sortant Évariste Ndayishimiye, selon des sources médiatiques. Déjà désigné candidat du parti au pouvoir, le CNDD-FDD, le chef de l’État bénéficie ainsi d’un soutien politique supplémentaire dans la perspective de ce scrutin. La scène politique burundaise connaît un rapprochement inattendu à l’approche de la prochaine présidentielle. Réunis à Bujumbura, le mardi 10 novembre 2026, onze partis d’opposition, parmi lesquels le FROLINA, le KAZE-FDD et le RADEBU, ont décidé de faire front commun derrière Évariste Ndayishimiye, candidat à sa propre succession. Pour motiver leur position, ces formations politiques mettent en avant les actions du président sortant, notamment dans les domaines de la lutte contre la corruption, de la sécurité et de la défense de la souveraineté nationale. Dans une déclaration conjointe, elles se sont également engagées à sensibiliser et mobiliser leurs militants en faveur du chef de l’État, tout en affirmant leur volonté de participer à la consolidation de l’État de droit. Cette prise de position intervient alors que le calendrier électoral entre dans une phase importante. Les candidats à la magistrature suprême sont en effet appelés à soumettre leurs dossiers de candidature à la Commission électorale nationale indépendante (CENI) du 13 au 22 novembre. Arrivé à la tête du Burundi en 2020, à la suite du décès de Pierre Nkurunziza, Évariste Ndayishimiye ambitionne de rempiler pour un second mandat de sept ans. La Constitution burundaise autorisant deux mandats présidentiels consécutifs, le scrutin du 3 mai 2027 constitue une nouvelle échéance décisive pour le chef de l’État et ses soutiens politiques. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Burundi: onze partis d’opposition rallient la candidature de Ndayishimiye pour 2027 est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Fire guts storey building in Lagos
items.description: By Olasunkanmi Akoni Fire on Saturday gutted a storey building at No. 9, Ola Market, Adedeji, Itire, Surulere, Lagos State. However, no life was lost in the incident. An eyewitness said the fire broke out in the early hours of Saturday. The Director-General of the Lagos State Fire and Rescue Service, Margaret Adeseye, confirmed the incident, saying firefighters were deployed to the scene following a distress call. “Following a distress call received at 10:12 hours, firefighters from the Sari Iganmu and Isolo Fire Stations were mobilised and arrived at the scene promptly to combat the fire,” Adeseye stated. The fire affected the top floor of the residential building but had been contained as of 11 a.m., according to the service.
