items.title: Pakistan, 16 other countries, condemn Israeli strike on southern Gaza hospital
items.description: Pakistan and 16 other countries,on Saturday condemned the Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, calling on Tel Aviv to protect civilians and medical facilities and ensure the sustained and unimpeded delivery of humanitarian aid to the Palestinian enclave. The deadliest single strike since Israel’s elections last month hit the surgery ward of Nasser Hospital in Khan Yunis early on Thursday, killing at least six Palestinians, including a 13-year-old boy, and wounding nearly 30 others. The Israeli military claimed it carried out an “aerial strike to eliminate the threat they posed, after the Hamas had established a presence within the hospital complex and used it as a command centre”. According to a joint statement issued by the Foreign Office (FO) on Saturday, the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Algeria, Djibouti, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Mauritania, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Sudan, Turkiye and the United Arab Emirates condemned in the Israeli strike in the “strongest terms” The statement said that strike “caused casualties among patients and medical personnel, in violation of international humanitarian law, which affords special protection to medical facilities and healthcare workers”. It also condemned continued Israeli attacks on Palestinian civilians, including strikes on tents and other sites sheltering displaced persons. “These attacks undermine the ceasefire and efforts to restore security and stability in Gaza and are inconsistent with US President Donald Trump’s Comprehensive Plan ,” the joint statement said. It expressed grave concern that “continued Israeli restrictions on humanitarian aid, shelter materials including tents, caravans and mobile homes, as well as medical supplies” were “deepening Gaza’s humanitarian catastrophe as winter approaches”. “Inadequate shelter and deteriorating water, sanitation and healthcare services put civilian lives at grave risk, particularly those of children and infants, who could once again die from exposure to freezing temperatures,” it said. The statement called on Israel to heed appeals from the international community and the Board of Peace for increased aid and to fulfil immediately and in full its obligations under the Sharm El-Sheikh Agreement . “Israel must uphold the ceasefire, protect civilians and medical facilities, and ensure the safe, sustained and unimpeded delivery of humanitarian aid in sufficient quantities, including shelter and early recovery supplies and equipment to restore essential infrastructure. “It must also allow United Nations agencies and humanitarian organisations to carry out their mandates without obstruction,” the joint statement said. These first-phase commitments were due to take effect upon signature, it added. “Israel must implement them without further delay or additional conditions, including political and security conditions, that impede humanitarian access,” the statement said. “Urgent humanitarian assistance must proceed independently of progress on subsequent phases,” it said. Per the statement, the foreign ministers called on the US and the Board of Peace to “intensify their efforts to ensure Israel’s full implementation of these commitments and the lifting of all restrictions on the entry of humanitarian aid, thereby preserving the credibility of the agreements and consolidating the ceasefire”. The foreign ministers reaffirmed their determination to work with regional and international partners to consolidate the ceasefire, implement all phases of the plan and scale up humanitarian assistance to alleviate the suffering of the brotherly Palestinian people, the statement concluded. Earlier this month, the Trump’s “Board of Peace” said that Israel needed to act immediately to help war-battered Gaza cope with impending winter, saying measures ahead of deadly floods had been insufficient. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Nov 9 said he had directed the foreign ministry to pursue all possible means to urgently “escalate humanitarian assistance” to Gaza amid heavy rainfall.

items.title: Kédougou : ActionAid renforce la résilience climatique à Tomboronkoto
items.description: ActionAid Sénégal, en partenariat avec KHEO (Kédougou Encadrement Orientation et un Développement Humain), a lancé vendredi un projet de renforcement de la résilience climatique et de la participation citoyenne des communautés affectées par l’exploitation minière dans la région de Kédougou. Financé par Covid Relief à hauteur de 120 200 euros (plus de 78 millions de FCFA), le programme sera déployé sur deux ans dans la commune de Tomboronkoto. L’initiative intervient dans un contexte marqué par les effets du changement climatique, notamment les inondations, l’irrégularité des pluies et la dégradation des écosystèmes liée à certaines pratiques d’orpaillage. Présidant la cérémonie, le préfet de Kédougou, El Hadj Malick Sémou Diouf, a souligné la nécessité de promouvoir des pratiques minières responsables et de préparer les populations à l’après-exploitation. Il a également insisté sur l’importance du dialogue et du partage de bonnes pratiques. A lire aussi : Salémata : une infirmerie scolaire inaugurée au lycée Selon Mohamed Diakhaté, responsable du suivi-évaluation à ActionAid Sénégal, le projet cible particulièrement les femmes et les jeunes, à travers des formations et des espaces d’échanges communautaires. L’objectif est de renforcer leurs capacités à défendre leurs droits et à réclamer davantage de justice climatique. Les communautés, les autorités administratives, les services techniques et les médias seront associés à la mise en œuvre de cette initiative axée sur la protection de l’environnement et la justice sociale. Amadou DIOP (Correspondant)

items.title: Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026: Day Two kicks off with exciting bargains, irresistible deals at Ghud Park
items.description: The shopping excitement is back, the bargains are calling, and the opportunities to discover Ghanaian-made products are getting even bigger as Day Two of the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 gets underway at Ghud Park, Accra Mall. With more than 80 brands showcasing an impressive variety of products and services, Saturday, November 14, promises to be an exciting day for shoppers, families, entrepreneurs and anyone looking to enjoy quality products at attractive prices. Patrons who have not made it to the exhibition have another opportunity to experience the buzz, explore the stalls, interact with business owners and take advantage of special offers and discounts being rolled out by participating vendors. And there is plenty to look forward to. From delicious Ghanaian delicacies and refreshing beverages to fashionable clothing, beauty products, footwear, electronics, household essentials and innovative business solutions, the fair has transformed Ghud Park into a vibrant marketplace where there is something for practically everyone. Whether you are looking to restock your kitchen, upgrade your wardrobe, surprise a loved one, purchase a new gadget or simply enjoy a refreshing day out, the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair is the place to be. The deals are waiting, the vendors are ready, and the shopping experience promises to be worth every minute. From delicious delicacies to refreshing drinks – food lovers, this is for you! If you love good food, prepare to have your appetite stimulated. The fair brings together an exciting collection of food processors, agro-based businesses and beverage manufacturers offering patrons the opportunity to discover, sample and purchase a variety of locally produced products. Didi Shito, Sankofa Spices, Manellah Foods, Adjoor Ventures, Yaapee Royal Foods, Nutrismart Ventures and Koa Impact Commerce are among the businesses showcasing their products. For those who love refreshing drinks, Delsoy has its soy milk offerings, while Orave Juices, Jussvina Drinks, Pinnacle Coco and Green Cup are bringing exciting beverage options to the exhibition. Koa Impact Commerce is also showcasing natural cocoa juice, while Green Cup offers beetroot, guava and pawpaw tea. Farm Mate, Orrab Farms, T&C Farms and Atohfield are showcasing agricultural products and fresh produce, while Flourish Foods Africa is bringing grilled chicken and poultry products to the fair. When hunger strikes, patrons can also explore the offerings from MamsiJoy Ventures, Ellie Catering Services, Martha’s Yam Trading, Selis Satisfactory, Bliss Pop, Evive Delight, 97 Bakes and Aladdin Bakery. From savoury meals to sweet treats, there is enough to keep food enthusiasts occupied. Fashion, beauty and style – refresh your look without breaking the bank Ladies and gentlemen looking to give their wardrobes a fresh touch should not miss the fashion section. Haute Xklusive, La Robe Classique, Asangenta, Utonez Clothier, Kofikyere Klothing, Regy Couture, JAT Couture and other fashion businesses are displaying a variety of clothing, accessories and stylish pieces. Whether you are searching for an elegant outfit for a special occasion, something fashionable for everyday wear or a unique piece to make a statement, the exhibition offers an opportunity to explore different styles and engage directly with designers and vendors. Shoes TE3 is also showcasing footwear for different sizes, while Kinky Love Crochet is bringing hair products and wigs to the exhibition. Beauty enthusiasts are equally catered for, with Haus of Lush, RNS Beauty, Leepoku Ventures, Atlas Prime Merchantile and Chocho displaying cosmetics and personal-care products. Mist and Strands, Reed Diffusers Ghana and Esquicet Scents are also presenting products to enhance personal care and the atmosphere in homes. And for those looking to add a little romance and creativity to their appearance, Hetty’s Beads is offering something particularly intriguing. At the exhibition, the company’s Chief Executive Officer, Henrietta Fosuah, has been introducing patrons to the idea of using customised waist beads to communicate affection and romantic messages. Imagine having your partner’s name or a sweet message incorporated into your waist beads. It is fashion with a personal touch! Men are also being encouraged to visit the stand and learn more about the meanings behind the different designs. The business is offering discounts on purchases during the exhibition, making it another interesting stop for patrons. Electronics, technology and household solutions – explore, compare and shop! The fair is not just about food, fashion and beauty. Technology enthusiasts and shoppers looking for household essentials also have plenty to discover. Galop Sea Limited is showcasing laptops and accessories, while Xfromo Hypermart is exhibiting mobile phones and accessories, including Google Pixel devices. Those interested in modern transportation can explore electric vehicles from Atlantic Meridian EV, while Vital Vendors is offering car essentials. For homeowners and prospective property owners, there are also businesses presenting products and services in housing, roofing and real estate. Sintex Tank is showcasing water storage solutions, while DBS is exhibiting housing and roofing products. Kemz Ceramics is also displaying ceramic products, offering another opportunity for patrons to explore items that can add a touch of elegance to their homes. From household improvements to technological upgrades, the fair provides an opportunity to engage vendors, compare available products and make informed purchasing decisions. Businesses, entrepreneurs and service seekers are not left out Beyond the products on display, the exhibition is also providing an opportunity for patrons to discover services that can make business and everyday life easier. Katon 360 Technologies is showcasing a digital platform for small and medium-sized enterprises, while Solid Connect is presenting an application designed for artisans. We Shop Africa and Ayuda are also represented in the e-commerce space. Financial and institutional services are another major feature, with Ecobank, MTN, the Ghana Export Promotion Authority (GEPA) and Glico Life among the participating organisations. Whether you are an entrepreneur looking for business support, a consumer exploring financial services or someone interested in connecting with established institutions, the fair offers an opportunity to engage directly with representatives. Expect entertainment, interactions and exciting encounters While shopping is a major attraction, the atmosphere promises to offer much more than transactions and price negotiations. For entrepreneurs, it is also an opportunity to tell their stories, demonstrate their products, attract potential customers and create lasting business connections. The fair brings businesses and consumers together in an environment where products can be experienced first-hand, and business owners can receive direct feedback from prospective buyers. Why you should make it to Ghud Park today The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair is designed to bring the marketplace closer to consumers. Instead of visiting several shops and businesses across the city, patrons can explore products and services from more than 80 brands at one location. There are special offers to explore, new brands to discover, business owners to meet and a variety of products to choose from. For those preparing for the Christmas season, this is also an excellent opportunity to begin shopping early, explore gift ideas and take advantage of available promotional deals. The fair builds on the maiden edition held in October 2025, which attracted more than 160 exhibitors and over 1,000 visitors on its opening day. The inaugural event also provided businesses with opportunities to increase sales, improve brand visibility and connect with prospective customers. This year’s exhibition continues that mission by creating a marketplace where Ghanaian businesses can showcase their ingenuity, and consumers can access a wide range of locally produced goods and services. So, what are you waiting for? Gather your family, call your friends and make your way to Ghud Park at Accra Mall. Come ready to shop, discover exciting products, enjoy the atmosphere and support Ghanaian businesses. Take time to visit the different stands, ask about available discounts and promotional packages, and leave with purchases that offer value for money. The second day has just commenced, and there is still plenty of time to be part of the excitement. The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 runs from Friday, November 13, to Sunday, November 15, at Ghud Park, Accra Mall.

items.title: Salémata : une infirmerie scolaire inaugurée au lycée
items.description: Le lycée de Salémata dispose désormais d’une infirmerie scolaire. L’infrastructure a été inaugurée vendredi 13 novembre 2026 par le Mouvement des jeunes leaders du Sénégal, dans le cadre d’un programme national visant à améliorer la prise en charge sanitaire des élèves en milieu scolaire. Selon son président, Mame Samba Diamanka, cette initiative vise à apporter une réponse rapide aux malaises, blessures et autres urgences médicales dans les établissements publics. « Nous avons constaté beaucoup de malaises dans les écoles et des insuffisances dans la prise en charge des urgences médicales », a-t-il expliqué. A lire aussi : Kédougou : ActionAid renforce la résilience climatique à Tomboronkoto Le choix de Salémata répond à une volonté de réduire les inégalités territoriales, en accordant une attention particulière aux zones enclavées et les plus nécessiteuses. Le responsable s’est félicité de la mobilisation des populations autour du projet et a annoncé son extension progressive aux autres régions du Sénégal. À travers cette initiative, le mouvement entend faire de la santé un levier de réussite scolaire et offrir aux élèves un environnement d’apprentissage plus sûr. Amadou DIOP (Correspondant)

items.title: AMR: WHO warns of 4.7m deaths, demands urgent action as Abuja hosts global summit
items.description: … Says gap between political pledges and implementation remains wide … Warns livestock antibiotic use could rise 30% by 2040 without intervention By Chioma Obinna The World Health Organisation (WHO) has warned that antimicrobial resistance (AMR) remains one of the world’s gravest public health threats, with bacterial drug resistance associated with more than 4.7 million deaths in 2021, urging governments to translate political commitments into urgent, measurable action. The global health body said the growing threat, driven by the misuse and overuse of antibiotics and other antimicrobial medicines, weak infection prevention, poor water and sanitation, and environmental pollution, could undermine the treatment of common infections and reverse gains in human and animal health. The warning comes ahead of the 2026 World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week, WAAW, scheduled for November 18 to 24, with the theme, “One Health, One Action: Prevent AMR Now.” Speaking at the sixth Annual Global Media Forum on AMR, Dr Jean-Pierre Nyemazi, Director a.i. of WHO’s Department of Antimicrobial Resistance and Director of the Quadripartite Joint Secretariat on AMR, described the challenge as both a health emergency and a development threat. “AMR is one of the most urgent global health threats and development challenges. It threatens our ability to treat infections, protect animal and plant health, and produce safe food, and also has an impact on the environment,” he said. Nyemazi said the millions of deaths associated with bacterial AMR should not be treated as mere statistics. “These are not just statistics. Behind these numbers are patients, families, farmers and communities,” he said. He expressed concern that despite global political commitments to tackle AMR, implementation remained far below expectations. At the 2024 United Nations General Assembly High-Level Meeting on AMR, world leaders adopted a Political Declaration, committing to reduce bacterial AMR-associated deaths by 10 per cent by 2030, against a 2019 baseline of 4.95 million. They also pledged to ensure that at least 60 per cent of countries had funded national AMR action plans by 2030 and called for at least $100 million in catalytic funding, including through the AMR Multi-Partner Trust Fund. However, Nyemazi said: “The gap between commitments and pledges versus implementation remains wide,” identifying inadequate financing, fragmented coordination and weak surveillance as major obstacles. He said the forthcoming Fifth Global High-Level Ministerial Conference on AMR, scheduled for Abuja, Nigeria, from December 6 to 8, would provide an opportunity to review progress, confront implementation challenges and renew political commitment. An updated Global Action Plan on AMR for 2026–2036 has been finalised and is expected to be launched at the Abuja conference. Work is also advancing towards establishing the Independent Panel on Evidence for Action against AMR, which is expected to be launched at the meeting. Nyemazi urged journalists to sustain public attention and hold governments and other stakeholders accountable. “You make visible what is often invisible. Your accurate, evidence-based and solution-focused reporting shapes public understanding, sustains political attention and holds all of us accountable,” he told journalists. In his remarks, Dr Kefas Samson, Senior Technical Officer and Lead of Multisectoral Coordination in WHO’s AMR Department, said country-level action was critical to closing the gap between global commitments and actual progress. He identified inadequate funding, weak national surveillance of antimicrobial resistance and use, poor infection prevention in healthcare facilities, limited diagnostic capacity, unequal access to quality-assured medicines and shortages of health workers as major barriers. “Significant gaps still persist, and progress among countries also remains uneven,” Samson said. He described the updated 2026–2036 Global Action Plan as “a renewed blueprint” for translating the 2024 UN Political Declaration into measurable national interventions. “It is not just a plan; but a framework that translates the aspirations and ambitions of the political declaration on AMR 2024 into tangible actions at the country level,” he said. The plan adopts a One Health approach, integrating human, animal, agricultural and environmental health, with priorities including prevention, surveillance, responsible antimicrobial use, stronger laboratories, equitable access to medicines, resilient supply chains, research and sustainable financing. Samson said other 2030 targets included ensuring that 70 per cent of antibiotics used in human health belonged to WHO’s Access group, while 80 per cent of countries should have the capacity to test for priority bacterial and fungal pathogens under the Global Antimicrobial Resistance and Use Surveillance System. Meanwhile, the Food and Agriculture Organisation of the United Nations (FAO) warned that global antibiotic use in livestock could increase by nearly 30 per cent by 2040 if preventive measures were not strengthened. Dr Junxia Song, FAO Deputy Chief Veterinarian and Chief of its One Health and Disease Control Branch, said improved animal health and farm management practices could reduce antibiotic use by as much as 57 per cent. “Prevention must become central to the global fight against antimicrobial resistance, with farmers placed at the heart of the response,” she said. Song said FAO’s assessment showed that agricultural priorities remained inadequately integrated and funded in many national AMR action plans, while nearly half of countries had either no or only partial legislation governing antimicrobial use in animal and plant health. She said FAO was addressing the challenge through its 10-year initiative, Reduce the Need for Antimicrobials on Farms (RENOFARM), which has attracted more than 400 partners, including over 80 FAO member countries. The initiative focuses on better animal health services, improved production practices, alternatives and innovation, incentives and partnerships. On the environmental dimension, Aitziber Echeverria, AMR Coordinator, Chemicals and Health Branch of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), warned that the global response would remain incomplete unless environmental pollution was tackled alongside human and animal health interventions. “The environment plays a key role in the emergence, transmission and spread of AMR. The environment and AMR cannot be treated separately. That is the One Health concept,” she said. She identified pharmaceutical manufacturing, agriculture and food systems, healthcare, and municipal waste and wastewater management as priority areas requiring urgent intervention. “Environmental action on AMR is not an optional addition to the response. It is a prerequisite for success,” Echeverria said. She called for investments in wastewater treatment, safe disposal of antimicrobial medicines, laboratory capacity and environmental surveillance, noting that environmental authorities remained inadequately represented in many national AMR governance structures. Similarly, Dr Jane Lwoyero, Programme Officer at the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), called for increased investment in animal health, vaccination, farm biosecurity, surveillance and veterinary services. “For every US$1 that is invested in prevention of animal diseases and for better animal health systems, we are ensured of getting a return of US$28,” she said. Lwoyero disclosed that fewer than 20 per cent of WOAH member countries vaccinated animals against notifiable diseases, while animal diseases caused estimated annual global losses of up to $300 billion. She said global antimicrobial use in animals declined by three per cent between 2019 and 2024, but warned that antimicrobial use for growth promotion remained a concern. Chairperson of the Global AMR Media Alliance and host of the forum, Shobha Shukla, said even everyday injuries, including cuts and needle pricks, could expose people to drug-resistant infections. She called for responsible use of antibiotics, antifungals, antivirals and antiparasitic medicines, alongside stronger infection prevention. Shukla said the central challenge was no longer simply getting countries to recognise AMR or develop national action plans, but ensuring adequate funding, surveillance, laboratory capacity and accountability to implement them. She called for a people-centred, rights-based and gender-transformative response that would prevent unnecessary antimicrobial use without denying essential medicines to people who genuinely need them. The post AMR: WHO warns of 4.7m deaths, demands urgent action as Abuja hosts global summit appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Bauchi suspends Emir of Lame over alleged abuse of office
items.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi The Bauchi State Government has suspended the Emir of Lame, Alhaji Aliyu Yakubu Lame, over allegations of abuse of office, unlawful interference in land administration and unauthorised collection of levies. The government also constituted a 12-member Administrative Panel of Inquiry, chaired by a retired Deputy Inspector-General of Police, Sani Mohammed, to investigate the allegations and submit its report within three weeks. Other allegations against the monarch include interference in mining operations and arbitrary exercise of traditional authority. The state government said the suspension followed petitions and intelligence reports from community leaders, stakeholders and security agencies concerning activities allegedly capable of threatening peace and security in the emirate. It explained that although the Emir had responded to the allegations, his explanations were considered unsatisfactory, prompting the decision to constitute the investigative panel. However, the government emphasised that the allegations remained unproven and assured that the monarch would be given an opportunity to defend himself before the panel. The suspended Emir was directed to remain within the emirate throughout the investigation and barred from performing official and traditional functions pending the submission of the panel’s report. Meanwhile, the Senior Councillor of the Lame Emirate Council, Alhaji Bala Abubakar Gumau, popularly known as Galadiman Lame, has been directed to oversee the day-to-day administration of the emirate. The government urged residents, traditional titleholders and other stakeholders in Toro Local Government Area to remain calm, law-abiding and cooperate with the investigative panel. The post Bauchi suspends Emir of Lame over alleged abuse of office appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Education Minister promises Mfantsipim School a 66-seater bus as part of its 150th anniversary celebration
items.description: The Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, has pledged to provide Mfantsipim School with a 66-seater bus as part of activities marking the institution’s 150th anniversary. He gave the assurance during the school’s sesquicentennial celebration, stating that the vehicle would be delivered on or before January 1, 2027. Mr Iddrisu said the commitment was being made on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama and the government, in response to the needs of the school as it marks a major milestone in its history. Addressing the gathering, the Education Minister specifically assured the school’s Senior Prefect that the government would fulfil the promise within the stated timeframe. “I want to assure the senior school prefect that, for and on behalf of President John Dramani Mahama and the government of Ghana, on or before 1st January, I will deliver a 66-seater bus to Mfantsipim School as part of your 150th anniversary celebration,” he said. The pledge forms part of the government’s recognition of the school’s longstanding contribution to education and national development. The announcement was one of the notable highlights of the anniversary celebration durbar on Saturday, November 14, which brought together government officials, traditional leaders, education stakeholders, alumni, staff, students and other well-wishers to commemorate 150 years of the institution’s existence. Founded in 1876, Mfantsipim School has played a significant role in Ghana’s educational history, producing generations of professionals and leaders who have contributed to the country’s development.

items.title: 2027: Why Tinubu may still win presidential election
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA – President Bola Tinubu goes into the January 16, 2027 presidential election with 31 governors from the All Progressives Congress, APC, as well as three from the “opposition”, a run of off-season victories and an opposition split across multiple platforms. Read Also: * 2027: Why Peter Obi could win presidential election * 2027: Why Atiku could win presidential election These are advantages that may carry him to a second term, even though living standards for millions have crumbled under his reforms. He faces Atiku Abubakar of the African Democratic Congress, ADC; Peter Obi of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, and Seyi Makinde of the Allied Peoples Movement, APM. These are among 18 candidates on the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC final list. Kashim Shettima, a fellow Muslim, is again his running mate. Cost of living crisis The pain is measurable. The World Bank says the immediate effects of subsidy removal and exchange rate adjustment were a sharp rise in the cost of living, hitting poor and vulnerable households hardest. Subsidy removal pushed up transport and logistics costs, while the floating of the Naira triggered depreciation and costlier imports. Petrol is about six times higher than before the subsidy ended, and the World Bank puts poverty at just over half the population last year, up from about 42 per cent in 2022. Development partners say more than 31.8 million Nigerians face acute food insecurity. Food accounts for over 60 per cent of consumption among low-income households. Borrowing has also grown. Public debt rose from N87.38 trillion in June 2023 to N166.79 trillion in June 2026, about 90.9 per cent higher. External debt climbed from about $43.1 billion to about $54.5 billion. The NDC has criticised a proposed N10.79 trillion external loan. The government’s defence is that the reforms were unavoidable. Finance Minister Taiwo Oyedele said the country was living in “fiscal illusions.” The International Monetary Fund, IMF, has called subsidy removal one of Nigeria’s most important macroeconomic reforms. Inflation down The numbers are also moving in his favour. Headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September 2026, its fourth straight monthly decline, and the Naira strengthened to N1,333 per dollar in mid-October. External reserves have climbed to $55.07 billion. Even so, the central bank rate stands at 26.5 per cent, which keeps loans out of reach for many businesses. Governors: More money, less accountability The governors are both his greatest asset and a weakest spot. States and local governments have received a combined N31.77 trillion from the Federation Account Allocation Committee FAAC since the subsidy was removed. Civil society groups say the money has not translated into better infrastructure or services, and that governors still hold sway over council funds despite the Supreme Court’s 2024 autonomy judgment. Tinubu has conceded the problem publicly. He recently told governors to “wet the ground” and deliver dividends of democracy at the grassroots. There is no sign that any consequence has followed. 31 govs and their worth At least nine governors, among them those of Plateau, Kano, Delta, Enugu and Bayelsa, have crossed to the APC since 2023. The party says it now controls about 31 governors, up from about 22 in the last cycle, and is targeting at least 20 states. It also holds 89 senators and 282 House members. Three opposition governors have also declared support for his second-term bid. Critics call this a drift towards a one-party state. Tinubu has rejected the accusation and urged his party to bring in more defectors. The governors’ value at the ballot box is less certain. Analysts note that the number of governors backing a candidate does not directly measure his popularity. Allies have set a target of 18.7 million votes, against the roughly 8.79 million he won in 2023. Whether the 31 are genuinely loyal is also in question, and Federal Capital Territory FCT minister Nyesom Wike’s separate coalition is already feuding with them. Off-season results: a mixed scorecard The APC can point to several wins. In Ekiti, Governor Biodun Oyebanji became the first governor to win back-to-back re-election, and the party took five of six by-elections. It also won five of the six Federal Capital Territory, FCT, area councils in February. One tally says the APC has won five of eight off-cycle governorship elections since Tinubu took office, plus 15 of 19 National Assembly by-elections. But the biggest recent test went the other way. In Osun, Governor Ademola Adeleke of the Accord beat the APC candidate by 66,252 votes – 511,067 to 444,815. The loss came in the South-West, Tinubu’s home zone, and Adeleke had earlier declared support for Tinubu’s re-election. In Anambra, Governor Charles Soludo of the All Progressives Grand Alliance, APGA, won all 21 local government areas. Turnout was about 22 per cent. Split opposition The opposition is Tinubu’s strongest card. In 2023, Atiku and Obi polled more than 13 million votes between them, well above Tinubu’s winning tally. Tinubu won with 36.6 per cent against 29 per cent for Atiku and 25 per cent for Obi. This time they are on separate tickets, and Atiku’s has been shaken. On November 5, Justice Peter Lifu of the Federal High Court in Abuja voided the ADC’s leadership and primaries, which stripped Atiku of his nomination. Atiku has said he will appeal. Makinde has confirmed talks with Atiku and Obi on a possible alliance. Both camps had earlier cooled on a single candidate, and no mechanism for choosing one has been agreed. The odds Several things favour Tinubu. He holds the incumbency and most of the governors. The opposition is fractured, and in 2023 he scored over 25 per cent in 30 states, five more than the 25 required. Inflation is falling and the Naira is arguably steadier. The election is also only nine weeks away, so he has little time to absorb new shocks. Against him are poverty at roughly 60 per cent, petrol prices several times higher than before the subsidy ended, a debt stock that has almost doubled and a Muslim-Muslim ticket that the Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, condemned in 2023. The Osun loss shows that governors and incumbency cannot guarantee a result even in his own region. The opposition may still unite, and a late alliance would make the contest far tighter. Obi’s running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso, has already told the APC what he thinks of the numbers. Those who believe that 30-plus governors make defeat impossible, he said, are “making a very big mistake.” Vanguard News The post 2027: Why Tinubu may still win presidential election appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nigeria won’t progress till it abandons primitive leadership selection — Jonathan
items.description: By Dapo Akinrefon & Henry Obetta Former President Goodluck Jonathan has warned that Nigeria will continue to struggle with development until it abandons what he described as primitive methods of selecting political leaders based on religion, ethnicity, language and other narrow considerations. Jonathan said the country must move away from such practices and prioritise competence and merit in leadership recruitment, stressing that no matter how qualified an individual might be, Nigeria could not make meaningful progress if leadership selection remained tied to divisive considerations. The former president spoke on Saturday at the Herbert Macaulay Colloquium held in Lagos to mark the 162nd anniversary of the birth of the nationalist pioneer. Born on November 14, 1864, Macaulay is regarded as one of the founding figures of Nigerian nationalism. Speaking at the colloquium, Jonathan said: “We are still suffering from political leaders being recruited based on religion, language and all kinds of things. Sometimes it is even beyond Muslim or Christian. I know of a particular state in southern Nigeria that 99.9 per cent of them are Christians. But if you don’t belong to one particular denomination, you cannot be the governor of the state. “That is the kind of thing we do. So no matter how good you are, until we move away from these primitive ways of recruiting political leaders, this country cannot go.” The former president identified leadership challenges, institutional weaknesses, corruption, policy inconsistency, inadequate infrastructure and insecurity as some of the factors impeding Nigeria’s development. He also called for comprehensive democratic reforms, describing Nigeria’s current democratic system as “opaque and amorphous”. According to him, the country’s democratic system must be reviewed to reflect popular participation, the rule of law, respect for human rights, judicial independence, accountability, pluralism and a vibrant civil society. Jonathan further stressed the need to prioritise functional education and establish research-intensive universities capable of driving technological advancement and innovation. Citing India, Singapore and South Korea as examples, he said the countries had leveraged quality education to achieve remarkable development. He said, “You can’t go anywhere with weak educational institutions.” He added that Nigeria must deliberately invest in its best brains and establish world-class universities to compete globally. Paying tribute to Herbert Macaulay and other founding nationalists, Jonathan said the greatest honour the country could accord them was not merely celebrating their sacrifices but building a nation that reflected the ideals for which they fought. The post Nigeria won’t progress till it abandons primitive leadership selection — Jonathan appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Julius Debrah calls for unity as NDC elects Eastern Regional executives
items.description: The Chief of Staff, Julius Debrah, has called on delegates participating in the NDC’s Eastern Regional executive election to uphold peace and unity, reminding them that the outcome of the contest should not divide the party. He made the call during a visit to the voting centre at Kwahu Obomeng, where he interacted with delegates and supporters. Mr Debrah said the party’s collective interest must take precedence over the ambitions of individual candidates, adding that members should continue to work together irrespective of the results. “I urge all the delegates to be united and vote peacefully today. The atmosphere here and the enthusiasm tell us that indeed we are resetting the country. We are all one family, and we should remain united regardless of who wins or loses,” he said. The Chief of Staff also expressed optimism about the NDC’s ability to strengthen its electoral presence in the Eastern Region, where the party made gains in recent general elections. Mr Debrah, who hails from the Eastern Region, expressed confidence that the party could build on its recent performance and make further progress in future elections. The newly elected regional executives are expected to play a key role in strengthening the party’s structures at the grassroots and sustaining its efforts to expand its support base in the region.

items.title: Budget général Sénégal : 3 785,2 milliards de FCFA de recettes réalisées en septembre 2026
items.description: Les recettes du budget général du Sénégal ont été réalisées à hauteur de 3 785,2 milliards à fin septembre 2026, soit 63,8 % de l’objectif annuel de 5 932,2 milliards. C’est ce qui ressort du rapport trimestriel d'exécution du budget au 30 septembre 2026 rendu public samedi par le ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et du Plan. Au troisième trimestre 2026, le budget sénégalais affiche une exécution partielle avec un déficit de 585,5 milliards FCFA, soit 2,5 % du PIB. Selon le rapport trimestriel d'exécution du budget au 30 septembre 2026, publié le samedi 14 novembre 2026 par le ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et du Plan, l'activité économique au niveau national est restée bien orientée avec une progression du PIB réel de 6,1 % au deuxième trimestre 2026, dont 6,4 % hors hydrocarbures (pétrole et gaz). L'inflation s'est établie à 1,0 % en septembre, après 1,2 % en août. « Les recettes du budget général ont été réalisées à hauteur de 3 785,2 milliards à fin septembre 2026, soit 63,8 % de l’objectif annuel de 5 932,2 milliards. Les recettes internes ont atteint 3.739,3 milliards, soit 65,1% de l’objectif annuel et 97,6% de la cible à fin septembre (3.831,0 milliards), et ont progressé de 16,8% sur un an », indique le rapport de la tutelle. A lire aussi : Examen PLFI 2027 : Cheikh Diba : « Un budget ne se juge pas à ses intentions » La moins-value de 91,7 milliards s’explique principalement, selon la même source, par le rendement inférieur aux prévisions des mesures du Plan de redressement économique et social (PRES) qui étaient de 162,3 milliards. Ce rendement est partiellement compensé par la plus-value des recettes hors PRES de 70,6 milliards. Concernant les recettes fiscales, elles se sont établies à 3 484,3 milliards, soit 64,7 % de l’objectif annuel et 96,5 % de la cible à fin septembre de 3 611,4 milliards, correspondant à une moins-value de 127,1 milliards. « En glissement annuel, elles sont en hausse de 496,4 milliards (+16,6 %), principalement sous l’effet de l’impôt sur les sociétés. La moins-value fiscale de 127,1 milliards résulte du niveau de mobilisation des recettes du PRES, inférieur de 154,3 milliards à la cible à fin septembre. Ce déficit est partiellement compensé par une plus-value de 27,2 milliards sur les recettes fiscales hors PRES », lit-on dans le rapport. 255,0 milliards de recettes non fiscales recouvrées Il ressort également de ce rapport que les recettes non fiscales ont été recouvrées pour un montant de 255,0 milliards, soit 116,1 % de la cible à fin septembre de 219,6 milliards et 71,6 % de la prévision annuelle. Elles se sont accrues de 40,9 milliards sur un an, portées par les revenus du domaine, en lien avec la redevance minière, et par les recettes issues de l’exploitation des hydrocarbures. Toutefois, cette bonne tenue des recettes non fiscales contraste, selon le ministère, avec les réalisations des recettes non fiscales du PRES, ressorties à 1 milliard sur des prévisions annuelles de 59 milliards de FCFA, soit un taux de 1,69 %. Les dons ont été mobilisés à hauteur de 45,9 milliards, soit 24,0 % de l’objectif annuel de 191,5 milliards. Ils comprennent 45,8 milliards de dons en capital et 0,1 milliard de dons budgétaires. « Les dépenses totales du budget général ont été exécutées pour un montant de 4 370,7 milliards à fin septembre 2026, soit 60,8 % des crédits ouverts. Les taux d’exécution des dépenses ordinaires et des dépenses en capital s’établissent respectivement à 75,4 % et 38,1 % », souligne le ministère en charge des Finances. 3 207,7 milliards de dépenses ordinaires Le rapport d’exécution budgétaire informe aussi que les dépenses ordinaires se sont chiffrées à 3 302,7 milliards, soit 75,4 % des crédits ouverts. Elles comprennent notamment les dépenses de personnel pour 1 142,5 milliards et les transferts courants pour 1 049,9 milliards. Les charges financières de la dette ont, pour leur part, atteint 874,0 milliards tandis que les acquisitions de biens et services se sont établies à 236,3 milliards. Pour les dépenses en capital, elles ont été réalisées à hauteur de 1 068,0 milliards à fin septembre 2026, soit 38,1 % des crédits ouverts. Elles sont constituées de 641,3 milliards d’investissements sur ressources internes, répartis entre les investissements directement exécutés par l’État pour 197,4 milliards et les transferts en capital pour 443,9 milliards et exécutés à hauteur de 22,1 % et 79,9 % respectivement. Le déficit budgétaire ressort à 585,5 milliards Il urge de noter également que pendant la période sous revue, les dépenses sur ressources extérieures s’établissent à 426,7 milliards, dont 381,4 milliards de prêts projets et 45,3 milliards de dons en capital, avec des taux d’exécution respectifs de 31,5 % et 31,2 %. « Le déficit budgétaire est ressorti à 585,5 milliards à fin septembre 2026, soit 2,5 % du PIB nominal de la LFI 2026, pour une cible annuelle de 1 245,1 milliards (5,4 % du même PIB) fixée dans la LFI 2026, dont il représente 47,0 % », informe le texte. Par rapport au Fonds national de retraite (FNR), il a dégagé un excédent de 28,2 milliards à fin septembre 2026. Les recettes se sont établies à 144,6 milliards et les dépenses à 116,4 milliards, soit 62,9 % de la dotation annuelle. Le nombre de cotisants est passé de 152 787 à 161 213 en glissement annuel, tandis que celui des pensionnés se situe à 77 850. À fin septembre 2026, selon le document, 188 organismes publics, disposant d’un budget consolidé de 2 445,6 milliards, ont été suivis. Les recettes mobilisées ont atteint 1 166,5 milliards (47,7 % des prévisions) et les dépenses exécutées 980,7 milliards (40,1 %). L’investissement affiche un taux d’exécution de 20,6 %, contre 58,3% pour le fonctionnement. Mariama DIEME

items.title: 2027: Why Peter Obi could win presidential election
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- AHEAD of next year’s elections, the National leadership of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, has already predicted an overwhelming victory for its presidential candidate, Peter Obi. They said the platform presents a formidable pathway to victory for the party. Read Also: * 2027: Why Tinubu may still win presidential election * 2027: Why Atiku could win presidential election The party said both the South-East and South-South are firmly blocked, and the North-West and North-East are equally blocked for Obi/ Kwankwaso for January 16, 2027 presidential election. According to the NDC, the 2023 election already demonstrated Obi’s clear electoral strength across the North-Central, where he carried Plateau, Nasarawa, and the FCT, stressing that Nigerians are ready to look past incumbency and deliver a decisive mandate for Peter Obi and the NDC. Speaking with Vanguard exclusively, the spokesperson, NDC National Campaign Council, Dr. Chiogo Constance Ikokwu said those who mistake Peter Obi’s gentlemanly demeanor for weakness overlook what she described as the grit and resilience of a leader who grew up navigating the tough, street-smart realities of Onitsha. The NDC National Campaign Council Spokesperson said another major advantage for the party that would contribute to its victory next year is that Kwankwasiyya movement is no pushover when it comes to electoral sturdiness against the backdrop that the group had been tested, it is a disciplined one and ready to defend its mandate at the polls. Ikokwu, who noted that no sensible election rigger would wish to confront the potent combination of the Obidient and Kwankwasiyya (OK) movements, stressed that as many voters demonstrated in the previous cycle, financial inducements on election day will not stop struggling citizens from voting their conscience, adding that Nigerians are ready to look past incumbency and deliver a decisive mandate for Peter Obi and the NDC. The NDC said Obi will win the presidential election despite the fact that critics often point to the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, boasting over 30 aligned state governors as an insurmountable advantage, stressing that Nigerian political history had proven it that governors do not cast votes, but citizens do. According to the NDC, In 2015, an incumbent president backed by the vast majority of state governors was defeated at the polls, and even in 2023, President Bola Tinubu lost key states where his most enthusiastic governors held sway, including Lagos, Kaduna under Nasir El-Rufai, and Imo. The NDC spokesperson said: “The 2027 Nigerian presidential election is shaping up not merely as a contest between political parties, but as a decisive referendum between entrenched incumbency and the survival of ordinary citizens. “Looking closely at the political mathematics, grassroots momentum, and prevailing economic realities, the joint ticket of Peter Obi and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) presents a formidable pathway to victory. “First, the sheer electoral arithmetic of an Obi–Kwankwaso alliance fundamentally alters Nigeria’s political landscape. In 2023, running separately without the backing of a single sitting state governor, Peter Obi won 12 states, including the Federal Capital Territory, on the strength of an organic, youth-driven Obidient movement across the South and North-Central. “Also consider that while INEC officially declared Tinubu the winner of Rivers State, Nigerians know who truly won that state. The Kwakwanso factor “Meanwhile, Rabiu Kwankwaso commanded a disciplined, revolutionary Kwankwasiyya grassroots network that dominated Kano and resonated deeply across the core North. Uniting these two massive, people-powered movements under the NDC bridges Nigeria’s traditional North–South divide, creating a broad coalition that rivals any political machine in Nigerian presidential history.” Ikokwu further said, “Unlike the Obi-Kwankwaso alliance, the Tinubu-Shettima ticket faces no viable path to victory. Both the South-East and South-South are firmly blocked, and the North-West and North-East are equally blocked. Moreover, the 2023 election already demonstrated Obi’s clear electoral strength across the North-Central, where he carried Plateau, Nasarawa, and the FCT. “Critics often point to the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) boasting over 30 aligned state governors as an insurmountable advantage. Yet Nigerian political history proves that governors do not cast votes—citizens do. In 2015, an incumbent president backed by the vast majority of state governors was defeated at the polls, and even in 2023, President Bola Tinubu lost key states where his most enthusiastic governors held sway, including Lagos, Kaduna under Nasir El-Rufai, and Imo. “Equally, the Kwankwasiyya movement is no pushover when it comes to electoral sturdiness; the group is tested, disciplined, and ready to defend its mandate at the polls. “Simply put, no sensible election rigger would wish to confront the potent combination of the Obidient and Kwankwasiyya (OK) movements. Unlike in 2023, when organizational gaps left opposition tallies vulnerable, the NDC is actively building disciplined, lawful structures to guard and protect every ballot across Nigeria’s 176,000 polling units. “Backed by over 200 million citizens determined to stand firm at the polls through peaceful civic vigilance and overwhelming turnout, intimidation or vote-buying will not override the will of the Nigerian people. As many voters demonstrated in the previous cycle, financial inducements on election day will not stop struggling citizens from voting their conscience. Economy “Above all, 2027 is a battle between the ruling establishment and millions of suffering Nigerians. Never in Nigeria’s peacetime history has the cost of basic human survival escalated by over 500 percent in such a short span. Staple foods have slipped out of reach, with a bag of rice surging from roughly ₦15,000 to over ₦70,000, while relentless fuel price hikes have crippled transportation, small businesses, and household incomes. Speaking on debt burden exceeding $120 billion by the present government as an advantage for Peter Obi to win the election, the NDC spokesperson said, “Simultaneously, the administration has presided over a total public debt burden exceeding $120 billion, alongside an independent inquiry into how borrowed funds and subsidy savings have been managed, without delivering tangible improvements in power supply, healthcare, or security. Today, no one is safe in Nigeria, thanks to President Tinubu. Nigerians are not fools. “They will cast their votes recognizing that President Tinubu failed to keep his 2023 campaign promises, and they are set to hold him accountable at the ballot box for the reckless manner in which he removed the fuel subsidy, a decision that has brought average citizens to their knees. At the polls, voters will demand a clear answer: Where are the savings from the removal of the fuel subsidy? That is, where is our money that Peter Obi has been asking?” Citing insecurity and hunger in the as parameters that will work against the President Tinubu led government, Ikokwu said, “Nowhere will the political fallout of this hardship be felt more acutely than in Northern Nigeria, where acute hunger and persistent insecurity have pushed communities to the brink. Beyond immediate survival, Northern voters are also weighing the strategic question of 2031 and national leadership succession, comparing the proven grassroots loyalty and developmental record of Kwankwaso alongside Obi against the current administration’s trajectory. “Ultimately, 2027 offers Nigerians a stark choice: between a ticket anchored in verifiable enterprise, prudence, and transparent wealth creation, and an incumbent establishment burdened by economic hardship and long-standing controversies over the origins of its wealth. Faced with empty stomachs and broken promises, Nigerians are ready to look past incumbency and deliver a decisive mandate for Peter Obi and the NDC.” Vanguard News The post 2027: Why Peter Obi could win presidential election appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ADC: Atiku hasn’t reached out to me despite coming from the same zone – Nafiu Bala
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo A factional leader of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Nafiu Bala Gombe, has expressed disappointment that former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has not personally reached out to him despite their coming from the same geopolitical zone. Bala, who spoke in an interview with BBC Hausa on Saturday, said he regarded Atiku as a father figure but was disappointed that the former vice-president had not contacted him amid the leadership crisis rocking the party. He said this while reacting to a court judgment that affirmed his faction’s position in the ADC leadership dispute, adding that he remained willing to work with Atiku, former Senate President David Mark and other party chieftains to strengthen the opposition ahead of the 2027 general elections. Bala said the judgment had vindicated his faction as the authentic leadership of the party, insisting that its position was based on the provisions of the ADC constitution. “Alhamdulillah. As we always say, truth is truth, while lies remain lies. Allah has vindicated us. The court has seen the merit of our case and our truthfulness and has decided to return the party leadership to us,” he said. He disclosed that his faction was awaiting the Certified True Copy of the judgment to enable it to approach the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for the necessary changes to the party’s leadership records. Bala, however, cautioned against interpreting the judgment as an opportunity to settle scores with members of the opposing faction, saying he was extending a hand of friendship to them. “This is not a fight. Allah has given us victory, but we are not enemies. We are extending a hand of friendship to them to stop being arrogant and whatever they may say, so that we can strengthen the opposition and face the government,” he said. He maintained that anyone seeking to join the ADC or contest an elective position on its platform must comply with the party’s constitution, particularly provisions governing membership registration, payment of dues and eligibility for leadership positions. According to him, the party’s constitution requires members to fulfil prescribed conditions, including two years of membership and payment of stipulated dues, before qualifying for leadership positions. He alleged that the opposing faction failed to follow the party’s membership registration procedures, claiming that David Mark obtained his membership card from a former national chairman in Abuja rather than registering at his ward. Bala said he had repeatedly warned the opposing group about the consequences of disregarding the party’s constitution, but his advice was ignored. He also dismissed allegations that he was being used by the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to destabilise the opposition, insisting that his court action was solely aimed at protecting his rights and upholding the ADC constitution. “I went to court with only the constitution. I told the world that if they had followed the right procedures, the court should rule in their favour. But if we were right, we should be given our rights,” he said. On the continued appearance of Atiku’s and David Mark’s names on INEC’s portal, Bala said the commission would act appropriately once it received the Certified True Copy of the judgment. He dismissed suggestions that INEC was deliberately delaying the implementation of the judgment, saying the commission might not have received the official court document. Bala also rejected arguments that the large crowds attracted by the ADC during political engagements in Sokoto and Kebbi states should have persuaded him to abandon the legal battle. READ ALSO: I went to court to defend my rights, not working for APC to destabilise opposition — Nafiu Bala He argued that political popularity and financial influence should not be used to justify disregard for the law, warning that the country could not make progress if influential politicians continued to violate established rules. The factional leader further claimed that some individuals involved in the dispute had circulated documents suggesting that he had resigned from his position, describing the claims as misleading. On the party’s preparations for the 2027 elections, Bala said his faction had directed all aspirants seeking elective positions on the ADC platform to continue their campaign activities. He urged members of the opposing faction to remain patient, follow the party’s constitutional procedures and complete their membership registration at their respective wards. On funding, he said his faction relied largely on membership dues and other contributions generated through the party’s internal activities. Bala also defended his security arrangements and lifestyle, saying he was entitled to protection like other prominent political figures. He added that he was a businessman with other sources of livelihood. He urged Nigerian youths to remain law-abiding and avoid being drawn into political confrontations, stressing that opposition politics should be conducted with respect for democratic institutions and the rule of law. Vanguard Newspaper The post ADC: Atiku hasn’t reached out to me despite coming from the same zone – Nafiu Bala appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: OIF : les remerciements du candidat de la Roumanie qui acte le retrait de la candidature de Juliana Lumumba

items.title: Émigration irrégulière : Une nouvelle pirogue échoue à Sagg, aucun mort enregistré
items.description: Alors que le deuil des victimes du naufrage d’une pirogue au large de Loumpoul, dans le département de Kébémer, n’est pas encore achevé, une autre embarcation transportant des candidats à l’émigration irrégulière s’est échouée, ce samedi, à Sagg, une localité située dans la commune de Léona, dans le département de Louga. Selon notre source, les migrants auraient quitté la Gambie. Après six jours passés en mer, leur embarcation de fortune a finalement échoué à Sagg. Notre interlocuteur précise que tous les passagers s’en sont sortis indemnes. Aucune perte en vie humaine n’a été enregistrée. Certains migrants ont pris la fuite, tandis que d’autres ont été interpellés par les forces de défense et de sécurité. Malgré les risques et les dangers liés à ces traversées périlleuses, des jeunes continuent, coûte que coûte, de tenter de rallier l’Europe à bord de pirogues. Cette succession de départs et de naufrages témoigne de l’ampleur persistante du phénomène de l’émigration irrégulière. Face à cette situation préoccupante, il devient urgent de trouver des solutions durables pour offrir des perspectives aux jeunes et les dissuader de risquer leur vie dans les eaux de l’Atlantique. Falel Pam

items.title: ADC leadership crisis: Nafiu Bala extends olive branch to Atiku, David Mark faction
items.description: …Says court has vindicated authentic party leadership …Insists aspirants should continue campaigns By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo A factional leader of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Nafiu Bala Gombe, has extended an olive branch to former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, former Senate President David Mark and other chieftains of the party following a court judgment that affirmed his faction’s position in the party’s leadership dispute. Bala, who spoke on BBC Hausa on Saturday while reacting to the judgment, said the ruling had vindicated his faction as the authentic leadership of the ADC, insisting that its position was based on the provisions of the party’s constitution. “Alhamdulillah. As we always say, truth is truth, while lies remain lies. Allah has vindicated us. The court has seen the merit of our case and our truthfulness and has decided to return the party leadership to us,” he said. He disclosed that his faction was awaiting the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment to enable it to approach the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) for the necessary changes to the party’s leadership records. Bala, however, said the judgment should not be seen as an opportunity to settle scores with the opposing faction, stressing that he was willing to work with Atiku, David Mark and other prominent politicians to strengthen the opposition ahead of the 2027 general elections. “This is not a fight. Allah has given us victory, but we are not enemies. We are extending a hand of friendship to them to stop being arrogant and whatever they may say so that we can strengthen the opposition and face the government,” he said. He maintained that those interested in joining the ADC or seeking elective positions under its platform must comply with the party’s constitution, particularly the provisions governing registration at the ward level, payment of membership dues and eligibility for leadership positions. According to him, the party’s constitution stipulates that members must fulfil the prescribed requirements, including two years of membership and payment of stipulated dues, before qualifying for leadership positions. He accused the opposing faction of disregarding the party’s registration procedures, alleging that David Mark obtained his membership card from a former national chairman in Abuja instead of registering at his ward. Bala said he had repeatedly cautioned the opposing group about the consequences of failing to follow the party’s constitution but that his advice was ignored. He also dismissed allegations that he was being used to destabilise the opposition or working for the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), insisting that his legal action was solely aimed at protecting his rights and the party’s constitution. “I went to court with only the constitution. I told the world that if they had followed the right procedures, the court should rule in their favour. But if we were right, we should be given our rights,” he said. Reacting to the continued appearance of Atiku and David Mark’s names on INEC’s portal, Bala said the electoral commission was law-abiding and would act appropriately after receiving the certified true copy of the judgment. He dismissed suggestions that INEC was deliberately delaying the implementation of the judgment, explaining that the commission might not have received the official court document. Bala also rejected the argument that the large crowds attracted by the ADC during political engagements in Sokoto and Kebbi states should have persuaded him to abandon the legal battle. He said political popularity and financial influence should not be used as justification for disregarding the law, adding that Nigeria could not make progress if influential politicians continued to violate established rules. The ADC factional leader further claimed that some individuals involved in the legal dispute had circulated documents suggesting that he had resigned from his position, describing such claims as misleading. On his relationship with Atiku, Bala said he regarded the former vice-president as a father figure, noting that they came from the same geopolitical zone. He, however, expressed disappointment that Atiku had never personally reached out to him despite the controversy, while some party chieftains had continued to describe him as a spoiler. Bala said his faction had directed all aspirants seeking elective positions on the ADC platform to continue their campaign activities while urging members of the opposing faction to exercise patience, follow the party’s constitutional procedures and register properly at their wards. On the party’s source of funding, he said his faction relied largely on membership dues and other contributions generated through the party’s internal activities. He also defended his security arrangements and lifestyle, saying he was entitled to protection like other prominent political figures, adding that he was a businessman and had other sources of livelihood. Bala called on Nigerian youths to remain law-abiding and avoid being drawn into political confrontations, insisting that opposition politics should be conducted with respect for democratic institutions and the rule of law. items.title: Achakzai, Abbas move FCC for release of Sohail Afridi, detained lawmakers
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The leaders of the opposition in both Houses of Parliament on Saturday approached the Federal Constitutional Court (FCC), seeking the immediate release of Sohail Afridi, the non-functional Khyber Pakhtunkhwa chief minister, along with eight other elected members of the provincial assembly and six members of the National Assembly. Afridi has not been seen since the Centre imposed governor’s rule and emergency in KP on Oct 11. The very next day, a federal minister confirmed that he and some of his cabinet members were in preventive custody . While the government has transferred powers to KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, the PTI has asserted that Afridi “remains and shall continue” to serve as the KP chief minister with the “confidence and support” of party founder and ex-premier Imran Khan. On Saturday, National Assembly Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai and Senate Opposition Leader Raja Nasir Abbas jointly filed a petition before the FCC. The petition sought the enforcement of fundamental rights and constitutional protections against the alleged unlawful arrest, detention and confinement of Afridi, KP Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, Fazal Shakoor Khan, Dr Amjad Ali, Sultan Room, Yameen Khan, Abdus Salam Afridi, Muhammad Azam Khan and Ikram Ghazi, as well as six members of the National Assembly — Junaid Akbar Khan, Dr Amjad Ali Khan, Iqbal Khan Afridi, Fazal Mohammad Khan, Zubair Wazir and Maulana Naseem Ali Shah. The petition said it raised substantial questions of public importance concerning the supremacy of the Constitution, the sanctity of the democratic mandate, constitutional limits on executive authority under Articles 232, 234 and 245, and the protection of fundamental rights guaranteed under Articles 4, 9, 10, 14, 17 and 19-A of the Constitution. The petition also sought disclosure of the places of detention, production of the alleged detainees before the FCC, a declaration that their custody was unlawful and without lawful authority, and appropriate constitutional relief in the interest of justice and the rule of law. The federal secretaries of interior and defence, the KP chief secretary, the secretary of the KP Home and Tribal Affairs Department, the provincial inspector general of police, the Peshawar capital city police officer, the Peshawar deputy commissioner and the Federal Investigation Agency (FIA) director general were named as respondents. The petition raised the question of whether the constitutional mandate conferred upon members of the National Assembly and provincial assemblies through the electoral process carried with it enforceable constitutional protection against arbitrary state action designed to obstruct, frustrate or undermine their participation in representative governance. “Whether the arrest, intimidation, coercive restraint or other unlawful interference with elected legislators, in circumstances affecting their ability to represent their respective constituencies, amounts to an indirect disenfranchisement of the electorate and an impairment of the constitutional scheme of representative democracy?” it stated. The petition questioned the selective or collective targeting of elected representatives on account of their political affiliation, parliamentary position or participation in opposition politics and contended that these constitute discriminatory treatment, political victimisation and an abuse of public authority contrary to Articles 4, 14, 17 and 25 of the Constitution. It also prayed that the FCC declare that the Constitution was the supreme law of the land and that no proclamation of emergency, assumption of provincial executive authority, deployment of the armed forces or other extraordinary governmental measure could confer upon any state authority unfettered power to disregard fundamental rights, constitutional safeguards or the democratic mandate of the people. The petition further requested the court to declare that the “liberty, dignity, political association and representative functions of elected members were constitutionally protected, and that any arrest, detention, confinement, restriction of movement or coercive action against them was unlawful, unconstitutional and without legal effect”. “Moreover, the electoral mandate of the affected elected representatives cannot be defeated, neutralised or rendered ineffective through arbitrary executive action, political victimisation or the misuse of state machinery. “The people of KP are constitutionally entitled to effective representation through their duly elected representatives.” It also requested the FCC to order the production before the court of the members in custody. It further pleaded that Articles 232, 234 and 245 of the Constitution must be exercised strictly within their respective constitutional parameters and cannot be invoked to justify the suppression of political dissent, disabling of elected representatives, interference with parliamentary functions or circumvention of the fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution. The petition argued that the exercise of executive and administrative authority under governor’s rule does not suspend the constitutional obligations of the state, displace the supremacy of fundamental rights or place the actions of public functionaries beyond the scrutiny of the FCC. On Thursday, PTI lawmaker Shandana Gulzar also approached the FCC, seeking the immediate release of Afrid, the provincial assembly speaker and other party workers. The petition requested the FCC to order the respondents to “immediately disclose before the court their whereabouts, the identity of the authority exercising custody, the legal instrument and statutory provisions invoked as well as the grounds of detention and the date and circumstances of their taking into custody”. It further urged the court to order the production of the PTI’s provincial leadership in person so that their present condition, liberty and legal status be ascertained and the “legality of any such restraint upon their liberty be examined judicially”. Separately, Abbas and Balochistan National Party Chairman Sardar Akhtar Jan Mengal also approached the FCC on Saturday, seeking their impleadment in the case concerning the restraint imposed on the Peshawar High Court (PHC) from hearing petitions relating to the detention of PTI activists, which is likely to take up on Monday (Nov 16). The PHC on Oct 31 granted interim bail to scores of PTI activists detained under the Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance following the imposition of emergency. However, the FCC on Nov 5 restrained the high court from hearing cases concerning the arrests of scores of PTI activists detained under the ordinance. Through a miscellaneous application, the applicants through their counsel Sardar Latif Khosa, pleaded that they were the necessary and proper party to the proceedings since the FCC’s Nov 5 order of restrained the high court rom hearing cases concerning arrest of scores of PTI activists detained under Section 3 of the Pakistan Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance following the imposition of governor’s rule in KP. The application said the FCC’s Nov 5 order directly affected their constitutional rights. It contended that if the applicants were not impleaded, they would suffer irreparable loss and would be condemned unheard, in violation of Article 10-A of the Constitution. “That the applicants being proper and necessary party to the proceedings and matter in hand seeks impleadment to assist the FCC and also to seek clarification/modification/recall of the Nov 5, order to the extent that it suspends petitions challenging the proclamation/governor’s rule itself, and to plead that Article 245 cannot be used to oust jurisdiction of the high court to examine whether the preconditions for invoking Article 245 itself existed,” the application said.
