items.title: KGL Foundation commits $2m to maintain Mfantsipim’s Alex Dadey Sports Centre
items.description: The KGL Foundation has committed an additional $2 million towards the long-term maintenance of the Alex Dadey Sports Centre at Mfantsipim School, following its commissioning as part of the school’s 150th anniversary celebrations. The commitment, announced by the chairman of the anniversary celebration and KGL Group founder, Alex Apau Dadey, will provide the facility with an annual maintenance grant of $100,000 over the next 20 years. Speaking at the anniversary event, Mr Dadey said the funding was intended to ensure that the sports centre remained functional and continued to serve generations of students. He described the facility as an investment in sporting excellence and the school’s future, stressing that the value of infrastructure depended not only on its construction but also on how well it was maintained. “The true measure of infrastructure investment is not the grandeur of its commissioning, but the quality of its maintenance and the longevity of its service,” he said. The sports centre, funded through the KGL Foundation, is named after Mr Dadey’s late father, Dr Alex Dadey. Mr Dadey said the project held personal significance for him, recalling that he enrolled at Mfantsipim in September 1974 and that his years at the school helped shape his approach to leadership and personal development. “I once ran barefoot on the same grounds where the new sports facility now stands,” he said. Reflecting on the lessons he learnt through athletics, he said the discipline of sport had reinforced the importance of hard work and performance. “On the track, there were no shortcuts. At Mfantsipim, we were taught that the stopwatch does not recognise your family name, social standing, or excuses. It recognises performance,” he said. Mr Dadey also highlighted other educational projects undertaken by his family through the KGL Foundation. He said the family had recently commissioned the University of Ghana Alumni Centre, also named after his late father. He further announced that his wife, Caroline, would commission the Caroline Dadey ICT Centre at Aburi Girls’ Senior High School, where she is an alumna. The anniversary chairman urged Mfantsipim alumni to contribute to the school’s development and ensure that each generation leaves the institution stronger. “Every generation of old boys must leave Mfantsipim stronger than it found it,” he said. He also encouraged current students to prioritise character, discipline, curiosity and courage, rather than measuring achievement solely through wealth or social status. “Do not aspire to be successful men; aspire to be useful men,” he told the students. Looking ahead, Mr Dadey challenged the school community to begin considering the institution’s future as it approaches its bicentenary in 2076. “Let us honour the past, not live in it,” he said. Established in 1876 through the Methodist Church, Mfantsipim School is marking 150 years of education and service. Its anniversary celebration brought together the Vice-President, traditional authorities, including the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, religious leaders, government officials, school authorities, alumni and students.

items.title: Mfantsipim lessons shaped my leadership philosophy and business journey – KGL Group Chairman
items.description: Group Executive Chairman of the KGL Group of Companies, Alex Apau Dadey, says the values of discipline, resilience, consistency and perseverance instilled in him at Mfantsipim School have played a significant role in shaping his leadership philosophy and business journey. He said the lessons he acquired at the school had influenced his approach to building an African business conglomerate, particularly the importance of performance, innovation and determination in achieving success. Speaking at the Mfantsipim SESSIQUENTENNIAL Grand Durbar, Mr Dadey reflected on how his education at the institution prepared him for the demands of leadership and business. He said one of the enduring lessons from his school days was that success was determined not by family background or social standing, but by individual performance. “At Mfantsipim, we were taught that the stopwatch does not recognise your family name, social standing or excuses; it recognises performance,” he said. Mr Dadey explained that the principle had remained relevant throughout his professional life, noting that business leadership demanded the same commitment to results and excellence. He said his experience had taught him that building a successful enterprise required leaders to prepare thoroughly, innovate continuously and persevere despite challenges. “These lessons learnt in Mfantsipim helped shape my leadership philosophy and my journey in building an African business conglomerate,” he said. The KGL Group chairman further emphasised the importance of discipline and consistency, saying natural ability alone was insufficient to guarantee lasting success. According to him, while talent may provide an opportunity to compete, sustained effort and resilience determine whether an individual ultimately achieves distinction. “We were taught that talent may give you a place in the race, but discipline, resilience and consistency determine whether you become a champion,” he stated. Mr Dadey said the values acquired at Mfantsipim had remained central to his personal and professional development, describing his opportunity to support the school as a privilege. He said his contribution was an expression of gratitude to an institution that had helped shape his life and prepared him for the responsibilities he now carries. “So today, I have the privilege of giving back to an institution that helped in shaping my life,” he added. The KGL Foundation has committed an additional $2 million towards the long-term maintenance of the Alex Dadey Sports Centre at Mfantsipim School, following its commissioning as part of the school’s 150th anniversary celebrations. items.title: 2027: Why Atiku could win presidential election
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s 2027 presidential ambition is drawing attention amid growing discontent with the All Progressives Congress, APC, in Northern Nigeria, claims of a shift in the late President Muhammadu Buhari’s political support base and mounting public frustration over economic hardship. Read Also: * 2027: Why Tinubu may still win presidential election * 2027: Why Peter Obi could win presidential election Although President Bola Tinubu retains the advantages of incumbency and an extensive political structure, developments in the North, where Atiku has considerable political networks, could provide the former vice-president with an opportunity to mount a formidable challenge in the next presidential election. The emerging political calculations are being driven by Atiku’s renewed mobilisation efforts, claims of a possible realignment of Buhari’s political followers and the growing expectation that economic dissatisfaction could become a major factor in the 2027 contest. Atiku has placed considerable emphasis on Northern voter mobilisation, urging supporters in Sokoto to mobilise their families, friends and communities, turn out massively and protect their ballots. “I appeal to every one of you to come out, mobilise your families, your friends and all well-wishers. Vote massively, protect your vote, and make sure your vote is counted and announced,” he said. He warned that poor turnout could undermine the opposition’s numerical strength. “If you fail to turn out in large numbers, people will go from village to village buying voters’ cards to create the impression that we do not have as many supporters as those in the South,” he warned. The former vice-president’s emphasis on turnout reflects the importance of translating political support into actual votes, particularly in a region whose electoral strength could prove decisive in the next presidential contest. Northern calculations Adding another dimension to Atiku’s Northern calculations, former Minister of Sports and Youth Development, Solomon Dalung, an African Democratic Congress, ADC, chieftain who served under Buhari, claimed that the late president’s political following was shifting towards Atiku. Dalung linked the development to a reported visit by Buhari’s widow, Aisha, to the former vice-president. He described it as evidence of a political realignment. “The message she took for any politician to know is that the 12 million votes have been successfully transferred. We have had a phone call from the grave of Buhari that we should vote Atiku,” he said. He also expressed confidence that Atiku could defeat Tinubu, arguing that the former vice-president remained a formidable political contender despite the challenges facing his platform. “I am confident that as events are unfolding, Tinubu, even if he would take over the ADC secretariat and stop ADC from campaigning, cannot defeat Atiku Abubakar in 2027,” Dalung said. Although Dalung’s claim about the transfer of Buhari’s 12 million votes is a partisan political assertion rather than a verified movement of voters, it highlights the importance Atiku’s supporters attach to the late president’s political legacy and its possible implications for the 2027 election. Economic realities Beyond the Northern political calculations, economic hardship could provide another opening for the opposition. Rising living costs, food insecurity, unemployment and persistent insecurity have intensified public concerns about the direction of the country under the Tinubu administration. For Atiku, the opportunity lies in converting those grievances into electoral support through a convincing alternative on economic management, security and job creation. However, his ambition faces significant obstacles. The APC retains the advantages of incumbency, serving governors and established grassroots structures, while Atiku must rebuild his appeal beyond his traditional Northern support base, particularly in the South. There is also the unresolved legal uncertainty surrounding the ADC leadership and the implications of the Federal High Court judgment for the party’s political activities and candidates. Ultimately, the 2027 contest could test whether dissatisfaction with the Tinubu administration, combined with Atiku’s Northern political networks and the possible realignment of Buhari’s supporters, can translate into a broader national electoral challenge. items.title: Pakistan’s polio paradox
items.description: PAKISTAN’S latest polio case , a seven-month-old boy in Khyber district reported on Nov 6, is the ninth of 2026 and the seventh in Khyber Pakh­tun­khwa. It is another reminder of how elusive eradication has proved. After three decades of campa­i­gns, billions of dollars of international support , a field force of more than 400,000 workers, and the creation of one of the largest polio programmes in the world, the country has still not eliminated a pre­­ventable disease. Pakistan has not turned its abi­­lity to run campaigns into a system of public health protection that families trust, and that failure, which lies behind much of the refusal , is why the virus survives. The obstacles usually cited are real: insecurity, population movement, and difficult terrain keep teams from some children, while refusals, misinformation, and religious misconceptions keep others from being vaccinated. They do not account for the survival of the virus in communities that vaccination teams reach campaign after campaign and where families still turn the teams away. The reason lies beyond the vaccine, in the relationship between the state, its health institutions, and the communities they serve, and in whether those communities trust them. Political scientist Bo Rothstein has argued that trust in government depends on the quality and im­­partiality of public institutions: people trust ins­­titutions they experience as fair and reliable. Com­munication alone does not build trust, and a nati­onal health priority cannot command it. It grows out of people’s everyday experience of the state. The polio programme mobilises on a scale few public institutions in Pakistan can match. It deploys hundreds of thousands of vaccinators, maps households, monitors coverage, and returns repeatedly for the children who were missed. That capacity has saved many thousands of children from paralysis and remains essential to eradication. Beside that achievement stands the failure: the state’s ability to reach almost every household with polio drops has not become a working system of routine immunisation and basic healthcare. For many families, particularly in underserved parts of the country, the polio team may be one of the few regular points of contact with the state. A vaccinator arrives at the doorstep, sometimes several times a year, to administer polio drops. The same household may have no functioning health facility within reach, no routine childhood vaccines, no maternal care, and no clean drinking water. The state is visible when it wants to vaccinate a child, and often invisible when that child or family needs anything else. Pakistan’s polio programme has acknowledged that communities are using demand-based boycotts as a bargaining chip to draw attention to their problems. The contrast is sharpest in southern KP, where communities have boycotted polio campaigns to press the government on demands that have gone unanswered for years. Misinformation and religious opposition explain few of these boycotts. The British Medical Journal reported in December 2023 that tribal jirgas in southern KP had declared 677 boycotts during the year, with demands that ran from electricity, roads, and livelihoods to ref­u­­se collection. Pakistan’s own polio programme ack­nowledged that communities were using dem­and-based boycotts as a bargaining chip to draw attention to their problems. When a vaccination rou­­nd is the only occasion on which citizens can obtain ba­­sic services, the fault lies in the system of government as a whole. In some places a boycott is one of the few acts to which the government is compelled to respond, and communities have learnt as much. The frontline has weaknesses of its own. Too few female vaccinators and frequent changes of team members, with thin training for all of them, spoil the encounter at the door. Vaccinators do not always explain convincingly why a child needs repeated doses, least of all to parents who believe that earlier campaigns should have been enough, and programmes make too little use of trusted local figures who understand the concerns of families. Even a better trained and more persuasive team, though, cannot make up for the absence of reliable public services. Repeated visits can also do harm when families experience them as an imposition. For families who see little improvement in their lives, each arrival of a polio team can confirm that the state cares about one disease and one campaign, and little about the wellbeing of their children. The response is to make vaccination part of a broader and more consistent public health presen­­ce, by strengthening routine immunisation and pri­­mary healthcare. The outreach capacity the pol­io programme has built should find the children rou­­tine immunisation has missed and connect their families with regular health services. That takes trained health workers, reliable vaccine supplies, accessible facilities, and continuity of care, well beyond the occasional catch-up activities atta­ched to polio campaigns, so that immunisation beco­mes a regular function of the district health system. Behind this is the institutional separation between the polio programme and the wider health system. For years the National and Provincial Emergency Operations Centres have run as a well-funded parallel structure, answerable in large part to international donors, which mobilises large resources for campaign days while the provincial health departments beside them remain short of funds and bound by procedure. The dedicated funding, staffing, surveillance, and management arrangements that let the polio programme operate at scale belong inside the permanent health infrastructure of the provinces. Communities also need channels for their wider concerns, through local administration and elected representatives, and those channels have to work independently of vaccination campaigns. Otherwise the government teaches communities that withholding children from vaccination is an effective way to secure electricity, water, or roads. The responsibility rests with the Ministry of National Health Services, Regulations and Coordination, with the provincial governments, above all in KP, and with international donors, who should measure success by the strength of district health services as well as by the number of children reached in each round. Eradication depends on the campaigns, with better trained and more representative teams, and on what the campaigns cannot supply: a health system that protects children between rounds. When a vaccination team arrives at a door, the family should see it as part of a state that also protects their children and listens to them. Until that is so, Pakistan may go on running polio campaigns, and the conditions that make eradication so difficult will stay as they are. The writer is a strategic communication and public health professional, with experience across Asia, Africa and the Middle East. Published in Dawn, November 14th, 2026

items.title: Lekjaa : le projet de loi de finances, un document clair pour corriger les déséquilibres du passé
items.description: Fouzi Lekjaa, ministre de l’Économie et des Finances et de la Souveraineté numérique, a réaffirmé que le gouvernement actuel s’est donné pour mission de « changer de trajectoire afin de remédier au déséquilibre qui s’est accumulé au cours des étapes précédentes entre les dimensions économique et sociale ». Il a souligné que l’équité commande de reconnaître à la coalition actuelle le mérite d’avoir eu le courage « d’adopter des mesures et de mettre en œuvre des politiques qui redonnent toute sa place à la dimension sociale, dans un environnement international complexe ». Intervenant samedi lors d’une séance plénière de la Chambre des représentants, consacrée à la présentation de la réponse du gouvernement aux interventions des groupes et groupements parlementaires au sujet du projet de loi de finances n° 60.26, Lekjaa a indiqué que « la conjoncture mondiale évolue de plus en plus vers une contraction des capacités et des ressources, sous l’effet d’une instabilité généralisée qui rend incertaines les perspectives à moyen et à long termes ». Le ministre chargé des Finances au sein du gouvernement de Mansouri a expliqué que les manifestations de ces turbulences se font jour après jour, à travers les guerres en cours, les signes de crise que traverse le premier partenaire économique du Maroc, ainsi qu’une situation géopolitique mondiale ouverte aux scénarios les plus défavorables. Le responsable gouvernemental a estimé que le fait d’engager, dans un tel contexte, une refonte des fondements de l’État social, qui nécessite une augmentation importante des dépenses publiques, traduit « une conviction profonde quant à la nécessité de diagnostiquer la réalité et d’en anticiper les perspectives, ainsi qu’une foi profonde dans l’impératif de placer le citoyen au cœur des politiques publiques ». Lekjaa a insisté sur le fait que « cette transformation ne relève pas de simples discours ou de slogans autour de l’État social. Servir les intérêts du citoyen ne relève ni de la démagogie ni de la manipulation visant à gagner sa faveur, mais se traduit par des mesures concrètes qui permettront d’injecter plus de 350 milliards de dirhams sur la durée du mandat gouvernemental, répartis sur cinq ans, afin de soutenir le pouvoir d’achat des citoyens, d’améliorer leurs conditions de vie et de développer les services sociaux ». Le ministre a indiqué que, dès sa première année, le gouvernement a commencé à honorer cet engagement en consacrant 62 milliards de dirhams à la dimension sociale. Un effort qui, toutefois, n’a pas convaincu certaines composantes de la Chambre des représentants. « Certaines n’ont vu dans ces mesures aucun changement et les ont considérées comme une simple continuité des politiques sanctionnées par les urnes le 23 septembre dernier. D’autres ont estimé que le projet de loi de finances n’était qu’un ensemble de slogans, d’un côté, et une obsession des chiffres, de l’autre, réunissant ainsi une chose et son contraire » , a-t-il poursuivi. Il a considéré que ces jugements, ainsi que d’autres critiques, reviennent à qualifier prématurément le gouvernement d’échec, alors même qu’il n’avait pas encore achevé son premier mois d’exercice. Lekjaa a ajouté qu’un peu de patience et de recul, ainsi que l’attente de l’adoption du projet de loi de finances, auraient permis de prendre la mesure de nombreuses initiatives et décisions de gestion, qui viennent compléter une vision politique d’ensemble. Celle-ci encadre les différents domaines économiques, culturels et institutionnels et les inscrit dans une même dynamique incarnant le Maroc émergent, qui avance selon une vision de développement cohérente sur les plans social et territorial. Le ministre de l’Économie et des Finances s’est également arrêté sur l’articulation entre les dimensions économique et sociale dans le projet de loi de finances, en réponse aux critiques selon lesquelles celui-ci serait dépourvu de vision économique et ne constituerait qu’un document comptable. À cet égard, le responsable gouvernemental a affirmé que, au cours des dernières décennies, tous les projets de loi de finances ont été qualifiés de la sorte au sein du Parlement, alors même que l’économie nationale n’a cessé de croître et de se développer. Il a toutefois souligné que « cela ne dispense pas le gouvernement d’aborder cette question avec sérieux, d’écouter attentivement ces critiques et d’en tirer profit pour corriger les éventuelles erreurs ». Lekjaa a enfin souligné que « le gouvernement n’a aucun complexe à apprendre tout au long de son parcours ». Il s’est dit étonné que certaines critiques débouchent sur des propositions censées combler ce qui est présenté comme une absence de vision économique, alors que plusieurs de ces propositions figurent déjà dans le projet de loi de finances. Il a notamment cité la lutte contre les monopoles et la concentration, la garantie de la transparence et de la liberté de concurrence, ainsi que l’adoption de mesures visant, entre autres, à améliorer le climat des affaires. The post Lekjaa : le projet de loi de finances, un document clair pour corriger les déséquilibres du passé appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: ‘Truly beautiful’ to make football return, says Ronaldinho
items.description: Brazilian great Ronaldinho says it will be “truly beautiful” to make his return to the pitch on Sunday, 11 years after retirement, when he plays for Italian third-tier side Ravenna. The 46-year-old, who last played for Fluminense in 2015, will start for Ravenna in their local derby against Forli. “I want to have a great day. I’m happy to be here for the start of this wonderful story,” Ronaldinho told Sky Sports on Friday. “The president dreams of something big for Ravenna, and being a part of it makes me happy.” Ravenna president Ignazio Cipriani has said his goal is to take the club to Serie A for the first time in their history. The team’s Stadio Bruno Benelli, which usually holds 5,000 fans, is sold out, with a 1,800-capacity temporary stand — dubbed “R10” — also erected for the occasion. Ravenna, who have not even played in Serie B since 2008, are second in their group in Serie C, six points behind leaders Spezia. “Returning to the pitch after so much time is truly beautiful — I’m here to experience a special moment in my life,” added Ronaldinho. “It’s been a few years since I stopped playing — I’ve won everything I ever dreamed of. “Now I’m 46, and I’ve experienced everything there is to experience in football. This is a completely different kind of opportunity. I want to be part of the dream held by my friends who work for Ravenna.” The 2005 Ballon d’Or winner will be hoping to score his 300th career goal, over a decade after he netted his 299th. The former Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain star has even spent time in a Paraguayan prison since, after attempting to enter the country on a false passport, but did star in a prison futsal match. The move to Ravenna is widely regarded as a marketing stunt, but one Cipriani hopes can help kickstart his Serie A dream. “The long-term goal is to get Ravenna promoted to Serie A,” insisted the club president. The post ‘Truly beautiful’ to make football return, says Ronaldinho appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Des étudiants tunisiens inscrits dans des universités roumaines bloqués à Tunis
items.description: Des dizaines de jeunes étudiants tunisiens, officiellement admis au sein d’universités publiques en Roumanie pour l’année universitaire en cours, font face à une situation administrative critique. Les autorités des deux pays sont appelées à interagir pour débloquer une situation devenue dramatique pour ces jeunes et leurs familles. Bien qu’ils aient accompli l’intégralité des démarches réglementaires requises (obtention des arrêtés officiels d’acceptation aux études délivrés par le ministère roumain de l’Éducation, constitution de dossiers conformes et règlement intégral des frais de scolarité en devises auprès des établissements universitaires roumains), les visas de long séjour pour études (D/SD) demandés par ces étudiants sont toujours bloqués, leurs dossiers font l’objet d’un gel total et inexpliqué et leurs passeport nationaux physiquement retenus par l’ambassade de Roumanie à Tunis depuis plusieurs semaines, sans notification de décision, sans justification administrative et sans aucun délai de traitement communiqué. Alors que les cours ont déjà commencé dans les universités roumaines, ce blocage consulaire unilatéral engendre des conséquences dramatiques : la menace d'une radiation académique imminente, risquant de faire perdre une année entière d’études à des jeunes en règle ; un préjudice financier et moral considérable pour les familles ayant investi d’importantes ressources pour honorer les paiements universitaires en devises ; une atteinte caractérisée à la liberté de circulation, matérialisée par la rétention prolongée et sans base légale de documents d’identité officiels et souverains. Face à l’absence de réponse des services consulaires concernés, un appel urgent est adressé au ministère des Affaires étrangères, de la Migration et des Tunisiens à l’étranger, afin d’activer les canaux de la protection consulaire et d’intervenir rapidement auprès de la représentation diplomatique roumaine à Tunis pour exiger la restitution immédiate des passeports et le déblocage des dossiers. Les autorités et institutions roumaines compétentes sont appelées, pour leur part, à mettre fin à cette contradiction institutionnelle où des universités d’État valident et perçoivent les inscriptions d’étudiants étrangers tandis que leur consulat entrave l’accès au territoire. I. B. L’article Des étudiants tunisiens inscrits dans des universités roumaines bloqués à Tunis est apparu en premier sur Kapitalis .

items.title: I received N100m alert after APC campaign – Portable
items.description: Nigerian singer, Habeeb Okikiola, popularly known as Portable, has claimed that Ogun State All Progressive Congress governorship candidate, Senator Solomon Adeola, also known as Yayi, sent him N100m after he participated in campaign activities for the party. Portable made the claim in a video circulating on social media on Friday, where he expressed excitement over the alleged payment and thanked Adeola and another politician, IBD Dende. In the footage, the singer wore an APC-branded shirt and a cap bearing Yayi’s name, while displaying campaign materials featuring the senator. He explained that IBD Dende had earlier asked him to return home and promised to contact him, but some of his associates later informed him that the senator was looking for him. The singer said he initially doubted the information because of an earlier experience in which he was reportedly told that money had been sent to him, but he received nothing. “My dearest fans! I just woke up to an alert of N100m from Yayi! IBD Dende, oga mi! God bless you. Thank you! Yayi instructed them to send me the money. I took a nap, and God saved me from death,” he said. Portable added that he was initially suspicious when he heard that Adeola wanted to reach him. “Are you the one to tell me that Yayi is looking for me?’ I asked. They wanted to scam me, just as they did when Yayi sent money previously. I did not get a dime then,” he said. “Thank you, Lord! Yayi has sent N100m. Thank you, IBD Dende. May your children be glorious! May you live long, my daddy. It shall be well with you. N100m is not a small amount at all!” he added. The claim comes weeks after Portable publicly acknowledged receiving payments for taking part in APC campaign activities in support of President Bola Tinubu ahead of the 2027 general elections. items.title: Mineral wealth
items.description: PAKISTAN’S mineral wealth offers an opportunity to attract investment, earn foreign exchange and support long-term economic growth. But turning this potential into reality will require more than promises. At the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum 2026 , Deputy PM Ishaq Dar has promised predictable policies and institutional support to investors interested in the country’s mineral resources. Such assurances are welcome. However, investors will need more than that. The country’s experience with large mining projects has not always inspired confidence. The Reko Diq dispute remains an important reminder of what can happen when agreements and government commitments become contentious. We cannot afford another dispute that damages the country’s credibility. Policy consistency must therefore extend beyond individual governments. That said, mining rights must be awarded through transparent processes, with clear contractual obligations and effective regulatory oversight. Moreover, mineral development must benefit local populations. Communities should receive their share of employment, as well as better public services and improved infrastructure. Without local support, even commercially viable projects can falter. Additionally, Islamabad must avoid becoming merely a supplier of raw materials to the world. Exporting unprocessed minerals will bring some foreign exchange, but it will not deliver wider economic gains. The real opportunity lies in transfer of technology for refining minerals and producing finished goods locally. This would require investment in processing facilities and related industries. The aim must be to build an industrial base around mineral resources rather than simply dig them out and ship them abroad. The state should also resist the temptation to present minerals as a solution to Pakistan’s long-term economic difficulties. They can contribute significantly to sustainable growth and help diversify exports. But no country has ever developed on mineral wealth or exports alone. Natural resources can provide capital for development, but they cannot replace the hard work of building productive industries. Mineral wealth must become part of a wider industrialisation strategy. The country needs to raise productivity across manufacturing and agriculture, and develop products that can find markets abroad. Published in Dawn, November 14th, 2026

items.title: Journée mondiale du diabète : le Maroc mise sur le dépistage précoce
items.description: A l’occasion de la Journée mondiale du diabète, le ministère de la Santé et de la Protection sociale met l’accent cette année sur l’importance du diagnostic précoce et d’une prise en charge rapide, à travers le thème « Agir tôt contre le diabète pour préserver votre santé ». Au Maroc, le diabète touche environ 2,7 millions d’adultes, soit une prévalence de 10,6 % chez les personnes âgées de 18 ans et plus, selon les données de l’Enquête nationale sur les facteurs de risque communs des maladies non transmissibles 2017-2018. À cela s’ajoutent quelque 10,4 % d’adultes au stade du prédiabète. Le ministère alerte également sur le retard au diagnostic : près de la moitié des personnes diabétiques ignorent qu’elles sont atteintes de la maladie, ce qui augmente le risque de complications graves, notamment cardiovasculaires, rénales, oculaires et neurologiques. Maladie chronique souvent silencieuse, le diabète constitue l’une des principales causes de mortalité à l’échelle mondiale. Les estimations internationales les plus récentes font état de plus de 589 millions d’adultes vivant avec le diabète, un chiffre qui pourrait atteindre 853 millions d’ici 2050. Plus de quatre personnes sur dix ignoreraient par ailleurs leur maladie. Au Maroc, la pathologie représente également un coût important pour le système de santé. Les dépenses annuelles liées au diabète dépassaient 1,5 milliard de dirhams en 2021, selon les données de l’Agence nationale de l’assurance maladie, avec une progression annuelle moyenne supérieure à 10 %. Le diabète concerne également les plus jeunes : le ministère fait état de plus de 43.000 enfants atteints. Le dépistage précoce au cœur de la stratégie Face à cette situation, le ministère place la lutte contre le diabète parmi les priorités de ses plans sectoriels de santé. Un programme national a notamment été déployé à travers les établissements de soins de santé primaires et les structures territoriales. Ce dispositif repose sur plusieurs axes : sensibilisation et prévention, dépistage précoce, éducation thérapeutique et accompagnement des patients, ainsi que formation et renforcement des compétences des professionnels de santé. Le ministère insiste également sur le rôle de la prévention et de l’adoption de modes de vie sains, avec l’appui des médias pour renforcer l’information du public. Des signes d’alerte à ne pas négliger À l’occasion de cette journée, le ministère appelle les citoyens à rester attentifs aux principaux signes pouvant révéler un diabète : soif intense et persistante, mictions fréquentes, perte de poids inexpliquée, fatigue importante ou troubles de la vision. En cas d’apparition de ces symptômes, il recommande de consulter rapidement un médecin ou de se rendre dans l’établissement de santé le plus proche. À travers cette mobilisation, le ministère entend renforcer la prévention, améliorer la prise en charge des personnes diabétiques et favoriser un accès équitable à des soins de qualité et financièrement abordables. The post Journée mondiale du diabète : le Maroc mise sur le dépistage précoce appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Mahama, Akufo-Addo, Otumfuo expected at Agogo Manhene’s funeral
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama, former President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo and Asantehene Otumfuo Osei Tutu II are among prominent dignitaries expected at the final funeral rites of the late Agogomanhene, Nana Kwame Akuoko Sarpong. The three-day traditional funeral, known as Dotie Yie , will take place from November 24 to 26, 2026, at the Kyei and Ofori Krobron Stool Palace in Agogo in the Asante Akyem area. An announcement by the Agogo Traditional Council indicates that the funeral will bring together traditional rulers, political leaders, government officials, religious authorities, diplomats, security personnel and representatives of various institutions to pay their last respects to the late chief. The announcement was dated November 10, 2026, and signed by Nana Kwame Nti. The final day, Thursday, November 26, is expected to attract the country’s top political and traditional leadership, including the Asantehene, the President, former Presidents and Vice-Presidents, Ministers of State and other senior government officials. The programme, signed by the Krontihene of the Agogo Traditional Council, Nana Kwame Nti, outlines separate arrangements for groups expected to attend the three days of mourning. On Tuesday, November 24, the first day of the funeral, religious leaders, the Muslim community, churches, diplomats, members of the Council of State, political parties and officials of the Municipal Assembly are expected to attend. Heads of government departments, corporate institutions, non-governmental organisations, private unions, associations and members of the general public will also have the opportunity to pay their respects. Wednesday, November 25, will bring together traditional authorities from the National and Regional Houses of Chiefs, as well as security agencies and other state institutions. The Ghana Armed Forces, Ghana Police Service, Ghana National Fire Service, Customs Division of the Ghana Revenue Authority and Ghana Immigration Service are among those expected. State-owned enterprises, educational institutions and old students’ associations are also scheduled to participate. The final day’s observances will be attended by the Asantehene and other senior members of the Asante Kingdom, alongside the country’s political leadership and other invited dignitaries. The first two days will have morning sessions from 5 a.m. to 11 a.m. and afternoon sessions from 1 p.m. to 6 p.m. On Thursday, the morning session will run from 5 a.m. to 11 a.m., with the afternoon programme ending at 5 p.m. The Traditional Council said the funeral was an opportunity to celebrate the late chief’s years of service to Agogo, Asanteman and Ghana. It has urged dignitaries and other prospective attendees to make the necessary arrangements ahead of the event and directed that official RSVPs be submitted through designated representatives.

items.title: Amupitan’s resignation report false, misleading — INEC
items.description: By Ayobami Okerinde The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has refuted a social media report suggesting that its Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, is set to resign. The commission described the claim, which was shared alongside an image online, as fabricated and misleading. INEC made its position known on Saturday through a statement on its official X account, urging Nigerians to disregard the report and refrain from circulating unverified information. “The claim is FALSE, FABRICATED AND MISLEADING,” the commission stated. “Members of the public are urged to disregard the fabricated report, refrain from sharing unverified information and rely solely on INEC’s official communication channels for authentic information. “Stop the spread of fake news.” Recall Vanguard reported that Amupitan was confronted by protesters outside Chatham House on Thursday, calling for his resignation over alleged shortcomings in the voters’ register. The protesters surrounded his vehicle as he departed a discussion on Nigeria’s preparations for the 2027 elections, with some demanding that he step out to address their concerns. The post Amupitan’s resignation report false, misleading — INEC appeared first on Vanguard News .

Rapatriement des dépouilles des Sénégalais de l’Extérieur : un accord signé entre le Sénégal et la NSIA Vie Assurances
items.description: Une convention de partenariat visant à faciliter le rapatriement des dépouilles des Sénégalais de l’Extérieur, a été signée le vendredi 13 novembre 2026 entre le ministère de l’Intégration africaine, des Affaires étrangères et des Sénégalais de l’Extérieur et la compagnie NSIA Vie Assurances. Le ministère de l’Intégration africaine, des Affaires étrangères et des Sénégalais de l’extérieur et la compagnie NSIA Vie Assurances ont procédé, ce vendredi 13 novembre 2026, à la signature d’une convention de partenariat visant à faciliter le rapatriement des dépouilles des Sénégalais de l’extérieur. Cette importante initiative s’inscrit, selon un communiqué de la tutelle rendu public samedi, dans le cadre de la politique d’amélioration continue de l’assistance que le gouvernement apporte aux Sénégalais de la diaspora, y compris en cas de décès. « Dénommée »Sutura Diaspora », cette offre d’assurance rapatriement prévoit une prise en charge financière et logistique ainsi qu’une assistance juridique pour l’accomplissement des procédures et formalités requises, aussi bien dans le pays de survenance du décès qu’au Sénégal. Elle prévoit également une assistance financière à la famille éplorée », explique le document. A lire aussi : Consolidation du droit international: le Sénégal et la Cpi scellent les bases d’un nouveau partenariat Toutefois, le ministère précise que ce partenariat est ouvert à l’ensemble des prestataires d’assurances de droit sénégalais remplissant les conditions prévues par le cahier des charges. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Burkina: NutriSèn, 10 ans de combat contre les maladies par l’assiette
items.description: Créé en novembre 2016, NutriSèn, premier cabinet spécialisé en diététique et en nutrition formellement reconnu au Burkina Faso, a célébré son dixième anniversaire, le vendredi 13 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Une décenie d'engagement, d'accompagnement des patients et de sensibilisation aux bonnes habitudes alimentaires, que sa fondatrice, la diététicienne-nutritionniste Ida Zocli Nansi, entend prolonger avec de nouvelles ambitions. Dix ans au service de la santé, du bien-être et de la prévention. Le cabinet NutriSèn a marqué une étape importante de son histoire, le vendredi 13 novembre 2026, à l'occasion de la célébration de son dixième anniversaire. Dans une ambiance empreinte de convivialité et de fraternité, un cocktail organisé dans sa cour, à Somgandé, à Ouagadougou, a réuni patients, médecins, pharmaciens, partenaires et amis autour de sa fondatrice, Ida Zocli Nansi. Instant coupure de gâteau pour la célébration des 10 ans de NutriSèn Au-delà du caractère festif de la cérémonie, cette célébration a surtout été l'occasion de mesurer le chemin parcouru par cette structure spécialisée dans la diététique et la nutrition. Lancé en novembre 2016, NutriSèn s'est progressivement imposé dans le paysage sanitaire burkinabè comme une référence dans l'accompagnement nutritionnel, avec une approche fondée sur l'expertise, la rigueur professionnelle et la proximité avec les patients. En une décennie, le cabinet a élargi son rayonnement aux principales villes du Burkina Faso, tout en développant une présence auprès de la diaspora ouest-africaine. Son champ d'intervention couvre plusieurs catégories de populations, des enfants aux personnes âgées, en passant par les adolescents, les hommes, les femmes ainsi que les femmes enceintes et allaitantes. Dix ans après sa création, NutriSèn entend ainsi transformer une décennie de résultats en un nouveau chantier d'ambition. Sur le terrain, NutriSèn accompagne aussi bien les personnes désireuses de perdre du poids que celles qui souhaitent en prendre ou corriger des carences nutritionnelles. Le cabinet assure également un suivi diététique adapté aux personnes vivant avec des maladies chroniques, notamment le diabète, l'obésité, l'hypertension artérielle, la goutte, la stéatose hépatique, l'hypercholestérolémie et certains cancers. «NutriSèn a changé des vies» Pour Ida Zocli Nansi, ces dix années représentent bien plus qu'un anniversaire. Elles consacrent un engagement professionnel et humain dont les résultats se mesurent avant tout dans les transformations vécues par les patients. Ida Zocli Nansi, Fondatrice de NutriSèn «Nous pouvons le dire aujourd'hui, sans aucune prétention que par la grâce de Dieu, grâce à la confiance des professionnels de santé et à la prise de conscience des patients, NutriSèn a changé des vies», a-t-elle déclaré. Mais pour la fondatrice, l'enjeu ne consiste pas seulement à accompagner les personnes déjà confrontées à des problèmes de santé. Il s'agit surtout d'installer durablement une culture de la prévention dans les habitudes quotidiennes. Son appel est sans équivoque: «N'attendons pas d'avoir le dos au mur, que notre santé soit menacée ou déjà dégradée, pour faire des efforts. La prévention doit devenir un réflexe et non une réaction face à la maladie». Un message qui prend tout son sens au regard du constat ayant motivé la création du cabinet en 2016. À l'époque, la progression du surpoids, de l'obésité et des maladies chroniques liées à l'alimentation constituait déjà une préoccupation grandissante. Dix ans après, la situation demeure préoccupante. Ils étaient nombreux à l'occasion des 10 ans de NutriSèn pour témoigner leurs reconnaissances au cabinet pour son accompagnement Pour NutriSèn, plusieurs facteurs expliquent cette évolution: les prédispositions héréditaires, les mauvais choix alimentaires et les modes de vie contemporains, marqués notamment par le stress, la fatigue et la sédentarité. Des facteurs qui favorisent parfois le recours à la malbouffe, au tabac ou à l'alcool. Face à cette réalité, le cabinet a fait de l'information et de l'accompagnement ses deux principaux leviers d'action. Sa conviction: les mauvaises habitudes alimentaires résultent souvent d'un déficit d'information, mais aussi de la difficulté à transformer les connaissances en comportements durables. Dix ans de passion et de persévérance salués Marraine du cabinet, Dr Balkissa Sidikou Souna a salué le parcours accompli par NutriSèn et l'engagement de sa fondatrice. Elle a notamment mis en lumière la détermination nécessaire pour faire grandir une structure spécialisée dans un domaine aussi essentiel que la nutrition. Marraine du cabinet, Dr Balkissa Sidikou Souna «Dix années de passion, de persévérance, de travail et d'engagement: voilà ce que représente le parcours de NutriSèn. C'est une aventure qui mérite d'être saluée», a-t-elle souligné. Pour la marraine, cette première décennie ne doit cependant pas être considérée comme un aboutissement, mais comme un nouveau point de départ. «Dix ans constituent une belle étape, mais certainement pas une ligne d'arrivée. Je souhaite que NutriSèn poursuive son développement et demeure une référence dans le domaine de la nutrition et de la diététique au Burkina Faso», a-t-elle ajouté. Des témoignages qui parlent mieux que les chiffres L'une des séquences marquantes de la célébration a été consacrée aux témoignages de personnes ayant bénéficié de l'accompagnement du cabinet. Des expériences personnelles qui ont permis d'illustrer concrètement l'impact du suivi nutritionnel sur la santé et le bien-être. Parmi les témoins, Roland Nikiema, directeur général de Wendkouni Bank International (WBI), a partagé son expérience, mettant en avant les changements obtenus grâce aux conseils et à l'assistance de NutriSèn. En quelques mois de suivi, il affirme être sorti du stade de l'obésité. Roland Nikiema, directeur général de Wendkouni Bank International (WBI) «Grâce à l'accompagnement, aux conseils et au suivi de NutriSèn, j'ai pu obtenir des résultats concrets en quelques mois et sortir de l'obésité. Cette expérience m'a permis de prendre véritablement conscience de l'importance de la nutrition dans la préservation de ma santé», a-t-il témoigné. Dr Hortense Karambiri, également présente à la cérémonie, a pour sa part mis en avant l'importance de la régularité et de la qualité de l'accompagnement proposé par le cabinet. «L'accompagnement de NutriSèn va au-delà des simples recommandations alimentaires. C'est un suivi dans la durée, qui permet de mieux comprendre son corps, d'adopter de bonnes habitudes et d'améliorer durablement son bien-être», a-t-elle fait savoir. Dr Hortense Karambiri Ces témoignages ont donné une dimension particulièrement humaine à la célébration, rappelant que derrière les consultations et les programmes nutritionnels se trouvent des parcours de vie, des changements de comportement et des résultats qui peuvent transformer le quotidien. De nouvelles ambitions pour une deuxième décennie Pour les dix prochaines années, NutriSèn entend franchir un nouveau cap. La structure prévoit notamment de renforcer son équipe et d'élargir ses compétences afin d'améliorer davantage la qualité et l'efficacité de ses prestations. Le cabinet ambitionne également de consolider ses relations avec les professionnels de santé, de multiplier les partenariats avec les entreprises et les organisations pour développer l'éducation nutritionnelle en milieu professionnel, mais aussi de nouer de nouvelles collaborations avec les salles de sport et les restaurants. Les médias figurent également au cœur de cette stratégie. NutriSèn souhaite intensifier ses collaborations avec les organes de presse afin de porter plus largement ses messages de sensibilisation et d'éducation nutritionnelle auprès des populations. Cette volonté de vulgarisation n'est pas nouvelle. Au cours de ses dix premières années, le cabinet a déjà animé des conférences et des activités de sensibilisation dans plusieurs institutions et entreprises, notamment BOA, BSIC, Coris Bank, Total, l'Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS), l'ONEA et le ministère de l'Économie et des Finances. Il a également investi les médias nationaux à travers des émissions consacrées aux bonnes pratiques alimentaires. À travers ces initiatives, NutriSèn défend une vision: celle d'une société où hommes, femmes et enfants jouissent d'une meilleure santé grâce à une alimentation équilibrée et à un mode de vie sain. Dix ans après sa création, NutriSèn entend ainsi transformer une décennie de résultats en un nouveau chantier d'ambition. Car, au-delà des anniversaires et des distinctions, le véritable défi reste celui de faire de la bonne nutrition une culture, de la prévention un réflexe et de la santé une responsabilité partagée. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Burkina: NutriSèn, 10 ans de combat contre les maladies par l'assiette est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Here are some quality product displays at the Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 – Don’t miss out
items.description: The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 opened at GHUD Park, Accra Mall, bringing together an impressive collection of Ghanaian businesses, established brands, entrepreneurs and service providers for a three-day celebration of enterprise, innovation and commerce. With an extensive range of products and services on display, patrons have plenty of reasons to make their way to the exhibition grounds before the fair ends on Sunday, November 15. From delicious local delicacies and refreshing beverages to fashionable clothing, beauty products, technology, household essentials and financial services, the exhibition offers visitors an exciting opportunity to discover quality products, meet business owners and shop directly from participating brands. A marketplace bursting with flavour and innovation Food lovers are particularly well catered for, with exhibitors presenting an exciting selection of locally produced and processed products. Among them are Wilmar Africa, showcasing its Fortune Spread brand; Kivo; Didi Shito; Corki Ventures, with its spices; Adjoor Ventures, specialising in tuna distribution; Manellah Foods, known for cereal production; and Gold Coast Foods, presenting Sankofa Spices. Other food and beverage exhibitors include Yaapee Royal Foods, NutriSmart Ventures, Golden Parani Company Limited, Golden Pride (Yao Consult), G-Way Investments Africa Limited, Ikam Plus Company Limited, Desco Limited, Golden Parani Company Limited and ESBONY Food Package. Visitors can also explore natural and refreshing beverage options from Koa Impact Commerce, with its natural cocoa juice; Spring Board (Delsoy Ltd), showcasing soy milk; Spring Board (Orave Juices), with fruit juice; Pinnacle Coco Limited, offering coconut juice; Jussvina Drinks (Global 500); Green Cup, with its beetroot, guava and pawpaw tea; and Myst Natural Water. The culinary experience extends to Flourish Foods Africa’s grilled chicken and poultry products, MamsiJoy Ventures’ rice, Ellie’s Catering Services’ fufu, Martha’s Yam Trading, Farm Mate’s fresh tomatoes, Orrab Farms’ fresh produce, T&C Farms’ animal production and Atohfield’s crop and animal farming. Aladdin Bakery, 97 Bakes, Evive Delight Ltd, Bliss Pop, Selis Satisfactory and Golden Coast Foods add even more variety to the food offerings, with products ranging from baked treats and popcorn to kenkey and other processed foods. BB Brothers also brings its canned wine offering to the exhibition. Fashion, beauty and lifestyle take centre stage Fashion enthusiasts will find plenty to explore, with a diverse collection of clothing, accessories, footwear and personal-care products. Haute Xklusive, La Robe Classique, Kims Foods and Clothings, JAT Couture, Kofikyere KloTHING, Utonez Clothier and Regy Couture Ltd are among the brands presenting fashion options. Asangenta adds dresses, bags and hats to the mix, while Shoes TE3 caters for different footwear needs and sizes. Kinky Love Crochet brings its hair and wig offerings to the exhibition, complementing the wider lifestyle display. Beauty and personal-care enthusiasts can discover products from Haus of Lush, RNS Beauty, Atlast Prime Merchantile Ltd, Leepoku Ventures and Chocho. Mist and Strands also presents bath and body products, while Reed Diffusers Ghana Ltd adds scented home accessories to the experience. LIZ Imports showcases perfumes and home appliances, while Kemz Ceramics brings ceramics to the exhibition. Eldem Floral Services adds colour and elegance with fresh-cut flowers. Technology, business solutions and essential services Beyond consumer products, the fair provides a valuable opportunity to discover businesses using technology and innovation to address everyday challenges. Solid Connect is showcasing its application for artisans, while Greenhaul Solutions presents waste-management and scrap-procurement services. We Shop Africa and Ayuda bring e-commerce solutions into focus, while Katon 360 Technologies showcases a digital platform designed for SMEs. Technology enthusiasts can also visit Galop Sea Limited for laptops and accessories, Xfromo Hypermart for phones and accessories, including Google Pixel phones, and Vital Vendors for car essentials. Financial and institutional services are equally represented. Ecobank showcases banking services, while GLICO Life presents insurance solutions. MTN brings telecommunications and connectivity services to the exhibition. DBS showcases housing and roofing solutions, Sintex Tank presents water-storage products, and Vaal Real Estate offers real estate opportunities. GEPA also provides an important export-sector presence, connecting the exhibition to Ghana’s wider ambition of promoting locally made products and businesses. Other exhibitors include Worafam Group of Companies, showcasing safety wear; MGIG Suppliers, with powdered soap; BB Chemist, presenting Relax Liver Salt; Prestige Children’s Palace and Roses Enterprise and Mothercare, offering mother-care products; and Central University, representing the education sector. Travel and hospitality services are also represented by Grandeur Consult Travel and Tour and Astolinks, while Gorgeous Vie Event Hub showcases events and décor services. Afram Publication brings books to the exhibition, and Advantage GH Premium Apparel presents printing services. An opportunity patrons should not miss The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair goes beyond the traditional shopping experience. It creates an environment where businesses can interact directly with consumers, build brand awareness, generate sales and establish valuable commercial relationships. The initiative builds on JoyBusiness’s longstanding engagement with Ghanaian small and medium-sized enterprises, particularly the need to improve access to markets, financing, technology and business development opportunities. For patrons, it is an opportunity to discover emerging Ghanaian brands, compare products, make purchases and support businesses contributing to the country’s entrepreneurial landscape. With Saturday and Sunday still to come, the public is encouraged not to miss the remaining days of the fair. Whether you are searching for your next favourite food brand, refreshing your wardrobe, exploring beauty products, looking for technology solutions or simply interested in supporting Ghanaian businesses, there is something worth discovering at GHUD Park, Accra Mall. The Ecobank JoyBusiness SME Fair 2026 continues until Sunday, November 15. items.title: Hong Kong rail giant warns of cash crunch despite Northern Metropolis land grant
items.description: Hong Kong’s MTR Corporation has warned that it will face significant cash flow pressures over the next few years, even with the government’s grant of eight new sites for developing the Northern Link rail project in the Northern Metropolis. The warning came as the Liber Research Community cast doubt on the MTR Corp’s model of using property developments to fund rail construction, pointing out that about a third of the 18 sites granted in total were idle plots where developers had opted for cash...

items.title: Diphtheria: MSF warns of treatment shortages as Nigeria records over 1,100 deaths
items.description: MSF warns that shortages of diphtheria antitoxin are forcing medical teams to ration treatment in northern Nigeria. Fresh figures put the country's 2026 death toll at 1,126, while 70 of 86 patients managed by MSF teams in Katsina over 18 days had severe infections. The post Diphtheria: MSF warns of treatment shortages as Nigeria records over 1,100 deaths appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .

items.title: Disqualified NDC National Youth Organizer aspirant rules out appeal
items.description: A disqualified aspirant in the National Democratic Congress (NDC) National Youth Organiser race, Steven Nhyira Odarteifio, has ruled out challenging the party’s decision to disqualify him from the contest. He said he would neither protest the decision nor pursue an appeal, choosing instead to remain neutral as the party prepares to elect a new National Youth Organiser. In a statement following the conclusion of the party’s vetting process, Mr Odarteifio expressed disappointment with the outcome but thanked the NDC for giving him the opportunity to present his vision for the youth wing and young people across the country. He also congratulated the two candidates who survived the vetting and wished them well in the contest. Mr Odarteifio said he hoped the candidates would put their differences aside after the election and work together to strengthen the party’s youth wing. “I have decided to remain neutral in this contest, and I stand ready to support whoever wins,” he said. He reaffirmed his commitment to youth development and agricultural transformation, saying he would continue to advocate policies and initiatives that improve opportunities for young people and help the party fulfil its promises to them. The former aspirant also expressed gratitude to his sponsors, campaign volunteers and supporters for their contributions throughout his bid for the position.

items.title: Drug trafficking isn’t a political problem; it’s an institutional one – Senyo Hosi
items.description: Convener of the OneGhana Movement and Trustee of the Ghana Coalition Against Galamsey, Senyo Hosi, has described drug trafficking in Ghana as an institutional problem, calling for stronger enforcement systems, greater accountability and adequate resources for the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC). Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 14, he argued that the country’s fight against drugs must move beyond political debates to address weaknesses within institutions responsible for border security and law enforcement. Mr Hosi acknowledged improvements in NACOC’s operations, particularly the expansion of its presence from approximately eight districts to 81, but maintained that the Commission remained significantly under-resourced. Although he commended efforts to improve the institution’s capacity through training and equipment, he insisted that more investment was needed to enable it to effectively tackle drug trafficking. Mr Hosi also warned against limiting Ghana’s drug problem to cocaine, arguing that synthetic substances posed a serious threat to young people. “The drug problem should not be made a cocaine problem at all. The bigger problem we have is with the synthetics. Serious problem. That’s what our youth are getting into,” he said. Beyond NACOC’s capacity, Mr Hosi raised concerns about the effectiveness of cargo scanning systems at Ghana’s ports, questioning how cocaine consignments could pass through without detection. He called for investigations into the operations of port scanners, their maintenance and the role of Customs officers responsible for inspecting containers. He also questioned reports that some scanners frequently broke down, although he said he could not independently verify the information. For him, such concerns point to deeper institutional weaknesses that must be investigated rather than turned into political blame games. “It’s no more a political problem. It’s a whole institutional problem,” he stressed. He also expressed disappointment that the drug menace had not received sufficient attention in the government’s budget, urging authorities to prioritise funding for NACOC, just as they had highlighted the fight against illegal small-scale mining, popularly known as galamsey. He warned that Ghana must treat drug trafficking and substance abuse as major national concerns, particularly given the growing exposure of young people to illicit substances. He added that strengthening enforcement institutions, improving border surveillance, and holding those responsible for trafficking networks accountable were essential to addressing the problem.
