items.title: 10 Questions to Determine Whether Your Partner Is a Spy
items.description: Since Jensen Huang stepped down as the CEO of Nvidia amid revelations of his affair with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, the whole internet has been consumed with terror. If this can happen to Jensen Huang, the seemingly happily married, leather-jacket-clad leader of the Most Valuable Chip Company in the World, it can happen to anyone! Can’t it? Fortunately, I have devised a quiz. Ask your partner some simple questions and gauge their responses to determine whether or not you are being honeypotted. (1) What should we do tonight? a. What if I told you some fun facts about an interest we do not share and then we went to bed early? b. Whatever you want to do, babe! c. How about we [ unprintable ] on a pile of your favorite chips and then we send them all over the globe, randomly? Definitely to China, though. d. Let’s go down to the waterfront and eat some bread! (2) Would you still love me if I were a worm? a. Probably not. But as a worm, you would lack the higher brain functions to find this fact disappointing, and we would part ways amicably. b. You bet, babe! c. If as a worm you still had access to proprietary information about CPUs. d. I WOULD LOVE YOU MORE THAN ANYTHING! I WOULD DEVOUR YOU. (3) Are there any secrets you haven’t told me? a. Probably? b. Babe, I tell you everything! c. No! But I like the idea of sharing secrets! Do you have any secrets you want to tell me? d. I have a cloaca. (4) How did we meet? a. Why are you asking me this? You were there. I have to get up in the morning. b. Love at first sight, babe! c. The classic way. You were signing a woman’s chest . I was there for normal business reasons. d. At the park, by the waterfront. You had bread. (5) Do you want to come with me on my official trip to China with President Trump? a. No. b. Only if you want me there, babe! c. ( Sexily ) Yes d. Ordinarily I would love to, but I have to sit on these eggs. (6) What do you love most about me? a. Why are you asking me all of these questions? Is this one of those memes about being a spy? b. Everything about you! c. How good you look in your leather jacket! d. When you have bread in your pocket. (7) If I weren’t the billionaire CEO of a wildly successful company that makes a restricted chip, would you still love me? a. Well, you aren’t, and I do! b. You bet, babe! c. Obviously, but I do think it’s really, really cool that you are! But obviously I would. Although we probably wouldn’t have met if you weren’t! But obviously I would. d. Yes, if you still had access to bread. (8) Talk dirty to me. a. I took the trash out already so we can go to bed early. b. ( Growls .) c. Baby, this bra must be a restriction on the export of sensitive high-tech goods, and you must be the Commerce Department, because I want you to Take! It! Off! d. ( Quacks .) (9) What frightens you? a. Losing the people I love; having a bug fly into my mouth. b. Spending even a second without you, babe! c. The Commerce Department’s export-control list. d. LOUD NOISE! DON’T KNOW WHAT IT WAS! SOUNDED LIKE A PREDATOR. (10) What’s something you wish I would do for you? a. Watch even a single Hallmark movie voluntarily. b. Just be yourself, babe! c. Complete this multifactor authentication. d. Help me get my long, beautiful neck out of this bag of chips. Answer Key: Mostly A’s : Your partner is likely not a spy. Mostly B’s : Your partner could be a spy; more info needed. Mostly C’s : Your partner is almost certainly a spy. Mostly D’s : Your partner is a duck.

items.title: What the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier Means to Its Guards
items.description: I n the autumn of 1921 , the U.S. Army faced a difficult choice. Among four identical, flag-draped caskets—each containing the unidentified remains of an American soldier killed in World War I—only one would be laid to rest at the new Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery. It seemed only appropriate that an experienced commissioned officer ought to make the selection. All four men had died in the war and been buried at American cemeteries in France. But when word came that the French military had asked an enlisted man to pick France’s Unknown Soldier, the Americans quickly determined that they would not be one-upped by French egalitarianism on that day. That is how the selection came to be made by Edward Younger, a 23-year-old sergeant and one of the pallbearers who had carried the four caskets under consideration. Younger had survived being knocked unconscious by a shell and later being shot through the left thigh during vicious fighting in World War I. But he later wrote that being told to make this choice, standing alone with the four coffins, left him overwhelmed and numb. “Maybe these buddies had once been my pals,” Younger wrote in This Week , a syndicated magazine supplement, 15 years later. “Perhaps one of them had fought with me, had befriended me, had possibly shielded me from a bullet that might have put me in his place. Who would even know?” Younger left roses on the second casket to his right and reported that his duty was complete. The Unknown Soldier traveled that night by train to Paris and westward the following day to Le Havre, where his casket was carried aboard the USS Olympia en route for Arlington. The Unknown Soldier was buried under a marble slab atop a hill overlooking the nation’s capital from across the Potomac River. Among thousands of those who died in the Civil War , the Spanish-American War, World War I, and other conflicts, Younger’s choice offered a place to mourn for every parent whose child never returned home from battle. The tomb soon became a destination for tens of thousands of visitors to pay their respects to America’s war dead. In 1926, military guards were posted to discourage visitors from climbing or stepping on it. The large marble monument familiar to anyone on today’s tours was completed in 1932, and the watch became a 24-hour duty in 1937. Like Younger, the guards today belong to an infantry unit. Also like Younger, Thomas Iglesias, a specialist, was almost certainly not expecting to become famous just by showing up for work. On Wednesday, Veterans Day, senior officials gathered for the annual observance. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth , his wife, and three of his top advisers posed for photographs near the tomb. But, as they departed, the group began talking and someone laughed. Iglesias paused, then did his job. “All visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times!” Iglesias shouted. A CNN camera captured the moment. Warnings aren’t unusual at the tomb. A 2022 Army article quotes a tomb guard saying that sentinels issue two or three of them a day, usually to oblivious tourists. It’s another thing entirely to admonish Hegseth and his entourage. Hegseth’s detractors quickly scolded him for the group’s misbehavior or lauded the young specialist for correcting the behavior of a man who has regularly disparaged members of his department for lack of decorum, be they “fat” generals or bearded soldiers. Others, on Hegseth’s side, chided the soldier for failing to show proper respect to his boss. Hegseth, at least in this moment, chose not to pick a fight. His press office affirmed the warning as appropriate, and Hegseth awarded Iglesias the Joint Service Commendation Medal. I didn’t read any grand motive into Iglesias’s assertive correction of Pentagon leadership, because I’ve witnessed the devotion of the tomb guards many times. In October 2021, I traveled to the town where Younger had made his choice 100 years before, since renamed Châlons-en-Champagne. Active-duty tomb guards, all part of the 3rd Infantry Regiment “Old Guard,” were there with former soldiers who belonged to the Society of the Honor Guard, Tomb of the Unknown Soldier. They had joined a 10-day pilgrimage across France. They gathered in a broad town square, where French and American flags adorned the way to the neoclassical city hall, completed, as it happens, in 1776. Gavin McIlvenna, the society’s president at the time, spoke with me just outside , while visitors filed in to pay their respects in the room where Younger once stood. “I don’t know how many times I can say this is overwhelming. But it is,” McIlvenna said. I appreciated his passion for the moment. I also didn’t totally get it at the time. I initially saw their jobs as honorable but tedious. Walk 21 steps, turn and face the tomb for 21 seconds more. Turn again, shift the rifle to the outside shoulder, count another 21 seconds and walk. During visiting hours, repeat for 30 minutes in the warmer months and an hour in the colder months. After the cemetery closes, each watch lasts two hours. During a 24-hour shift, guards alternate time on the plaza with rest and preparation for their next watch. If the weather is miserable, that’s part of the mission. [ From the November 2023 issue: The patriot ] If any of the tomb guards in France that week ever saw their duty as I once did, they never let on. The Old Guard soldiers spend an average of 18 months at the tomb. Standing watch on a busy day means inspecting your surroundings, keeping your rifle at the correct angle, and maintaining a steady walk. There is no casual conversation, so guards communicate through scrapes and clicks of the steel plates attached to their shoes. A sentinel scrapes a heel to acknowledge veterans and distinguished guests or strikes the plates together on the inside of his heels to signal to another guard. The same standards of behavior apply once visitors leave the cemetery for the night, though the solitude provides plenty of time for the soldiers’ introspection. Several sentinels told me that, during the watch, they think about the tomb and all those it honors. An Unknown Soldier has no backstory to limit what others see in him. On those walks in the darkness, he can embody the courage and selflessness of combat or a remembrance of loved ones the guards have lost in their own lives. Many tomb guards have deployed to Iraq or Afghanistan, while others served as far back as the Vietnam War. Some are never far from friends buried in other sections of the cemetery. In France, shared devotion brought together guards whose service spanned generations. From Châlons-en-Champagne, they traveled to Paris with other military organizations for a ceremony under the Arc de Triomphe, followed by dinner at the École Militaire. At dinner, they lived it up and mostly kept the conversation light, while accommodating my interest in their jobs. I remember the look in the eyes of one former tomb guard when he talked about his service. I began to understand that every moment on that walk, and every little detail performed with precision, was an expression of gratitude for a debt that will never be fully repaid. And so it continues, uninterrupted. [ Read: The inside story of what happened at Stars and Stripes ] T he World War I Unknown Soldier would later be joined by unidentified service members from World War II and the Korean War, buried in separate crypts beside his tomb. But scientific advances have made future unknown burials very unlikely in the U.S. armed forces. In 1998, the Vietnam Unknown was identified as First Lieutenant Michael J. Blassie, an Air Force pilot shot down in 1972. The Vietnam Unknown’s crypt has been kept empty since Blassie’s remains were exhumed. DNA-based evidence can restore a fallen soldier’s identity. But people still have to choose to remember them. Edward Younger never forgot the Unknown Soldier he picked. He traveled to Arlington in 1930, telling The Washington Post that it was “real nice to get a chance to visit him again.” Twelve years later, Younger himself was laid to rest at the national cemetery. Younger described himself and his comrades as just “good, average soldiers.” He always imagined the man in the tomb to be a lot like him. That’s why the unidentified man in that tomb is paradoxically so easy to identify with. Few of us will be remembered by name for long. But what good, average people accomplish can outlast the memory of any one of them.

items.title: Psychoanalyzing a Megalomaniac
items.description: I n the spring of 1943, Walter C. Langer, a psychoanalyst at Harvard, received a query from William J. Donovan, the head of the U.S. government’s Office of Strategic Services, the covert-operations predecessor to the CIA. Donovan was interested in commissioning Langer to prepare a psychological profile of Adolf Hitler. “What we need is a realistic appraisal of the German situation,” Donovan told Langer. “If Hitler is running the show, what kind of a person is he? What are his ambitions? How does he appear to the German people? What is he like with his associates?” The OSS chief wanted to understand Hitler’s “psychological make-up—the things that make him tick.” Donovan was especially keen to know how Hitler might respond to increasing adversity. Hitler was used to winning. From 1933 to 1943, the Nazi leader had marched from one stunning political and military triumph to the next, securing the chancellorship, crushing the German constitutional order, annexing Austria, dismembering Czechoslovakia, and then invading Poland, France, Belgium, the Netherlands, Denmark, countries across North Africa, and Russia. Until 1943, Hitler had seemed to be an inexorable political and military force, smashing constitutional guardrails, shredding international treaties, breaking trade alliances, upending the international order, and ultimately plunging the entire world into war. But then came military reversals that stopped Hitler in his tracks: El Alamein, in November 1942, then Stalingrad, in January 1943. Donovan wanted to know how Hitler would react—militarily, politically, personally—if the tides of war began to change. “Do you suppose you could come up with something along these lines?” Donovan asked Langer. This was the first time the U.S. government would commission a psychological profile of a foreign leader to determine his possible future courses of action. Donovan was not interested in an academic study. Rather, he wanted a “realistic appraisal” that might provide actionable intelligence about what the führer might do next. [ Read: Hitler could have been stopped ] Langer engaged three fellow psychoanalysts—one from Harvard, one from the New School for Social Research, and one of the New York Psychoanalytic Institute—and set to work. He immersed himself in Hitler’s speeches and writings. He read both volumes of Mein Kampf front to back. He collected newspaper clippings and magazine articles. He interviewed former Hitler associates who had broken with the Nazi leader and were now living in exile. “The world has come to know Adolph Hitler for his insatiable greed for power, his ruthlessness, cruelty and utter lack of feeling, his contempt for established institutions and his lack of moral restraints,” Langer wrote in framing the scope of his work. “In the course of relatively few years he has contrived to usurp such tremendous power that a few veiled threats, accusations or insinuations were enough to make the world tremble.” It was only when the world wearied of Hitler’s threats and bluster, “and concluded that it was all a bluff,” Langer wrote, that the Nazi leader had “initiated the most brutal and devastating war in history.” Hitler was a man, Langer was told repeatedly, with an insatiable ego who needed to be the center of attention, always, everywhere. Hitler saw himself as the ultimate authority in all matters regardless of their import or insignificance. “It makes little difference whether the field be economics, education, foreign affairs, propaganda, movies, music or women’s dress,” Langer reported. “In each and every field he believes himself to be an unquestioned authority.” One former Hitler associate described to Langer what had happened when he tried to correct the Nazi leader about something. “I cannot be mistaken,” Hitler said. “What I do and say is historical.” Langer attributed this “infantile thinking” to an arrested emotional development that also resulted in frequent tantrums, both in private and public. Langer heard repeated stories about Hitler’s unbridled rages against his staff. Otto Strasser, an early Nazi Party member who had broken with Hitler over economic policy, told Langer that Hitler regularly browbeat members of his inner circle. “Rage and abuse became the favorite weapons in his armory,” Langer wrote, along with public degradation, humiliation, and, occasionally, murder. Strasser’s brother Gregor Strasser, another Nazi Party member who had also broken with Hitler over policy matters, was killed on the Night of the Long Knives. “Some of his closest associates have felt that he induces these rages consciously to frighten those around him,” Langer wrote. Hermann Rauschning, another early Nazi Party official, told Langer that some of Hitler’s “well-timed fits of rage” were intended to throw his entourage into confusion and submission. Langer reported that Hitler used a social gathering attended by his propaganda minister, Joseph Goebbels, and his Luftwaffe chief, Hermann Göring, to disparage both with juvenile humor. “You all know what a volt is and an ampere, don’t you?” Hitler said to the assembled crowd. “But do you know what a goebbels, a goering are? A goebbels is the amount of nonsense a man speaks in an hour and a goering is the amount of metal that can be pinned on a man’s breast.” Langer observed that Hitler used radio and rallies to spew lies and hatred, in order to manipulate public opinion. “Hitler’s speaking has been aptly described as a ‘verbal diarrhea,’” Langer wrote, and he reported that Rauschning had compared a Hitler speech to “an oral enema.” Langer also heard much about Hitler’s obsession with women. “Hitler likes to be surrounded with pretty women and usually requests the moving picture companies to send over a number of actresses whenever there is a party in the Chancellory,” Langer wrote, supporting this with an Associated Press photograph of Hitler surrounded by young film stars. Langer also cited unverified accounts of Hitler’s sexual proclivities and capacities, ranging from impotence to homosexuality to myriad perversions. Hitler, Langer wrote, “derives sexual gratification from the act of having a woman urinate or defecate on him.” Although this was likely not the kind of “actionable intelligence” that the OSS chief had been seeking, Langer, schooled in Freudian psychology, devoted much of his report to psychoanalysis of the Nazi leader. “Hitler’s outstanding defense mechanism is one commonly called projection,” Langer wrote. “It is a technique by which the ego of an individual defends itself against unpleasant impulses, tendencies or characteristics by denying their existence in himself while he attributes them to others.” As evidence, Langer noted that Hitler accused his political opponents of the “bombardment of lies” that Hitler himself assailed them with. Hitler’s hatred of the Jews, Langer theorized, emanated from hatred of himself: Hitler’s “own personal problems and conflicts were transferred from within himself to the external world where they assumed the proportions of racial and national conflicts.” Langer attributed Hitler’s rages, hatreds, obsessions, and delusions to an unhappy childhood with a brutish father and an emotionally battered but loving mother. Langer also spent considerable time analyzing Hitler’s preoccupation with architectural projects—in particular, the Eagle’s Nest, outside Berchtesgaden, Germany. “First there is a long hard road, then a heavily guarded entrance, a trip through a long tunnel to an extremely inaccessible place. There one can be alone, safe and undisturbed, and revel in the joys that Mother Nature bestows,” Langer wrote. “From a symbolic point of view one can easily imagine that this is a materialization of a child’s conception of the return to the womb.” B y October 1943, when Langer’s report was rushed to completion at Donovan’s insistence, Hitler was on his back heel but hardly finished. London was being pummelled. Rumors of a Wunderwaffe , a “miracle weapon,” that could change the course of the war proliferated. German physicists, led by Werner Heisenberg, were at work on an atomic bomb. Göring had already developed a prototype for a delivery mechanism—the Messerschmitt Me 264, dubbed the “Amerika Bomber”—and Manhattan was its first target. Hitler “described the skyscrapers being turned into gigantic burning torches, collapsing upon one another, the glow of the exploding city illuminating the dark sky,” Hitler’s armament minister, Albert Speer, recalled. “With such range we could repay America a thousandfold for the destruction of our cities.” Not until the final three pages of his long report did Langer provide the “realistic appraisal” of Hitler’s potential courses of action that Donovan had been seeking. Based on his interviews and his review of 11,000 pages of source materials, Langer discerned scenarios for Hitler’s possible reactions were he to face ultimate defeat. Langer thought it unlikely that Hitler would try to escape to another country, as dictators were known to do—because “nothing would break the myth” of Hitler as a great leader more assuredly than running away. [ Read: Trump: ‘I need the kind of generals that Hitler had’ ] Although Langer doubted that Hitler would allow himself to fall into the hands of the Allies, he did not rule out the possibility that the führer’s warped personality could welcome such an outcome, citing the case of a 16th-century religious fanatic who, when his theocratic cult was disbanded, asked to be paraded around in a cage. “In Hitler’s case such an outcome seems remote,” Langer wrote, “but it is difficult to estimate the extent to which an extreme masochist will go in order to gratify these tendencies.” Langer did think it possible that Hitler would sacrifice himself in combat. “When he is convinced that he cannot win, he may lead his troops into battle and expose himself as the fearless and fanatical leader,” Langer wrote. But it was equally likely, Langer concluded, that Hitler would suffer a complete nervous breakdown. “Hitler has many characteristics which border on the schizophrenic,” Langer continued. “This would not be an undesirable eventuality from our point of view since it would do much to undermine the Hitler legend.” Langer presciently posited suicide as the most likely scenario. He knew that Hitler had always been a man whose “infantile thinking” drove him to extremes and blinded him to compromise. Hitler sacrificed an entire army at Stalingrad, and his entire Afrika Korps in Tunisia. Langer cited Hitler’s fatalistic fanaticism verbatim: “We shall not capitulate … no, never. We may be destroyed, but if we are, we shall drag a world with us … a world in flames.” If anything, Langer suggested, the worse things got for Hitler, the more intransigent he would become. “He will fight as long as he can with any weapon or technique that can be conjured up to meet the emergency,” Langer concluded. “The course he will follow will almost certainly be the one that seems to him to be the surest road to immortality and that at the same time wreaks the greatest vengeance on a world he despises.” It is fortunate that Hitler never had access to a nuclear button.

items.description: About 200 unarmed police officers have arrived at the Nalerigu Senior High School, the venue for the National Democratic Congress (NDC) Regional executive election ahead of the polls. A total of 231 delegates are expected to participate in the regional election. The officers assembled at the election grounds on Saturday, November 14, as part of security arrangements to ensure a peaceful electoral process. The Police explained that the presence of the officers was intended to guarantee a free, fair and orderly election. He disclosed, however, that armed police personnel had been placed on standby to respond to any eventuality that might threaten security during the exercise. The commander urged all candidates, their supporters and other party stakeholders to conduct themselves responsibly and avoid actions that could undermine the electoral process. The security arrangements come amid deepening divisions within the NDC in the Nalerigu-Gambaga Constituency, which have triggered legal disputes and public exchanges between rival party executives. The disagreements centre partly on the selection and legitimacy of five co-opted constituency executives and their eligibility to participate in the regional election. The dispute resulted in an application to the Nalerigu High Court, which restrained five individuals from participating in the election. The internal tensions have also exposed a broader political rivalry between Regional Minister Ibrahim Tia and former Nalerigu-Gambaga MP and former Minister for Climate Change, Alhaji Baba Issifu, over political influence in the constituency. The deployment of approximately 200 police officers, with armed personnel on standby, highlights security concerns surrounding the closely watched election involving 231 delegates.

items.title: NAFDAC uncovers unregistered cosmetics, falsified medicines, banned soaps at Trade Fair Complex
items.description: By Chioma Obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control, NAFDAC, has uncovered a suspected illegal cosmetics production and packaging operation at the Tools and Hardware section of Trade Fair Complex, Lagos. The raid exposes a network of unregistered products and materials allegedly intended for illicit manufacturing. Read Also: NAFDAC uncovers another fake herbal factory in Lagos, arrests manager The discovery followed an enforcement operation at the sprawling market along the Lagos-Badagry Expressway. Officials found unlabelled cosmetics, empty product containers, packaging materials and already-produced creams across different floors of a two-storey building. In a video of the operation shared on the Agency’s official X account on Saturday, Mr. Olakunle Ojo, NAFDAC enforcement team lead, and other officials were seen inspecting the building and displaying the recovered materials, raising concerns over the production and circulation of cosmetics of unknown origin and regulatory status. “This is exactly what we are able to find at this particular location,” Mr. Ojo said while displaying various packaging materials and empty containers. The inspection revealed packaging materials bearing names such as turmeric vitamin C and other cosmetic product descriptions, alongside empty shampoo tubes, lotion containers and materials suspected to be intended for the packaging of unregistered products. On the upper floors, officials discovered additional packaging materials, including containers for different cosmetic products, as well as already-produced glutawide cream. The agency also displayed materials bearing different product names, but could not immediately establish the identity and regulatory status of some of the substances and products found at the premises. NAFDAC described the operation as part of its ongoing enforcement activities at the Trade Fair Complex, where it has uncovered several suspected illegal manufacturing, storage and distribution activities. ‘Drugs’ In a related discovery at the complex, the agency uncovered a warehouse on the last floor of a building containing packaging materials for suspected falsified medicines, including Augmentin 625mg and Amplicloxa. Bottle caps bearing the Gordon’s Gin brand were also reportedly found among the materials. The latest discoveries add to a series of enforcement operations by NAFDAC at the Trade Fair market. In previous raids, the agency recovered 728 cartons of Crusader soap, 718 cartons of E45 soap and quantities of Extract Gold whitening soap, products it said were banned by the Federal Government. The repeated discoveries have raised concerns about the scale of illegal product manufacturing and repackaging activities operating within the market, as well as the potential risks to unsuspecting consumers. items.title: We can’t rely on NAIMOS alone to fight galamsey – Senyo Hosi
items.description: Convener of the OneGhana Movement and finance and economic policy analyst, Senyo Hosi, has called for a major rethink of Ghana’s approach to tackling illegal mining, warning that the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) cannot win the fight on its own. He says the country must adopt a broader strategy that addresses the economic and social conditions sustaining illegal mining, particularly in communities where it has become a major source of livelihood. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 14, Mr Hosi criticised what he described as an overreliance on NAIMOS, arguing that local authorities must take greater responsibility for enforcing mining laws and protecting their communities. He specifically challenged Metropolitan, Municipal and District Chief Executives (MMDCEs) to strengthen enforcement at the local level rather than leave the responsibility largely to the national task force. “We cannot rely on NAIMOS alone to win a war which has taken seed at the local level. MMDCEs, who control security at the local level, continue to fail to enforce the laws,” he said. He also questioned the effectiveness of NAIMOS operations that involve moving from one community to another without ensuring that illegal mining activities are permanently halted. “NAIMOS should just stop roaming people’s villages,” he stated. Citing operations at Osino, he questioned the sustainability of interventions if illegal miners returned immediately after security personnel withdrew. “You went to Osino. You left the place. The people went back in. What did you achieve?” he asked. Mr Hosi also raised concerns about allegations of extortion associated with anti-illegal mining operations, recalling similar accusations against previous interventions, including Operation Vanguard. Economic realities must inform galamsey fight Mr Hosi argued that the government’s approach must recognise the scale of the economic interests and livelihoods tied to illegal mining. He said it would be unrealistic to expect security operations alone to eliminate an activity involving an estimated one million to three million people without providing alternative sources of income. “You are dealing with a trade that has about a million to three million people involved, a whole community. You can’t just shut them down when that is actually their livelihood,” he said. He noted that illegal mining had become intertwined with the economic survival and social realities of some communities, making enforcement without alternative livelihood opportunities difficult to sustain. “The communities have this intertwined with their culture, their economic survival. You can’t shoot poverty away. That is the reality of this,” he stated. He further argued that the continued participation of residents, despite the deaths and dangers associated with illegal mining, demonstrated the depth of the socioeconomic challenges confronting affected communities. For Mr Hosi, the government must recognise that the fight requires more than arrests, excavator seizures and military deployments. “We can’t keep wanting to do things the same way. There’s a need for a total rethinking of this,” he said. Questions need for state of emergency Responding to whether Ghana still needed a state of emergency to address illegal mining, Mr Hosi said such a measure could be implemented in severely affected areas if the government was prepared to accept the political consequences. He maintained that the problem was not necessarily the absence of the legal and security measures required to tackle galamsey, but a lack of political willingness to apply them decisively. “It’s not as though there’s no need. Let me be very clear. While I often say the fight can’t be won in the context of the political inertia that we have, if you want to win this, you will win it,” he said. However, he cautioned against relying exclusively on military intervention, citing the disparity between Ghana’s estimated military strength of 28,000 to 30,000 personnel and the millions of people he believes are involved in the illegal mining economy. He also questioned the political and practical sustainability of shutting down livelihoods without addressing the conditions that drive people into the activity. Cleaner water bodies, forest reserves should define success Mr Hosi said Ghana must clearly define what success in the fight against illegal mining should look like, arguing that protecting water bodies and forest reserves must be the immediate priorities. He said the country should focus its resources on achievable objectives rather than pursue an overly broad campaign without clearly identifying measurable outcomes. “We just have to be clear and select our victories, our winnable tasks. We have to define what victory looks like at first,” he said. According to him, the most important measure of progress should be cleaner rivers and the protection of forest reserves, rather than the number of enforcement operations conducted. “What does victory look like for us in Ghana? Galamsey. It must mean cleaner waters. That is what victory should look like for us, number one. Number two, our forest reserves,” he stated. He suggested that NAIMOS should prioritise stopping mining activities in rivers and their immediate surroundings, arguing that sustained enforcement in these areas would produce more visible environmental benefits. “If NAIMOS and their work were just committed to our rivers, and nobody was mining on our rivers, at least for now, we wouldn’t have this water we are seeing in front of us,” he said. He also questioned the effectiveness of government expenditure on the anti-galamsey campaign, insisting that the results must be assessed against improvements in water quality and the restoration of degraded forest reserves. Referring to the government’s 2027 budgetary allocations and statements by the Finance Minister, Mr Hosi said the public deserved measurable evidence that the resources committed to the fight were producing results. “You should be telling us whether our water bodies have improved with all the investments you have made in that particular sector,” he said. “It hasn’t. It has gotten worse,” he added. He maintained that unless Ghana addresses the economic incentives sustaining illegal mining while protecting its critical environmental resources, the country risks repeating enforcement exercises without achieving lasting results.

items.title: Yvelines : un vice-président d’université blessé à l’arme blanche, l’agresseur en fuite
items.description: L'attaque s'est produite vers 19h45, au siege de la presidence de l'universite de Versailles-Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines (UVSQ). Selon Le Parisien , l'assaillant dissimulait son visage. Il a frappe l'un des vice-presidents avec une arme blanche, le blessant a l'arriere de la tete et a la main, puis a quitte les lieux. Le vice-president a ete emmene a l'hopital apres l'intervention des secours. Samedi 14 novembre, Loïc Josseran, president de l'UVSQ, a confirme que son pronostic vital n'etait pas engage. C'est sur X que Philippe Baptiste, ministre de l'Enseignement superieur et de la Recherche, a rendu l'attaque publique, le soir du 13 novembre. Le ministre y a exprime sa solidarite avec le vice-president blesse, ses proches et ses collegues : « Je condamne avec la plus grande fermete cet acte d'une extreme gravite. » Il y a egalement affirme : « Aucune violence n'est acceptable. L'etat se tient aux cotes des universites, de leur gouvernance et de leurs equipes ». Le ministre a dit compter sur la justice pour etablir les faits et identifier l'agresseur. Son message ne donne cependant aucun indice concernant le mobile. Ce soir, un vice-président d'une grande université d'Île-de-France a été violemment agressé à l'arme blanche, dans son propre bureau. Il est blessé. Je lui ai dit mon soutien, ainsi qu'à ses proches et à l'ensemble de ses collègues. Je condamne avec la plus grande fermeté cet acte d'une extrême gravité. Je fais pleinement confiance à la justice pour faire toute la lumière sur cette agression et pour que son auteur réponde de ses actes. Aucune violence n'est acceptable. L'État se tient aux côtés des universités, de leur gouvernance et de leurs équipes. — Philippe Baptiste (@PhBaptiste) November 13, 2026 Loïc Josseran a de son cote remercie les secours et les forces de l'ordre pour leur intervention rapide. Dans son communique, il a adresse ses pensees au collegue blesse et a sa famille. Une enquete est ouverte pour reconstituer precisement le deroulement de l'attaque. Un climat universitaire deja tendu L'affaire survient dans une periode agitee pour plusieurs etablissements francais. Depuis des semaines, des mobilisations etudiantes s'accompagnent par endroits de blocages et d'occupations. Mais rien, dans les informations rendues publiques sur l'agression de vendredi, ne permet de la relier a ces mouvements. Le 10 novembre, avant meme l'attaque, France Universites avait denonce les insultes et les menaces visant des dirigeants universitaires, parfois jusqu'aux menaces de mort. L'association signalait egalement des degradations de locaux. Dans son communique du 14 novembre, Loïc Josseran denonce la situation : « Je condamne avec la plus grande fermete cet acte de violence, intervenu dans un contexte universitaire tendu, dont les motivations ne sont pas encore connues et que rien ne saurait justifier. »

items.title: CAN 2025 : Benatia fracasse la gestion de la finale Maroc-Sénégal
items.description: L’ancien capitaine des Lions de l’Atlas, Mehdi Benatia, est revenu sans détour sur la finale de la CAN 2025 entre le Maroc et le Sénégal, un match dont l’issue continue de faire l’objet d’une bataille juridique. Pour l’ancien international marocain, même si les textes peuvent justifier la décision prise, le scénario laisse surtout un goût amer. Interrogé par Bertrand Latour dans le cadre d’un entretien diffusé sur la chaîne YouTube de Canal+, Benatia a estimé que cette finale, remportée initialement par le Sénégal sur le terrain, aurait dû connaître une autre issue. Le Sénégal s’était imposé 1-0 après prolongation grâce à un but de Pape Gueye, après notamment un penalty manqué par Brahim Diaz. La rencontre avait toutefois été marquée par un épisode particulièrement polémique : les joueurs sénégalais avaient temporairement quitté la pelouse pour protester contre certaines décisions arbitrales, avant de reprendre la rencontre. Pour Benatia, c’est précisément cet épisode qui a profondément terni l’image de cette finale. « C’est triste pour le foot marocain qu’on en arrive à se demander : qui a gagné, qui n’a pas gagné ? » , a-t-il déploré, regrettant que les polémiques aient pris le dessus sur une compétition qu’il jugeait jusque-là très réussie. L’ancien défenseur du Bayern Munich, de la Juventus et de l’AS Roma estime toutefois que le règlement pouvait permettre de sanctionner le comportement des Sénégalais. « Si tu reprends les textes de loi, ils disent quand même que si tu sors du terrain et que tu n’as plus tant de joueurs sur le terrain, c’est abandon » , a-t-il déclaré. Mais Benatia pointe surtout du doigt la gestion de l’incident par les officiels : « La faute, c’est celle de l’arbitre, des délégués, qui n’ont pas pris cette décision. » Une position qui rejoint sa frustration face à la tournure prise par le dossier. Pour lui, le fait que le Sénégal ait finalement repris la rencontre et l’ait terminée complique encore la perception de la décision. Le consultant de Canal+ considère que, quelle que soit l’issue définitive du dossier, cette finale restera marquée par la controverse. « Quand tu décides de revenir, que tu joues le match, que tu le finis et que tu as accepté ce qu’il s’est passé… je ne sais pas qui va décider, mais c’est un beau boulot de merde » , a-t-il lâché, très critique envers la gestion de cette finale. Benatia estime surtout que le Maroc ne pourra pas célébrer ce titre de la même manière s’il est définitivement confirmé sur tapis vert : « Elle n’aura jamais la même saveur de toute façon. » La décision de la CAF avait finalement donné le match perdu au Sénégal sur tapis vert et attribué officiellement le trophée au Maroc. La Fédération sénégalaise a toutefois saisi le Tribunal arbitral du sport (TAS), dont la décision est attendue avant la fin du mois de novembre selon les éléments rapportés dans l’entretien. Pour Benatia, cette bataille juridique ne pourra donc pas effacer complètement le souvenir d’une finale qui, selon lui, aurait dû rester avant tout une fête du football africain. The post CAN 2025 : Benatia fracasse la gestion de la finale Maroc-Sénégal appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : la Chine, patronne des Jeux
items.description: Les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse « Dakar 2026 » ont pris fin ce vendredi 13 novembre, et le tableau des médailles est sans appel : la Chine est la première puissance des Jeux. Avec 33 médailles, dont 18 en or, 8 en argent et 7 en bronze, la délégation chinoise devance le Japon (28 médailles, dont 11 en or) et la Russie (14 médailles, dont 8 en or). La domination de la Chine aux Joj « Dakar 2026 » s’est construite jour après jour. Après trois jours de compétition, la Chine et le Japon comptaient chacun quatre titres, mais la Chine tenait déjà la tête grâce à ses médailles d’argent. Le lundi 9 novembre, elle en était à 23 médailles, dont 13 en or. Le mercredi 11, elle franchissait la barre des 30, avec 16 titres. Trois médailles de plus, dont deux en or, ont porté son total final à 33. La gymnastique artistique a été son point fort. Elle a remporté l’or par équipes mixtes devant le Japon et Israël. Chez les garçons, elle s’est imposée devant le Japon et la Grande-Bretagne. Chez les filles, elle a battu le Japon de justesse. Une suprématie presque totale dans une discipline qui récompense la régularité, la précision et la préparation. A lire aussi : classement provisoire : la Chine domine le tableau des médailles En athlétisme, la Chine est la deuxième nation du tableau, derrière l’Éthiopie, avec 9 médailles (3 en or, 4 en argent, 2 en bronze). Wang Yaru a ouvert la série en remportant le 5000 m marche féminin. Sheng Xuefeng a gagné le triple saut masculin avec 16,18 m, et Zhang Keyi le 100 m haies féminin en 13 s 17. Chen Shijie (110 m haies, 13 s 40) et Liu Sen (saut en hauteur, 2,14 m) ont pris l’argent. Les sports collectifs ont aussi souri aux Chinoises. En basket 3×3 féminin, elles ont éliminé le Sénégal, pays hôte, en demi-finale, avant de s’incliner en finale face à la Pologne (12-11) et de décrocher l’argent. Ce bilan raconte une méthode : une délégation nombreuse, présente sur tous les fronts, régulière du premier au dernier jour, aussi à l’aise dans les disciplines de précision que dans les épreuves de vitesse et d’endurance. À Dakar, la Chine n’a pas seulement gagné des médailles. Elle a imposé sa constance et sa profondeur de banc, et transformé chaque finale en podium. Elle est la patronne incontestée de ces Joj. Derrière le trio de tête, l’Égypte est quatrième avec 12 médailles, dont 6 en or, et reste la première nation africaine. L’Éthiopie est cinquième. Le Sénégal, pays hôte, termine sixième avec 12 médailles, dont 5 en or et 7 en bronze, devant la France, septième avec 13 médailles. Par Samba Oumar FALL

items.title: Tunisie, ton football est moribond !
items.description: Après des participations calamiteuses aux dernières Coupes Arabe, d’Afrique et du Monde et un début poussif aux éliminatoires de la prochaine Coupe d’Afrique des Nations, avec deux matchs nuls à domicile contre des équipes très moyennes, on attendait un rachat de la part de l’équipe de Tunisie de football face au troisième adversaire du groupe, la Libye en l’occurrence, hier soir, vendredi 13 novembre 2026, à Sfax. On eut droit à une nouvelle défaite 0-2. Douche froide, déception, humiliation et rage aux tripes. Latif Belhedi Résultat des courses, après trois matches à domicile, au cours desquelles ils ont volé très bas, les Aigles de Carthage sont très logiquement retombés à la dernière place du groupe 8 des éliminatoires de la Coupe d'Afrique 2027 et ce ne sont pas leurs récriminations contre l’arbitre marocain du match qui vont les racheter aux yeux de leurs supporters qui, de déception en désillusion, se font de plus en plus rares. La sélection nationale occupe ainsi la lanterne rouge de son groupe, avec seulement 2 points au compteur après 3 journées, score historiquement le plus bas qu’elle ait jamais réalisé même lors de ses précédentes traversées du désert. N’étant pas parvenue à s’imposer à domicile face à l’Ouganda, au Botswana et à la Libye, l’équipe nationale tunisienne serait-elle en mesure de battre ces mêmes adversaires en déplacement devant leurs publics respectifs pour espérer gagner son billet pour la CAN 2027, compétition dont elle possède pourtant le record de participations ? Qu’on nous permette d’en douter sérieusement, car les protégés du pauvre Mouine Chaabani, quatrième coach appelé au chevet d’une équipe moribonde en moins d’une année (après Sami Trabelsi, Sabri Lamouchi et Hervé Renard) n’ont ni les moyens techniques et physiques, ni les ressources morales, ni la discipline tactique susceptibles de les porter vers la victoire. Football | L’équipe de Tunisie s’enlise dans la crise Une génération de joueurs très moyens Incapables de créer plus d’une ou deux occasions de buts par match, qu’ils ratent d’ailleurs souvent de manière lamentable, et devenant fébriles et brouillons à la moindre accélération de leurs adversaires, au point d’encaisser désormais plus de buts qu’ils n’en marquent (en trois matchs lors des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027, ils ont marqué 3 buts et en ont encaissé 5), on ne les voit vraiment pas capables de prouesses au-dessus de leurs forces. Et ce n’est pas manquer de patriotisme que d’admettre l’évidence : l’équipe de Tunisie n’a pas les munitions nécessaires pour espérer battre ses adversaires, ni des reins suffisamment solides pour résister à des équipes africaines qui la surclassent désormais sur pratiquement tous les plans. Hier soir, les Rouge et Blancs erraient sur la pelouse du stade de Sfax comme des âmes mortes : jambes lourdes, gestes lents, mouvements téléphonés, passes latérales, peu d'engagement, zéro créativité… Un football de pousse-ballon, ennuyeux à en mourir… La peur au ventre et du plomb dans les jambes, ils se renvoyaient la balle comme une patate chaude. Comme s'ils s'acquittaient d'une corvée ! Alors cessons de nous bercer d’illusions et d’espérer encore d’une génération de joueurs très moyens et qui se sont avérés être les plus médiocres (ou les moins performants pour dire les choses moins crûment) que le football tunisien ait eu dans son histoire ! Il fallait voir les deux autres matchs de la compétition joués hier soir où l'Egypte a écrasé le Malawi 4-0 et le Maroc a battu le Niger 4-1 pour prendre conscience de l'écart qui nous sépare désormais de nos voisins. N’ayant rien à espérer du présent, nous serions mieux inspirés de commencer dès maintenant à préparer l’avenir. Et d’abord, commençons par mettre à la retraite anticipée ces bons à rien de la Fédération tunisienne de football (FTF) qui n’ont pas fini de détruire le sport roi dans notre pays ! items.title: HSBC : après 18 ans de présence, la banque britannique quitte l’Algérie
items.description: Un grand établissement financier international quitte l’Algérie. Il s'agit de la banque britannique HSBC , qui vient d'annoncer sa décision de cesser ses activités sur le marché algérien. La décision survient suite à « un examen stratégique approfondi » de la branche de banque de gros de HSBC en Algérie et s'inscrit dans le cadre de « la simplification continue du groupe », qui vise à « renforcer son leadership dans les domaines où il dispose d'un avantage concurrentiel clair et des meilleures opportunités de croissance et de soutien à ses clients », indique HSBC Bank Middle East Limited. HSBC va cesser ses activités sur le marché algérien Depuis 18 ans, HSBC Algérie propose, « grâce à son réseau local et international », de multiples services aux clients de la banque de gros, notamment les organismes publics et les entreprises multinationales. « Nos solutions primées de paiement et de commerce international garantissent des transactions fluides, sécurisées et rapides pour les entreprises internationales, et notre large gamme de produits leur donne accès aux marchés mondiaux », explique la banque. HSBC : le dialogue a débuté avec ses clients algériens en vue de son retrait Le retrait du marché algérien se fera progressivement afin de ne pas léser les clients et partenaires locaux. Elle s’engage à « soutenir » ses clients et ses collaborateurs et à « respecter toutes ses obligations envers les organismes de réglementation, les tiers et le marché dans son ensemble jusqu'à la fin du processus de liquidation ». Le dialogue avec les clients a débuté, annonce HSBC, ajoutant que d'autres mises à jour seront fournies au cours des prochains mois afin de « les accompagner dans leur transition vers des prestataires bancaires alternatifs adaptés en Algérie ». HSBC est l’un des plus grands établissements bancaires au monde HSBC Holdings plc, la société mère de HSBC, a son siège social à Londres et compte parmi les plus grands établissements bancaires au monde avec un actif de 3.445 milliards de dollars et une présence dans 56 pays et territoires. HSBC est aussi le plus grand groupe bancaire international de la région MENA et Turquie. Outre l’Algérie où elle est présente depuis 18 ans, la banque opère aussi au Bahreïn, en Égypte, au Koweït, à Oman, au Qatar, en Arabie Saoudite, en Turquie et aux Émirats arabes unis. L’article HSBC : après 18 ans de présence, la banque britannique quitte l’Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Miracles Aboagye insists State must account for 6 deaths at Manso Keniago over galamsey
items.description: The Director of Communications for the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Miracles Aboagye, has called for a thorough investigation into the killing of six people during a confrontation involving personnel of the National Anti-Illegal Mining Operations Secretariat (NAIMOS) and residents of Manso Keniago in the Ashanti Region. He has cautioned against collectively labelling the deceased as illegal miners or members of a mob, insisting that the circumstances surrounding each death must be independently established to ensure justice for the victims and their families. Speaking on JoyNews’ Newsfile on Saturday, November 14, during a discussion on the incident, Mr Aboagye said available accounts suggested that some of the victims might not have participated in the confrontation. He expressed condolences to the bereaved families, citing reports of a woman who was allegedly shot in her bathroom and others who were shot on the street. “I express my condolences to the lost ones. The sad and painful reality is that some of the six fallen citizens may not even be part of anything,” he said. “I have seen a woman who was shot in her bathroom. The cameras were there. They showed where she was in the bathroom and the blood stains. But I’ve seen two people shot on the street,” he added. Mr Aboagye said he had listened to accounts from both the community’s chief and NAIMOS officials but maintained that the conflicting narratives made an independent investigation necessary. “Whatever the case is, we have lost six citizens that, as we speak now, we are yet to understand clearly why each of them died,” he said. He argued that each victim deserved an individual assessment rather than being grouped and presumed to have been involved in the confrontation. “Remember, you can’t bunch human souls together and label all of them with one issue and use that as a basis for their death. Every family deserves justice. We need to understand why each of the six people has died,” he stated. State must take responsibility for citizens’ safety While urging civilians to avoid confronting armed security personnel, Mr Aboagye said the State had the primary responsibility to protect lives, particularly during enforcement operations. He argued that residents should exercise restraint when confronted by armed officers, as there was little to gain from engaging security personnel in a potentially dangerous confrontation. “My view is that there is no glory in confronting armed men, especially those who are backed by the law,” he said. However, he stressed that this did not absolve security personnel or the State of their responsibility to protect innocent people during operations. “The number one responsibility of the State is the security, safety and protection of its citizens. That comes before every other thing,” he said. “When it comes to our safety and security, it’s solely in the hands of the State. And so the State must take responsibility,” he added. Mr Aboagye further argued that the presence of a crowd at the scene did not necessarily mean everyone within it was participating in an attack on security personnel. He said officers must exercise restraint and distinguish between those actively confronting them and innocent residents who might have gathered out of curiosity. “You must be mindful. And even if there’s one single soul, just one person in that mob that is innocent, you have a duty and responsibility to be moderate to protect that person,” he said. He maintained that the possibility of innocent people being caught up in the confrontation made it unacceptable to justify all six deaths simply on the grounds that a mob had confronted the task force. “There is no justification in getting a single innocent person to die in a mob in an attempt or with the justification that it’s a mob and your life is under threat. You are trained, they are not,” he stated. Questions NAIMOS use of drone surveillance The NPP Communications Director said he would accept the outcome of an investigation establishing that all six deceased persons were illegal miners who actively obstructed the NAIMOS operation. However, he insisted that such a conclusion must be supported by credible evidence rather than assumptions about the victims’ involvement. “If all six people are identified to be galamseyers who are standing in the way of NAIMOS, we can do this. But we don’t know that yet,” he said. He also questioned why drone footage was not being used to establish the sequence of events and identify the individuals who participated in the confrontation. “If you have a drone and you encounter such a mob, you don’t leave the drone. You let the drone fly,” he said. Mr Aboagye also alleged that influential individuals benefiting from illegal mining continued to enjoy political protection, declaring that “the kingpins of galamsey are backing government”. How the Manso Keniago confrontation unfolded The incident occurred on Wednesday, November 11, at Manso Keniago in the Amansie South District of the Ashanti Region, when NAIMOS personnel were transporting excavators seized during an anti-illegal mining operation to a designated location for safekeeping. Read also: Manso Keniago clash death toll rises to six, 15 injured The confrontation reportedly followed disagreements between the task force, some residents and traditional authorities over the transportation of the seized equipment through the community on a tarred road. Residents reportedly preferred that low-bed trailers be used. NAIMOS maintained that its personnel encountered an armed group attempting to obstruct the operation and said officers fired warning shots to disperse the crowd. The Secretariat subsequently described the shooting as an act of self-defence. The death toll, initially reported as three, later rose to six, while 15 others were reported injured. Two NAIMOS personnel also sustained gunshot wounds but were subsequently treated and discharged from hospital. Mr Aboagye’s comments add to growing calls for an investigation into the circumstances of the deaths, with questions remaining about the conduct of the operation, the use of firearms and the individual roles, if any, played by those who lost their lives.

items.title: Kamsar : L’ANAIM mobilise contre le diabète à une marche de sensibilisation et un dépistage gratuit
items.description: À l’occasion de la Journée mondiale du diabète, célébrée ce samedi 14 novembre 2026, la coordination de l’Agence nationale d’aménagement des infrastructures minières (ANAIM), en collaboration avec l’Hôpital ANAIM de Kamsar, a organisé une marche de sensibilisation suivie d’une campagne de dépistage gratuit du diabète. Placée sous le slogan « Prévenir, se faire dépister pour mieux vivre avec le diabète », cette initiative a mobilisé de nombreux participants autour d’un parcours allant de l’Hôpital ANAIM jusqu’à la Villa 3 Avril de Kamsar. L’objectif de cette activité était de sensibiliser les populations aux risques liés au diabète, tout en mettant l’accent sur l’importance de la prévention, du dépistage précoce et de l’adoption de bonnes habitudes de vie pour mieux lutter contre cette maladie. La mobilisation a connu la participation des autorités préfectorales et communales de Kamsar, des travailleurs de l’ANAIM ainsi que de nombreux citoyens venus de différentes localités de la préfecture. Au-delà de la marche, la campagne de dépistage gratuit a constitué une occasion importante pour les populations de connaître leur état de santé et de bénéficier de conseils sur la prévention et la prise en charge du diabète. À travers cette initiative, la coordination de l’ANAIM et l’Hôpital ANAIM réaffirment leur engagement en faveur de la promotion de la santé publique et de la prévention des maladies non transmissibles au sein des communautés. Cette mobilisation rappelle une réalité essentielle : le dépistage précoce, associé à une bonne hygiène de vie, demeure un moyen important de prévenir les complications et de mieux vivre avec le diabète.

Nollywood sequel “Issakaba: The Return” hits cinemas after 25 years
items.description: Nollywood action thriller ‘Issakaba: The Return’ has returned to cinemas nationwide after 25 years of the release of the original movie, ‘Issakaba’. The director, Lancelot Imasuen, announced the cinema release in a post on his Instagram page on Friday, expressing excitement over the return of the popular movie franchise to the big screen. In the post, Imasuen described the production as the return of a legend and urged movie lovers to watch the film in cinemas. The sequel features veteran actor Sam Dede reprising his role as Ebube, leader of the Issakaba Boys, while introducing other actors from different generations of Nollywood. Other cast members include Chidi Mokeme, Iyabo Ojo, Regina Daniels, Chiwetalu Agu, Alex Osifo, Charles Okafor, Nosa Rex and Mark Angel. Directed by Imasuen, who also helmed the original production, ‘Issakaba: The Return’ revisits the story of the fictional vigilante group against the backdrop of contemporary Nigerian society. The original film, released in 2001, drew inspiration from the activities of the Bakassi Boys, a vigilante group that emerged in south-eastern Nigeria to combat criminal activities. The sequel, distributed by Blue Pictures, brings together returning actors and newer Nollywood performers, marking the revival of one of the industry’s recognised action film franchises. items.title: Rock ‘n Roll Hall of Fame honours Fela Kuti
items.description: The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame will, today, honour Nigerian music legend Fela Kuti, as music stars and industry figures gather in Los Angeles to celebrate the latest inductees. The list of inductees include Sade, Oasis, British rocker Billy Idol, rhapsodic hip-hop transformers Wu-Tang Clan, versatile rock star Phil Collins, English heavy metal band Iron Maiden, post-punk and electronic dance music renegades Joy Division/New Order and the velvet-voiced late Luther Vandross in the performer class of 2026. Five artists will receive an “early influence” honor: Queen Latifah, Celia Cruz, MC Lyte, Fela Kuti and Gram Parsons. The Cleveland-based Hall of Fame – which surveyed more than 1,000 musicians, historians and industry members to choose the entrants – will honor the acts in a star-studded gala concert at Los Angeles’s Peacock Theater. But who will show up and who will perform remains iffy. Often inductees perform themselves – the evening can serve as a way to reunite the long estranged – or fellow musicians take the stage to showcase an act’s legacy. Several of the 2026 artists have already said they’ll skip. Sade – the group whose sensual, captivating rhythms have endured as fan favorites for decades with hits including “Smooth Operator” and “No Ordinary Love” – said they were bowing out in a statement on their website. “Sorry we can’t be there in person to celebrate with the other artists. Please know that our absence takes nothing away from how much this recognition means to us,” said the group, fronted by the singer Sade Adu. Britpop’s one-time feuding brothers Liam and Noel Gallagher of Oasis – who recently announced a 2027 world tour – also declined to make the trip. Noel Gallagher is scheduled to perform solo in London. Liam Gallagher had previously voiced disdain for the institution, and earlier this week said in an X reply to a fan: “It’s too far to be going for the night.” Iron Maiden said they will miss the ceremony as they’re on tour in Australia. ‘Tremendous honour’ The two British rock bands Joy Division and New Order will get a rare joint induction. New Order formed from the ashes of Joy Division after the original group’s lead singer, Ian Curtis, died in 1980. New Order went on to pioneer the future of alternative dance, with signature tracks including “Blue Monday,” “True Faith” and “Bizarre Love Triangle.” But it’s unclear which members will attend, or if New Order will perform. Collins – one of rock’s great drummers, whose signature hits include “In the Air Tonight” and “Sussudio” – has said health problems will keep him from taking the stage. Staten Island’s own Wu-Tang Clan – the ragtag group of New Yorkers who paired raw production with streetwise rhymes and martial arts influences to create cinematic hip-hop that changed the game – recently wrapped a tour they billed as their last. The Clan – known for songs like “C.R.E.A.M” and “Protect Ya Neck” – doesn’t always appear at events or even on tour as a full unit, but receiving an honor from the Rock Hall could be an apt moment for a reunion. Ahead of Idol’s induction, Los Angeles named Friday, November 13 as “Billy Idol Day,” making it seemingly likely the rocker who came up in London’s punk scene and put out radio hits including “Dancing With Myself” will attend Saturday’s ceremony. When his induction was announced, Idol called it “a tremendous honor.” Eligible nominees into the Rock Hall must have released their first commercial recording at least 25 years prior to being nominated. items.title: 2 soldiers martyred, 16 terrorists killed in North Waziristan operations: ISPR
items.description: Two soldiers were martyred and 16 terrorists were killed in North Waziristan district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the military’s media wing said on Saturday. According to a statement issued by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), in continuation of a series of IBOs being conducted by security forces, multiple khwarij locations were engaged in the general areas of Mir Ali, Datta Khel and surrounding areas in North Waziristan. “Following fierce fire exchanges, in last twelve hours, 12 khwarij , including two Afghan nationals belonging to Indian-sponsored Fitna al Khwarij were sent to hell in Ali Khel, while two khwarij each were neutralised in Mir Ali and Datta Khel, thereby causing a significant blow to the khwarijs ’ network operating in the area,” ISPR said. Fitna al Khawarij is a term used by the state for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). ISPR said that during the operations, 43-year-old Havildar Asmat Ali and 32-year-old Naik Aftab Ali embraced martyrdom. “Weapons and ammunition were also recovered from the killed Indian-sponsored khwarij , who remained actively involved in numerous terrorist activities, including the killing of innocent civilians,” it said. The statement said that sanitisation operations would continue to eliminate “remaining holed up khwarij from these areas”, adding that the counterterrorism campaign would continue at full pace to wipe out the menace of foreign-sponsored terrorism from the country. President Asif Ali Zardari paid tribute to the security forces for their successful operation and expressed condolences over the martyrdom of the two soldiers. He said operations under the ongoing Azm-i-Istehkam campaign against foreign-sponsored terrorism would continue with full force until the elimination of the last terrorist. The operations come a day after ISPR said 74 terrorists were killed in IBOs in KP and Balochistan. On Friday, it said 43 terrorists were killed during operations conducted over 48 hours in KP, including 35 in Mir Ali, North Waziristan district, and eight in Orakzai district. Another 31 terrorists were killed in Balochistan during an operation launched on Nov 3. Pakistan has seen a surge in terrorism, especially in KP and Balochistan since the banned TTP ended its ceasefire deal with the government in November 2022, vowing to increase attacks. According to Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies , the country’s security environment continued to show considerable volatility from Oct 30 to Nov 5, 2026, with renewed terrorist activity in parts of KP and the former tribal districts, alongside intensified counterterrorism operations and changing patterns of militant violence. Correction: An earlier version of this story said 14 terrorists were killed. The error is regretted.

items.title: NDC is the biggest enabler of galamsey – Miracles Aboagye claims
items.description: Director of Communications for the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dennis Miracles Aboagye, has accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of enabling illegal small-scale mining, popularly known as galamsey, alleging that some party officials and government functionaries are involved in the practice while authorities appear to be taking action against other miners. Mr Aboagye argued that the fight against illegal mining was being undermined by what he described as selective enforcement of the law, insisting that the actions of some individuals associated with the governing party were creating resentment among communities affected by the government’s anti-galamsey operations. Responding to the killing of some six persons following a clash between community members and the government’s anti-galamey task force, NAIMOS, he maintained that the political leadership of the NDC could not distance itself from the activities of individuals allegedly engaged in illegal mining, particularly when videos had emerged purportedly showing some party officials making statements in support of galamsey activities. “There is no pretence here. The kingpins of galamsey are back in government. I keep saying it, and I have said it several times. I have always proven it. The NDC is the biggest enabler of galamsey in this country,” he stated. He accused the government of failing to confront the problem consistently, arguing that while security personnel were deployed to clamp down on illegal mining activities in some communities, other operations allegedly continued in areas where individuals linked to the governing party were believed to be involved. According to him, illegal mining activities were still taking place along major routes and in communities stretching from Osino and Konongo in the Asante Akim area towards Kumasi. He questioned the apparent inconsistency in the government’s approach, claiming that people were being subjected to police operations and other enforcement measures while illegal mining continued in other locations. “As we speak this morning, Osino, Konongo, Asante Akyem, all the way to Kumasi, people are mining,” he alleged. He warned that selective enforcement could have serious consequences for public confidence in the country’s institutions. “In a society where the people don’t feel justice is prevailing, in a society where the people feel there is selective justice, they will revolt,” he cautioned. “These people, before they came to office, gave us a roadmap. It is still in their manifesto, and it is still on their campaign videos. They said, ‘Vote for me, and when we come, these are the things we will do.’ Which ones have they done?” he questioned. “Today in Ghana, galamsey is worse than it was in 2024. Everywhere you go,” he claimed.

items.title: Burkina Faso : des poursuites engagées contre 45 personnes physiques et morales pour des infractions liées au terrorisme
items.description: Le parquet du pole antiterroriste burkinabe a entame six procedures judiciaires contre 45 personnes physiques et morales pour des faits lies au terrorisme et a des atteintes a l'ordre public. La plupart des personnes visees par l'action judiciaire ne resident pas sur le territoire du pays, d'ou l'emission de mandats d'arret internationaux et de demandes d'extradition et d'entraide penale internationale qui ont ete transmis aux autorites de plusieurs pays, dont la Cote d'Ivoire, les etats-Unis d'Amerique et la France. Ces mesures ont ete indiquees, lors d'un point de presse tenu le 13 novembre par Pingdwende Desire Sawadogo, procureur general pres la Cour d'appel de Ouagadougou. Le magistrat a precise que les procedures concernent notamment des faits de complicite d'association de malfaiteurs terroristes, de detention illegale d'armes a des fins terroristes, d'apologie du terrorisme, de divulgation d'images et de videos a connotation terroriste et de financement du terrorisme. Des faits presumes de diffamation, d'atteinte au moral des Forces armees nationales et d'outrage a l'autorite publique ont egalement ete mentionnes par le procureur general. D'anciens hauts cadres gouvernementaux et des journalistes dans le collimateur de la justice Plusieurs anciennes personnalites gouvernementales figurent parmi les personnes visees par les procedures judiciaires au Burkina ; parmi elles figurent les anciens ministres des Affaires etrangeres Djibril Bassole et Mamadou Alpha Barry. Les faits qui leur sont reproches concernent la complicite d'association de malfaiteurs terroristes, la complicite de detention d'armes a feu et de munitions a des fins terroristes et la complicite de financement du terrorisme. Le frere cadet de l'ancien president Blaise Compaore, Francois Compaore, ainsi que sa belle-mere, Alizeta Ouedraogo, font l'objet de poursuites pour complicite d'association de malfaiteurs terroristes et financement du terrorisme. Les journalistes Issaka Lingani, Inoussa Ouedraogo, Abdoulaye Barry et Ouedraogo Adama dit « Damiss » sont egalement poursuivis. Du cote des personnes morales, la chaîne d'information France 24 est accusee de complicite d'association de malfaiteurs terroristes et de complicite d'apologie du terrorisme. Les autorites burkinabe sollicitent Meta pour identifier et poursuivre les animateurs des pages incriminees Pingdwende Desire Sawadogo a indique que les autorites judiciaires du Burkina avaient sollicite la collaboration de leurs homologues aux etats-Unis pour demander a la compagnie Meta, et a son reseau social Facebook, d'identifier et de poursuivre les animateurs des pages « Burkina Debat » et « France-Afrique Media », qui font l'objet de poursuites pour complicite d'association de malfaiteurs terroristes et d'apologie du terrorisme. a noter que, pour le cas de l'activiste ivoirien Camille Makosso, poursuivi pour apologie du terrorisme et complicite d'association de malfaiteurs terroristes, le procureur general a indique que les autorites burkinabe attendent « que des poursuites soient engagees par les pays ou ces personnes mises en cause resident ».

Crise énergétique : l'Allemagne envisage de relancer ses centrales à charbon face au risque de pénurie de gaz
items.description: Le ministere allemand de l'economie a elabore un projet de loi visant a remettre en service d'anciennes centrales a charbon, a rapporte le Tagesspiegel , citant une source. La decision, prise dans le cadre de sa strategie climatique, de fermer progressivement ces centrales a ete remise en question en raison du risque de penurie de gaz cet hiver. Selon le journal, le taux de remplissage des stockages de gaz allemands se situe actuellement a un niveau critique de 58 %. D'apres les estimations de l'association allemande des exploitants de stockages de gaz (INES), en cas d'hiver rigoureux, les reserves de gaz en Allemagne pourraient etre epuisees des le mois de janvier. Selon le projet du ministere allemand de l'economie, les centrales electriques faisant partie de la reserve du reseau, ou celles pour lesquelles une interdiction de combustion du charbon entrera en vigueur dans les prochaines annees, pourraient fournir des capacites supplementaires de production d'electricite au plus tard fin mars 2028. Selon le Tagesspiegel , les exploitants seraient tenus de maintenir en etat de preparation le personnel des centrales et les stocks de combustible. Toutefois, les coûts lies a leur entretien seraient repercutes sur les consommateurs finaux. Ce projet a ete critique par les partis parlementaires des Verts et des sociaux-democrates. Les premiers ont rappele que les reserves des centrales a charbon sont destinees aux situations d'urgence, et non a intervenir sur le marche lorsque les prix sont eleves. Les seconds ont quant a eux emis des doutes quant a la conformite du document prepare avec les normes de l'UE et les objectifs climatiques. Le paradoxe europeen : l'UE se detourne du gaz russe tout en augmentant ses importations La penurie de gaz en Europe est devenue critique suite a la decision prise en janvier dernier de mettre fin, debut 2027, aux importations de gaz naturel liquefie (GNL) russe dans le cadre de contrats a long terme, mesure qui sera suivie, a l'automne, de l'arret des importations de gaz par gazoduc. La situation est aggravee par les tensions au Moyen-Orient, ou le detroit d'Ormuz, voie maritime essentielle pour le transport du gaz naturel liquefie, est regulierement bloque. Dans le meme temps, la grave crise energetique en Europe continue de s'aggraver. Fin octobre, le prix de reference du gaz sur le marche neerlandais de transfert de propriete a brievement atteint 100 euros par megawattheure, pour la premiere fois depuis decembre 2022. En France, le tarif de reference du gaz en decembre est en hausse depuis plusieurs mois d'affilee . Par ailleurs, les livraisons de gaz russe vers l'Europe ne ralentissent pas du tout, bien au contraire. Euronews, se referant aux calculs d'Urgewald, a indique que les depenses de l'UE en GNL, de janvier a octobre, a la veille de l'interdiction totale de son importation dans le cadre de contrats a long terme, avaient atteint 8,7 milliards d'euros, soit 21 % de plus que pour l'ensemble de l'annee 2025. Dans le meme temps, le volume des livraisons a augmente de 6,3 % en glissement annuel, pour atteindre 12,9 millions de tonnes. Moscou a par ailleurs souligne le caractere inopportun de la decision de l'Union europeenne de renoncer au gaz russe. Le 29 octobre, le porte-parole du Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, a commente la position de Bruxelles en declarant : « Ils sont en train de scier la branche sur laquelle ils etaient assis. » Selon lui, l'economie europeenne est en stagnation. Elle conserve certes une puissance considerable, mais l'energie russe bon marche, en particulier le gaz achemine par gazoduc, a longtemps soutenu sa competitivite et sa prosperite. En se privant de cette energie, les pays de l'UE renoncent a un avantage qui profitait tant a leurs usines qu'a leurs consommateurs.

items.title: Sommet de la Francophonie : Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri représente le Roi à Phnom Penh
items.description: La Cheffe du gouvernement, Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri, est arrivée samedi à Phnom Penh pour représenter Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI au 20e Sommet de la Francophonie, prévu les 15 et 16 novembre dans la capitale cambodgienne. À son arrivée à l’aéroport international de Techo, Mme El Mansouri a été accueillie par Un Kheang, secrétaire d’État au ministère cambodgien des Affaires étrangères et de la Coopération internationale, ainsi que par Abderrahim Rahhaly, ambassadeur du Maroc en Thaïlande et au Cambodge. Placée sous le thème « Réinvestir dans la paix pour une prospérité partagée et une stabilité durable », cette 20e édition réunira les chefs d’État et de gouvernement des 90 États et gouvernements membres de l’Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF). Les travaux seront consacrés aux grandes orientations de l’Organisation ainsi qu’aux principaux enjeux de la coopération francophone, dans un contexte marqué par une recomposition du multilatéralisme. Un nouveau secrétaire général de la Francophonie à élire Le sommet sera également marqué par l’élection de la prochaine ou du prochain secrétaire général de la Francophonie, pour un mandat de quatre ans couvrant la période 2027-2030. Plus haute instance de la Francophonie, le sommet permettra également de dresser un bilan de l’action de l’OIF. À un an de l’échéance de la programmation 2024-2027, les dirigeants devront notamment examiner les résultats obtenus et réfléchir à la place de l’Organisation dans l’évolution du système multilatéral. À l’issue des travaux, les participants devraient adopter la Déclaration de Phnom Penh, ainsi que plusieurs résolutions. Ils devront également se prononcer sur la date et le lieu du 21e Sommet de la Francophonie, prévu en 2028. The post Sommet de la Francophonie : Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri représente le Roi à Phnom Penh appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .
